# @olan-app/sdk — Olan Apps SDK (llms.txt)

> One-file digest of node_modules/@olan-app/sdk/docs/*.md (generated; edit the docs instead).
> Olan Apps are React + TypeScript running in a sandbox; UI = the 23 SDK components, data = permission-checked olan.* calls.
> Done = `npx olan-app validate --strict` and `npx olan-app test` both pass.

<!-- docs/getting-started.md -->
# Getting started

An Olan App is a small React program that runs in a sandbox (a Web Worker on web/desktop, an
isolated JS engine on mobile). It does not draw anything itself: it describes its screen with the
components of `@olan-app/sdk`, and Olan draws them with its own native controls on every platform.
Data comes from `olan.*` calls that Olan answers after checking the app's permissions.

Formerly @olan/app-sdk; the old name still builds.

## Create an app

```sh
npx olan-app init "Geciken görevler" --template list-detail   # or: olan app init …
cd geciken-gorevler
npm install
npx olan-app validate --strict
npx olan-app test
npx olan-app dev        # serve it to Olan Studio (Geliştirme sunucuları)
```

Templates: `blank` (one screen), `list-detail` (projects → tasks → task), `project-widget` (a card on
the project page), `project-tab` (a project tab and project settings with `olan.project.config`), `project-records`
(the app's records on tasks: a task action, a record card, the app's status, calendar items, feed
lines, approvals and a project template; SDK 1.7), `external-api` (`olan.http.fetch` with an `http:<host>` permission), `data-list`
(`olan.db`), `backend` (`--backend`: UI + backend code that Olan runs, backend.md).

## Project layout

```
olan-app.json          manifest: id, name, version, surfaces, permissions, settings (manifest.md)
src/app.tsx            the app; must `export default defineApp({ ... })`
tests/*.test.ts        headless tests (node:test + @olan-app/cli/testing) (testing.md)
fixtures/*.json        mock data for tests, validate --strict and dev (testing.md#fixtures)
assets/icon.png        icon referenced by the manifest
dist/app.js            build output (generated, git-ignored)
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md   instructions for coding agents
```

## The smallest app

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Button, Screen, Stack, Text, defineApp, olan } from '@olan-app/sdk';

function Home() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  return (
    <Screen title="Sayaç">
      <Stack gap="md" padding="md">
        <Text text={`Düğmeye ${count} kez bastınız.`} />
        <Button label="Bas" variant="primary" onPress={() => setCount((value) => value + 1)} />
        <Button label="Bildirim" onPress={() => olan.ui.toast({ text: 'Merhaba!', tone: 'success' })} />
      </Stack>
    </Screen>
  );
}

export default defineApp({ app: Home });
```

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "id": "com.example.counter",
  "name": "Sayaç",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "sdk": "^1.8.0",
  "entry": "dist/app.js",
  "surfaces": { "app": { "title": "Sayaç" } },
  "permissions": []
}
```

## Rules (the sandbox enforces them; `validate --strict` reports them)

1. **Surfaces are named components.** `defineApp({ app: Home })`, never an inline arrow function
   (the React hook rules only apply to named components). Surface names: `app`,
   `project.widget`, `project.tab`, `project.settings`, `settings` (and the in-context surfaces of
   surfaces.md) — and each one used must be declared in `olan-app.json` `surfaces`.
2. **Only SDK components.** No DOM elements (`<div>`, `<span>`), no `react-dom`, no
   `react-native`, no Node built-ins (`fs`, `path`, …). There is no `style` or `className`: Olan
   owns colours, fonts and spacing. Use `tone`, `variant`, `gap` and `padding` props instead.
3. **Text lives in `<Text>`.** A string directly inside `Screen`, `Stack`, `Card` or `Form` is an
   error (`tree.text_outside_text`). Write `<Text text="…" />` or `<Text>…</Text>`.
4. **No browser globals for I/O.** `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `WebSocket`, `localStorage`,
   `indexedDB`, `window`, `document` do not exist. Use `olan.http.fetch`, `olan.storage`,
   `olan.settings`.
5. **Every `olan.*` call needs its permission** in `olan-app.json` `permissions` (permissions.md).
   Without it the call rejects with `OlanError` code `permission_denied` (`http_blocked` for HTTP).
6. **Keys are unique.** Every `List` item, `Table` row, `Menu` item and `Action` has a unique `key`
   (string or number); events give it back as `{ key }`.
7. **Every `Button` has a `label`.** Every `Menu` has a `label` (or at least an `icon`).
8. **Use React normally:** `useState`, `useEffect`, `useMemo`, custom hooks, context. Load data with
   `useQuery(() => olan.….(), [deps])` (hooks.md).

## Done means

```sh
npx olan-app validate --strict   # manifest, build, TypeScript, every surface rendered, no missing permission
npx olan-app test                # all tests pass
```

Both exit with code 0. Add `--json` for machine-readable output (cli.md).

## Running it in Olan

During development the app runs unsigned, but only in development mode: Studio, `olan-app dev`
and "Olan'da dene" (`/apps/dev`), for people an administrator gave the `developer` grant, under
a "Geliştirme" label. **Studio** is in the Olan web app: sign in at your Olan web address (e.g. `https://olan.example.com`) with an account that has the `developer` grant (Yönetim → Kullanıcılar) and open `<Olan web address>/tr/studio`; `/tr/studio?section=publish` opens Yayınla (marketplace publishing).

Installing it (for yourself or the organization) needs a signed package. An Olan server installs a
package only when its signature verifies and the signing key is on the server's trusted key list.
Every Olan server ships with the Olan Marketplace key built in (`olan-marketplace-2026-10-17`), and
in production that is the only trusted key, so apps reach real organizations through Olan
Marketplace review. An unsigned package can be uploaded, but it is listed as "İmzasız" and
cannot be installed. For your own local Olan:

```sh
npx olan-app keygen --dev        # once; prints OLAN_APPS_TRUSTED_KEYS=dev-local=<key> for the local API
npx olan-app validate --strict   # first: pack runs only the non-strict checks (and refuses on errors)
npx olan-app pack --dev-sign     # dist/<id>-<version>.olanapp, signed with your development key
```

Then upload it in Olan → Yönetim → Uygulamalar → Katalog (or `olan-app publish --org --dev-sign`)
and install it there (cli.md#signing-and-publishing). Uploading and, by default, installing are for organization admins: an organization without an install policy is "admin only" until an admin lets members install apps.

For real organizations, submit it to Olan Marketplace (automatic checks, review, signing;
marketplace.md):

```sh
npx olan-app login --marketplace --server https://api.example.com   # once: signs you in in the browser
npx olan-app developer create --marketplace --slug acme --name "Acme Ltd" --accept-agreement   # once
npx olan-app publish --marketplace --age-rating 4+   # age rating (4+, 9+, 13+): required before release
npx olan-app release --marketplace <appId> <version>  # after approval (`olan-app status` prints the exact command)
```

With an Olan CLI that has the `app` command and is signed in, `olan app login --marketplace` works too. CI does not sign in: it uses the saved session as `OLAN_MARKETPLACE_SESSION` (marketplace.md#signing-in).

<!-- docs/components.md -->
# Components

Import every component from `@olan-app/sdk`. These 23 are the only ones that exist (SDK 1.5 added
`Tabs`, `Switch`, `MultiSelect`, `Stat`, `Banner`, `Image`, `Avatar` and `ProgressBar`; apps using
them declare `"sdk": "^1.5.0"`); Olan draws each
with its own native control (web, desktop, iOS, Android). All props are optional unless marked
**required**. Props not listed here are rejected (`tree.unknown_prop`), including `style`,
`className`, `color` and `id`.

Handler props (`onPress`, `onSelect`, `onChange`, `onSubmit`, …) may be async; a rejected promise is
reported as an app error. Event payloads are listed with each handler.

Shared value sets:

| Type | Values |
|---|---|
| `Tone` | `'default' \| 'muted' \| 'accent' \| 'danger' \| 'success' \| 'warning'` |
| `Spacing` | `'none' \| 'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` |
| `Key` | `string \| number` (non-empty string) |
| `IconName` | a name from the icon list at the end of this page |
| `Action` | `{ key: Key; label: string; icon?: IconName; onPress: () => void }` |

Children: `Screen`, `Stack`, `Card` and `Form` take any components; `Text` takes only text; every
other component takes no children (`tree.children_not_allowed`).

## Screen

Title bar plus body. **Required root** of the `app` and `settings` surfaces (`validate --strict`
warns `ui.root_not_screen`); also the recommended root of modal and panel surfaces (`chat.*`,
`mail.*`, `calendar.event.action`, `meeting.panel`, SDK 1.7 `task.action`, `issue.action`, `record.card`), where its title and actions are the header.
`project.widget` uses `Card` (or `EmptyState`) instead. `project.tab` and `project.settings` (SDK 1.6)
also start with `Screen`: its title heads the tab or the settings sheet.

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | `string` | Title bar text |
| `subtitle` | `string` | |
| `actions` | `Action[]` | Buttons in the title bar |
| `loading` | `boolean` | Shows a loading indicator |
| `scroll` | `boolean` | Body scrolls (default: host decides) |
| children | any | |

```tsx
<Screen title="Projeler" loading={q.loading} actions={[{ key: 'refresh', label: 'Yenile', icon: 'refresh', onPress: () => q.refetch() }]}>
  …
</Screen>
```

## Stack

Lays children out in a column (default) or a row.

| Prop | Type |
|---|---|
| `direction` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal'` |
| `gap` | `Spacing` |
| `align` | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end' \| 'stretch'` |
| `justify` | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end' \| 'between'` |
| `wrap` | `boolean` |
| `padding` | `Spacing` |
| children | any |

## Card

A grouped block. The usual root of a `project.widget` surface.

| Prop | Type |
|---|---|
| `title` | `string` |
| `subtitle` | `string` |
| `actions` | `Action[]` |
| `padding` | `Spacing` |
| children | any |

## Text

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `string` | Or pass the text as children: `<Text>Merhaba {name}</Text>` |
| `variant` | `'title' \| 'heading' \| 'body' \| 'caption' \| 'label'` | |
| `tone` | `Tone` | |
| `weight` | `'regular' \| 'medium' \| 'semibold' \| 'bold'` | |
| `truncate` | `boolean` | One line with an ellipsis |

Children may only be strings, numbers, booleans/null (ignored) or arrays of them — no elements.

## Badge

| Prop | Type |
|---|---|
| `text` **required** | `string` |
| `tone` | `Tone` |

## EmptyState

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `title` **required** | `string` | |
| `description` | `string` | |
| `icon` | `IconName` | |
| `action` | `{ label: string; onPress: () => void }` | A button under the text |

## List

Rows with a title. Send all items; the host virtualises long lists.

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `items` **required** | `ListItem[]` | |
| `onSelect` | `({ key }) => void` | Row pressed; `key` is the item's key |
| `emptyText` | `string` | Shown when `items` is empty |
| `loading` | `boolean` | |

`ListItem`: `{ key: Key (required); title: string (required); subtitle?: string; meta?: string (short trailing text, e.g. a date); badge?: { text: string; tone?: Tone }; icon?: IconName; disabled?: boolean }`.

```tsx
<List
  items={tasks.map((t) => ({ key: t.id, title: t.title, meta: t.due ?? undefined, badge: { text: 'Gecikti', tone: 'danger' } }))}
  emptyText="Görev yok"
  onSelect={({ key }) => navigation.push('task', { taskId: String(key) })}
/>
```

Do not pass `undefined`-valued text you need to see: `meta: t.due ?? undefined` omits it cleanly.

## Table

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `columns` **required** | `TableColumn[]` | below |
| `rows` **required** | `{ key: Key; cells: Record<columnKey, string \| number \| null> }[]` | |
| `onSelectRow` | `({ key }) => void` | |
| `emptyText` | `string` | |
| `defaultSort` | `{ key: string; direction: 'asc' \| 'desc' }` | Initial order (SDK 1.5) |

`TableColumn`: `{ key: string; title: string; width?: number; align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end';
format?: 'text' | 'number' | 'currency' | 'percent'; currency?: string; sortable?: boolean }`.
`width` is a relative (flex) weight > 0. SDK 1.5:

- `format`: the host formats number cells with the person's locale (`Intl.NumberFormat`); a cell
  that is not a number shows as it is. `percent` takes a fraction (`0.034` → "%3,4").
- `currency`: ISO 4217 (`'TRY'`), required with `format: 'currency'` (`tree.invalid_prop`).
- `sortable`: the person sorts by tapping the title. The host sorts the rows itself, on the raw
  cell values (numbers as numbers); there is no handler.

```tsx
<Table
  columns={[
    { key: 'name', title: 'Kampanya', sortable: true },
    { key: 'spend', title: 'Harcama', format: 'currency', currency: 'TRY', align: 'end', sortable: true },
    { key: 'ctr', title: 'TO', format: 'percent', align: 'end', sortable: true },
  ]}
  rows={campaigns.map((c) => ({ key: c.id, cells: { name: c.name, spend: c.spend, ctr: c.ctr } }))}
  defaultSort={{ key: 'spend', direction: 'desc' }}
/>
```

## Chart

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` **required** | `'bar' \| 'line' \| 'area'` | `area` since SDK 1.5 |
| `series` **required** | `{ name: string; points: { x: string; y: number }[] }[]` | `x` is a label (e.g. a date) |
| `height` | `number` | Integer 1–2000 |
| `stacked` | `boolean` | Stacks the series; `bar` and `area` only (SDK 1.5) |
| `valueFormat` | `'number' \| 'currency' \| 'percent'` | Axis and tooltip format (SDK 1.5; `percent` takes fractions) |
| `currency` | `string` | ISO 4217; required with `valueFormat: 'currency'` |

Colours come from Olan's chart palette; you cannot set them.

```tsx
<Chart kind="area" stacked valueFormat="currency" currency="TRY"
  series={[{ name: 'Meta', points: days.map((d) => ({ x: d.day, y: d.meta })) }, { name: 'Google', points: days.map((d) => ({ x: d.day, y: d.google })) }]} />
```

## Form

Groups fields and submits their values together.

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `onSubmit` **required** | `({ values }) => void` | `values: Record<string, string>` maps each field `name` to its value |
| `submitLabel` | `string` | Submit button text |
| `cancelLabel` | `string` | |
| `onCancel` | `() => void` | |
| children | any | Fields and layout |

```tsx
<Form submitLabel="Kaydet" onSubmit={({ values }) => save(values.title, values.due)}>
  <TextField name="title" label="Başlık" required />
  <DatePicker name="due" label="Bitiş" />
</Form>
```

Submitting does **not** clear the fields: an uncontrolled field (no `value`) keeps what the user
typed, in Olan and in `renderApp`. To empty the form after a save, either control the fields
(`value={title}` + `onChange={({ value }) => setTitle(value)}`, then `setTitle('')`) or remount
the form with a new React `key` (`<Form key={saved} …>`, `setSaved((n) => n + 1)`).

## TextField

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` **required** | `string` | Key in `Form` values |
| `label` **required** | `string` | |
| `value` | `string` | Controlled value; omit for an uncontrolled field (it is not cleared on submit, see `Form`) |
| `placeholder` | `string` | |
| `multiline` | `boolean` | |
| `secure` | `boolean` | Password entry |
| `required` | `boolean` | |
| `error` | `string` | Validation message under the field |
| `onChange` | `({ value }) => void` | `value: string` |
| `maxLength` | `number` | 1–100000 (SDK 1.5): the host stops input at this many characters and shows an "n/max" counter under the field. Counted in Unicode code points (`[...value].length`), so an emoji is one |

## Select

The platform's own picker.

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` **required** | `string` | |
| `label` **required** | `string` | |
| `options` **required** | `{ value: string; label: string }[]` | |
| `value` | `string \| null` | Selected option value; `null` = none |
| `placeholder` | `string` | |
| `onChange` | `({ value }) => void` | `value` is the option `value` |

## DatePicker

The platform's own date (or date and time) picker.

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` **required** | `string` | |
| `label` **required** | `string` | |
| `value` | `string \| null` | ISO date `YYYY-MM-DD` or ISO date-time |
| `mode` | `'date' \| 'datetime'` | |
| `onChange` | `({ value }) => void` | ISO string |

## Button

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `label` **required** | `string` | Never empty (`ui.button_label_missing`) |
| `onPress` **required** | `() => void` | |
| `variant` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'ghost' \| 'danger'` | |
| `icon` | `IconName` | Shown next to the label |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | |
| `loading` | `boolean` | Also blocks presses |

## Menu

An anchored menu button: UIMenu on iOS, PopupMenu on Android, the Olan menu on web.

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | Button text. `label` or `icon` is required; prefer a label |
| `icon` | `IconName` | |
| `items` **required** | `{ key: Key; label: string; icon?: IconName; destructive?: boolean; disabled?: boolean }[]` | |
| `onSelect` **required** | `({ key }) => void` | Chosen item |

```tsx
<Menu
  label="Durumu değiştir"
  items={[{ key: 'in-process', label: 'Sürüyor' }, { key: 'completed', label: 'Tamamlandı' }, { key: 'cancelled', label: 'İptal', destructive: true }]}
  onSelect={({ key }) => setStatus(String(key) as ProjectTaskStatus)}
/>
```

For a menu opened from code (not anchored to a button) use `olan.ui.menu` (api.md).

## SDK 1.5 components

The components below need `"sdk": "^1.5.0"` and an Olan server that knows them (an older one
reports `tree.unknown_type`). They take no children and are **not allowed in chat cards**
(`card.component_not_allowed`). Numbers are formatted by the host with the person's locale
(`Intl.NumberFormat`); `percent` always takes a fraction (`0.034` → "%3,4" in Turkish).

## Tabs

A controlled segmented control: UISegmentedControl on iOS, Material segmented buttons on Android
(a scrolling tab bar above 5 tabs), the Olan segmented control on web. Render the selected content
yourself.

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `items` **required** | `{ key: Key; label: string; badge?: string \| number; disabled?: boolean }[]` | 2–8 tabs; `label` ≤ 40, never empty (`a11y.tab_label_missing`); `badge` ≤ 16 characters or a count |
| `value` **required** | `Key` | The selected `key` |
| `label` | `string` | The tab group's accessible name for screen readers, not shown; ≤ 40, default "Bölümler". Leave it out rather than passing an empty string (`a11y.tab_label_missing`) |
| `onChange` **required** | `({ key }) => void` | |

```tsx
const [tab, setTab] = useState('media');
<Tabs value={tab} label="Medya bölümleri" onChange={({ key }) => setTab(String(key))}
  items={[{ key: 'media', label: 'Medya', badge: processing }, { key: 'upload', label: 'Yükle' }, { key: 'stats', label: 'Analiz' }]} />
{tab === 'media' ? <MediaList /> : tab === 'upload' ? <UploadForm /> : <Stats />}
```

## Switch

The platform's on/off switch (UISwitch, Material switch).

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `label` **required** | `string` | Never empty (`a11y.field_label_missing`) |
| `value` **required** | `boolean` | |
| `description` | `string` | A second line under the label |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | |
| `onChange` | `({ value }) => void` | `value: boolean`, the new state |

Not a `Form` field: its value is not in `onSubmit`'s `values` (still `Record<string, string>`);
keep it in state with `onChange`.

## MultiSelect

Several values from a list: a checkmarked native menu on iOS (it stays open while the person
ticks), a multi-choice dialog on Android, the Olan menu on web. The trigger shows how many are
selected.

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `label` **required** | `string` | Never empty (`a11y.field_label_missing`) |
| `value` **required** | `string[]` | The selected option values |
| `options` **required** | `{ value: string; label: string }[]` | ≤ 200 |
| `placeholder` | `string` | Shown when nothing is selected |
| `max` | `number` | Most values the person may select |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | |
| `onChange` | `({ value }) => void` | `value: string[]`, the new selection |

Not a `Form` field either: keep its value with `onChange`.

```tsx
<MultiSelect label="Kanallar" value={channels} onChange={({ value }) => setChannels(value)} max={3}
  options={[{ value: 'instagram', label: 'Instagram' }, { value: 'tiktok', label: 'TikTok' }, { value: 'linkedin', label: 'LinkedIn' }]} />
```

## Stat

One key figure (a KPI tile).

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `label` **required** | `string` | |
| `value` **required** | `number \| string \| null` | A number is formatted by `format`; a string shows as it is; `null` shows "—" |
| `format` | `'number' \| 'currency' \| 'percent'` | Default `number` |
| `currency` | `string` | ISO 4217 (`'TRY'`); required with `format: 'currency'` (`tree.invalid_prop`) |
| `delta` | `number` | Relative change as a fraction, shown as a signed percent (`0.124` → "+%12,4") |
| `deltaGood` | `'up' \| 'down'` | Which direction is good (green); default `up`, `down` for costs such as CPC |
| `caption` | `string` | A short line, e.g. "Son 30 gün" |

```tsx
<Stack direction="horizontal" gap="md" wrap>
  <Stat label="Harcama" value={1250.5} format="currency" currency="TRY" delta={0.08} caption="Son 7 gün" />
  <Stat label="Tıklama oranı" value={0.034} format="percent" delta={-0.012} />
  <Stat label="Tıklama başı maliyet" value={2.4} format="currency" currency="TRY" delta={-0.05} deltaGood="down" />
</Stack>
```

## Banner

A message across the screen: a connection that expired, an error to act on, a success.

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `tone` **required** | `'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | |
| `text` **required** | `string` | |
| `title` | `string` | |
| `action` | `{ label: string; onPress: () => void }` | One button; `label` never empty (`a11y.action_label_missing`) |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` | Shows a close button; remove the banner in the handler |

```tsx
{error ? <Banner tone="danger" title="Sunucuya ulaşılamıyor" text={error.message} action={{ label: 'Tekrar dene', onPress: () => items.refetch() }} /> : null}
```

## Image

An image from the app's own server.

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `src` **required** | `string` | `https:` URL ≤ 2048 (`http:` only to local addresses in development) |
| `alt` **required** | `string` | What it shows, read by screen readers; `""` only for decoration (`validate --strict` warns `a11y.image_alt_missing`) |
| `aspectRatio` | `number` | Width / height, 0.1–10; default 16/9 |
| `fit` | `'cover' \| 'contain'` | Default `cover` |
| `poster` | `string` | A still shown while `src` loads or when it fails; same URL rule |

Origin rule (the host enforces it): `src` and `poster` must be on the origin of the manifest
`remote.url` (or the installation's override) or on a host granted as `http:<host>`. Any other
image is drawn as a neutral placeholder and logged as a warning; it is not an error. Serve images
from your app server (or a CDN host you list as `http:<host>`); signed, expiring URLs work.

```tsx
<Image src={item.thumbnailUrl} alt={item.title} aspectRatio={1} fit="cover" poster={item.posterUrl} />
```

## Avatar

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` **required** | `string` | The person's or brand's name: read aloud and used for the initials. Never empty (`a11y.avatar_name_missing`) |
| `src` | `string` | Picture, with the `Image` origin rule; initials when missing or broken |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | |

## ProgressBar

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `number` | 0–1; leave it out for an indeterminate bar (the platform's activity indicator) |
| `label` | `string` | E.g. "Yükleniyor…" |
| `tone` | `'default' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | |

Keep the percentage out of `label`: the bar already shows `value` itself.

```tsx
<ProgressBar value={progress} label="Yükleniyor…" />
<Button label="İptal" variant="ghost" onPress={() => task.cancel()} />
```

## Accessibility checks

`validate --strict` and the marketplace lint the rendered tree (`lintUiTree`, errors.md): a
`Button`, field (`TextField`, `Select`, `DatePicker`, `Switch`, `MultiSelect`), `Menu` item, action
or `Banner` action without a label, a `Tabs` item without a label (`a11y.tab_label_missing`) and
an `Avatar` without a name (`a11y.avatar_name_missing`) are errors; an icon-only `Menu` and an
`Image` with an empty `alt` are warnings.

## Exported prop types

`ScreenProps`, `StackProps`, `CardProps`, `TextProps`, `BadgeProps`, `EmptyStateProps`, `ListProps`,
`ListItem`, `TableProps`, `TableColumn`, `TableRow`, `ChartProps`, `ChartSeries`, `FormProps`,
`TextFieldProps`, `SelectProps`, `SelectOption`, `DatePickerProps`, `ButtonProps`, `MenuProps`,
`MenuItem`, `TabsProps`, `TabItem`, `SwitchProps`, `MultiSelectProps`, `StatProps`, `BannerProps`,
`ImageProps`, `AvatarProps`, `ProgressBarProps`, `ValueFormat`, `Action`, `BadgeData`, `Key`,
`Tone`, `Spacing`, `IconName`, `TextChildren`.

## Icons

`icon` props take an Olan icon name. Unknown names fall back to a generic icon. Names:

`mail chat meetings calendar projects marketing contacts files settings inbox all-inboxes archive
delete report-spam reply reply-all forward compose edit draw mark-unread mark-read flag folder
search attachment send send-arrow add minus close clear check check-double check-circle checkbox
more back chevron-right chevron-down chevron-up chevron-up-down list day-view refresh copy paste
share document document-text photo photo-library camera camera-flip video-play gif emoji poll mic
mic-off video video-off call call-end screen-share speaker waveform play pause stop group account
lock block sidebar person-add link record signal approval compare clock warning status-open
status-active touch face-id fingerprint qr-scan help info pin list-checks seal-check warning-circle
undo favorite bell bell-slash timer sign-out crop rotate sticker download tag snooze print`

<!-- docs/api.md -->
# `olan.*` API

```ts
import { olan, OlanError, RemoteError, isRemoteError } from '@olan-app/sdk';
```

Every call is asynchronous: the sandbox sends it to Olan, Olan checks the permission and answers.
A failed call rejects with an `OlanError` whose `code` is one of `permission_denied`,
`not_installed`, `invalid_params`, `unknown_method`, `host_error`, `http_blocked`, `cancelled`,
`validation_failed`, `conflict`, `not_found`, `forbidden_record`, `quota_exceeded`, `project_not_enabled`
(SDK 1.6: the call names a project the app was not added to); `olan.remote.request`
rejects with a `RemoteError` (`remote_rejected`, `remote_unavailable`, `consent_required`, `rate_limited`, …),
uploads also with `upload_failed` (errors.md). Call `olan.*` from event handlers, effects or `useQuery` — not during render.

| Call | Returns | Permission |
|---|---|---|
| `olan.projects.list({ limit?, cursor? })` | `{ items: Project[]; nextCursor?: string }` (projects the app is enabled in) | `projects:read` |
| `olan.projects.get(projectId)` | `ProjectDetail` | `projects:read` |
| `olan.projects.tasks(projectId, { status? })` | `ProjectTask[]` | `projects:read` |
| `olan.projects.updateTask(projectId, taskId, { status?, due?, assigneeId?, revision })` | `ProjectTask` | `tasks:write` (or the older `projects:write`) |
| `olan.projects.createTask(projectId, { title, listId?, description?, status?, due?, allDay?, assigneeId?, priority? })` | `ProjectTask` | `tasks:write` |
| `olan.projects.deleteTask(projectId, taskId, { revision })` | `void` | `tasks:delete` |
| `olan.projects.deleteList(projectId, listId, { revision })` | `void` | `projects:delete` |
| `olan.users.get(ids)` | `DirectoryUser[]` | `users:read` |
| `olan.chat.conversations()` | `Conversation[]` | `chat:read` |
| `olan.chat.messages(conversationId, { limit? })` | `Message[]` | `chat:read` |
| `olan.storage.get<T>(key)` | `T \| null` | `storage` |
| `olan.storage.set(key, value)` | `void` | `storage` |
| `olan.storage.remove(key)` | `void` | `storage` |
| `olan.storage.keys()` | `string[]` | `storage` |
| `olan.db.collection<T>(name)` → `insert(data)`, `get(id)`, `query({ where?, orderBy?, limit?, cursor? })`, `update(id, patch, { revision })`, `delete(id, { revision? })`, `count(where?)` | `DbRow<T>`, `DbRow<T> \| null`, `{ rows, nextCursor }`, `DbRow<T>`, `void`, `number` | `db` (database.md) |
| `olan.settings.get()` | `Record<string, JsonValue>` | none |
| `olan.project.config.get(projectId)` | `ProjectConfig` (SDK 1.6) | none; the app is enabled in the project |
| `olan.project.config.set(projectId, value, { revision? })` | `ProjectConfig` | none; members who may change the project |
| `olan.project.statuses.list(projectId)` | `ProjectStatus[]` (SDK 1.7) | `projects:read` |
| `olan.project.statuses.define(projectId, statuses)` | the app's `ProjectStatus[]` | `projects:extend` |
| `olan.project.statuses.remove(projectId, key, { replacementKey? })` | `{ movedTasks }` | `projects:extend` |
| `olan.project.labels.list(projectId)` | `ProjectLabel[]` | `projects:read` |
| `olan.project.labels.define(projectId, labels)` | the app's `ProjectLabel[]` | `projects:extend` |
| `olan.project.labels.remove(projectId, key)` | `void` | `projects:extend` |
| `olan.project.fields.list(projectId)` | `ProjectField[]` (SDK 1.8) | `projects:read` |
| `olan.project.fields.define(projectId, fields)` | the app's `ProjectField[]` | `projects:extend` |
| `olan.project.fields.remove(projectId, key)` | `void` | `projects:extend` |
| `olan.project.fields.values(projectId, target)` | `{ target, values }` | `projects:read` |
| `olan.project.fields.setValues(projectId, target, values)` | `{ target, values }` | `tasks:write` |
| `olan.project.links.list(projectId, target?)` | `RecordLink[]` | `projects:read` |
| `olan.project.links.upsert(projectId, { target, externalId, card })` | `RecordLink` | `tasks:write` |
| `olan.project.links.remove(projectId, linkId)` | `void` | `tasks:write` |
| `olan.project.links.setStatus(projectId, linkId, input)` | `{ target, status?, statusId?, statusKey?, state? }` | `tasks:write` (or `projects:write`) |
| `olan.project.calendar.list(projectId, { from?, to? })` | `ProjectCalendarItem[]` | `projects:read` |
| `olan.project.calendar.upsert(projectId, item)` | `ProjectCalendarItem` | `projects:extend` |
| `olan.project.calendar.remove(projectId, externalId)` | `void` | `projects:extend` |
| `olan.project.activity.post(projectId, text, { target? })` | `void` | `projects:extend` |
| `olan.project.approvals.list(projectId, { state? })` | `ProjectApproval[]` | `projects:read` |
| `olan.project.approvals.request(projectId, input)` | `ProjectApproval` | `projects:extend` |
| `olan.project.approvals.cancel(projectId, approvalId)` | `ProjectApproval` | `projects:extend` |
| `olan.http.fetch(url, { method?, headers?, body? })` | `HttpResponse` | `http:<host of url>` |
| `olan.ui.confirm({ title, message?, confirmLabel?, cancelLabel?, destructive? })` | `boolean` | none |
| `olan.ui.prompt({ title, message?, placeholder?, defaultValue? })` | `string \| null` | none |
| `olan.ui.toast({ text, tone? })` | `void` | none |
| `olan.ui.menu({ items })` | chosen `key` or `null` | none |
| `olan.ui.datePicker({ value?, mode? })` | ISO string or `null` | none |
| `olan.ui.share({ text, url? })` | `void` | none |
| `olan.navigation.push(screen, params?)` | `void` | none |
| `olan.navigation.pop()` | `void` | none |
| `olan.navigation.replace(screen, params?)` | `void` | none |
| `olan.projects.create({ title, description? })` | `Project` | `projects:create` |
| `olan.projects.archive(projectId)` | `void` | `projects:archive` |
| `olan.chat.postCard({ conversationId, card, threadRootId? })` | `{ messageId }` | `chat:write` |
| `olan.chat.updateCard(messageId, card)` | `{ messageId }` | `chat:write` |
| `olan.calendar.calendars()` | `Calendar[]` | `calendar:read` |
| `olan.calendar.events({ from, to, calendarId?, limit? })` | `CalendarEvent[]` | `calendar:read` |
| `olan.calendar.createEvent({ title, start, end?, duration?, calendarId?, timeZone?, isAllDay?, location?, description? })` | `CalendarEvent` | `calendar:write` |
| `olan.calendar.updateEvent(eventId, patch)` | `CalendarEvent` | `calendar:write` |
| `olan.calendar.deleteEvent(eventId)` | `void` | `calendar:delete` |
| `olan.contacts.addressBooks()` | `AddressBook[]` | `contacts:read` |
| `olan.contacts.search(query, { limit? })` | `Contact[]` | `contacts:read` |
| `olan.contacts.create({ name, addressBookId?, emails?, phones?, organization?, title?, note? })` | `Contact` | `contacts:write` |
| `olan.contacts.update(contactId, patch)` | `Contact` | `contacts:write` |
| `olan.contacts.delete(contactId)` | `void` | `contacts:delete` |
| `olan.mail.getMessage(messageId)` | `MailMessage` | `mail:read` (only the email the surface was opened on) |
| `olan.meetings.get(meetingId)` | `Meeting` | `meetings:read` |
| `olan.backend.call<T>(name, args?)` | `T` (the function's JSON result) | none; the manifest declares `server` (backend.md) |
| `olan.remote.request({ method, path, query?, headers?, body?, timeoutMs? })` | `{ status, headers, body }` | none (implied `remote`); the manifest declares `remote.requests` (remote-requests.md) |
| `olan.files.pick({ accept?, multiple?, maxFiles?, maxBytes? })` | `FileHandle[]` | `files:pick` (files.md) |
| `olan.files.upload(file, { url, method?, headers?, formField?, fields?, onProgress? })` | `UploadTask`: a promise of `{ status, headers, body }` with `uploadId` and `cancel()` | `files:pick` |
| `olan.files.cancel(uploadId)` | `void` | `files:pick` |
| `olan.ui.openUrl(url)` | `void` | none (links.md) |
| `olan.ui.openExternal(url, { expectReturn? })` | `{ returned: true, params } \| { returned: false }` | none (links.md) |

## olan.projects

**Enabled projects (SDK 1.6, Olan Apps phase 6).** A project stays generic until a member adds an
app to it (project page → Uygulamalar). On the person's behalf an installed app reaches only those
projects: `list` leaves the others out, and every call naming one fails with `project_not_enabled`.
The project surfaces (`project.widget`, `project.tab`, `project.settings`) show only there too.
Projects the app creates (`projects.create`) have it enabled. Studio previews without an
installation keep the person's own reach.

```ts
const { items, nextCursor } = await olan.projects.list({ limit: 50 });     // limit default 50
const detail = await olan.projects.get('p0');                              // { project, members, lists, tasks }
const open = await olan.projects.tasks('p0', { status: 'needs-action' });
const updated = await olan.projects.updateTask('p0', task.id, { status: 'completed', revision: task.revision });
const created = await olan.projects.createTask('p0', { title: 'Follow up', due: '2026-10-20' });
await olan.projects.deleteTask('p0', created.id, { revision: created.revision });
await olan.projects.deleteList('p0', list.id, { revision: list.revision });   // empty, non-default work packages only
```

- Pass `cursor: nextCursor` to get the next page; `nextCursor` is absent on the last page.
- `updateTask` needs the task's current `revision` (optimistic concurrency). If the task changed in
  the meantime the call fails with `conflict` (`invalid_params` on Olan servers before 1b); reload
  the task and retry. The result is the updated task (with a new `revision`). Only `status`, `due`
  (ISO date or `null`) and `assigneeId` (user id or `null`) can be changed. New apps request
  `tasks:write`; `projects:write` keeps working for `updateTask` only.
- `createTask` puts the task in `listId`, or else in the project's default work package
  (`lists[].isDefault`). The task's `createdByApp` is your app id. Needs `tasks:write`.
- `deleteTask` needs the task's current `revision` and `tasks:delete`. Every deletion is written
  to the organization's audit log. Tasks with a delivery/approval workflow, and (when the admin
  turned on "only records the app created") tasks the app did not create, fail with
  `forbidden_record`.
- `deleteList` removes (archives) an **empty** work package: no live tasks or sub-packages. The
  project's default work package is never removed. Both fail with `forbidden_record`. Needs
  `projects:delete`. Apps cannot change or delete projects, nor create work packages; creating
  and archiving projects is `projects.create` / `projects.archive` (below).
- Protected records: projects, the default work package, task statuses and fields (fixed by
  Olan), project chats and calendars, members, accounts. Show a toast such as "Bu kayıt korunuyor"
  on `forbidden_record`.

Types (all exported from `@olan-app/sdk`):

```ts
type ProjectTaskStatus = 'needs-action' | 'in-process' | 'completed' | 'cancelled';

interface Project {
  id: string; name: string; description: string; timeZone: string; archived: boolean;
  revision: number; role: ProjectRole; createdAt: string; updatedAt: string;
  lastActivityAt?: string; taskKeyPrefix?: string;
}
interface ProjectTask {
  id: string; projectId: string; listId: string; key?: string; number?: number;
  title: string; description: string; status: ProjectTaskStatus; assigneeId: string | null;
  createdBy: string; start?: string | null; due: string | null; allDay: boolean;
  revision: number; updatedAt?: string;
  createdByApp?: string | null;      // app id when an app created it
}
interface ProjectDetail { project: Project; members: ProjectMember[]; lists: ProjectTaskList[]; tasks: ProjectTask[] }
interface ProjectMember { userId: string; displayName: string; role: ProjectRole }
interface ProjectTaskList { id: string; name: string; isDefault: boolean; revision: number; parentId: string | null }
type ProjectRole = 'owner' | 'manager' | 'member' | 'guest' | string;
interface UpdateTaskInput { status?: ProjectTaskStatus; due?: string | null; assigneeId?: string | null; revision: number }
interface CreateTaskInput { title: string; listId?: string; description?: string; status?: ProjectTaskStatus; due?: string | null; allDay?: boolean; assigneeId?: string | null; priority?: number }
```

`due` is an ISO date (`2026-10-16`) or date-time, or `null`. Compare dates as strings of the same
length (`task.due.slice(0, 10) < today`) or with `Date`.

## olan.project.config

The app's own configuration of one project (SDK 1.6), kept per installation and project: which
brand, account or pipeline the project uses, the app's choices for it. No permission is needed; the
app must be enabled in the project (else `project_not_enabled`). Any member reads it; members who
may change the project set it (read-only members get `permission_denied`, archived projects
`conflict`). The value is a JSON object of at most 64 KiB (`payload_too_large`).

```ts
const config = await olan.project.config.get(projectId);
// { projectId, value: { brandId: 'b1' }, revision: 3, updatedBy: '<user id>', updatedAt: '2026-10-22T09:00:00Z' }
// Before the first set: { value: {}, revision: 0, updatedBy: null, updatedAt: null }
await olan.project.config.set(projectId, { ...config.value, brandId: 'b2' }, { revision: config.revision });
```

- `set` replaces the whole value. With `{ revision }` it is refused with `conflict` when someone
  changed it meanwhile (`revision: 0`: only if nothing is stored yet); without it the write wins.
- The configuration stays when the app is removed from the project, and answers again once a member
  adds it back. It goes with the installation (uninstall) or the project.
- The app's server reads and writes it too: `GET`/`PUT /api/v2/apps/installations/:id/projects/:projectId/config`
  with the app's own token (server.md), and backend code with the same `olan.project.config`.
- In React, `useProjectConfig(projectId?)` (hooks.md) loads it and saves on the loaded revision.

```ts
interface ProjectConfig {
  projectId: string;
  value: Record<string, JsonValue>;
  revision: number;                 // 0 until the first set
  updatedBy: string | null;         // a user id, or 'app:<installationId>' (the app's server)
  updatedAt: string | null;
}
```

## olan.project: records, statuses, calendar, feed, approvals

SDK 1.7 (Olan Apps phase 6): what the app adds to the projects it is enabled in — the same calls in
the UI and in backend code; the app's server uses the routes under
`/api/v2/apps/installations/:id/projects/:projectId/` (`links`, `statuses`, `labels`, `fields`,
`field-values`, `calendar`, `activity`, `approvals`) with its own token. Projects without the app fail with
`project_not_enabled`; archived projects refuse changes with `conflict`.

**Record links.** One of the app's records (`externalId`, the app's own id) attached to a task or an
issue, with a card the app draws on it. The card is a chat card (cards.md) whose buttons only
`{ kind: 'open', payload? }`: they open the app's `record.card` surface (surfaces.md). Any other
button fails with `validation_failed` (`invalid_card`). The same `externalId` on the same target
replaces the card; an app links at most 10 records to one task or issue (`quota_exceeded`).

```ts
const link = await olan.project.links.upsert(projectId, {
  target: { kind: 'task', id: task.id },
  externalId: 'SAT-12',
  card: { version: 1, root: 1, fallbackText: 'SAT-12 · Toplantı masası', nodes: [
    { id: 1, type: 'Card', props: { title: 'Toplantı masası', subtitle: 'SAT-12' }, children: [2] },
    { id: 2, type: 'Button', props: { label: 'Kaydı aç', action: { kind: 'open', payload: { id: 'SAT-12' } } }, children: [] },
  ] },
});
await olan.project.links.setStatus(projectId, link.id, { statusKey: 'awaiting-approval' }); // a task
await olan.project.links.setStatus(projectId, issueLink.id, { state: 'closed', stateReason: 'completed' }); // an issue
const onTask = await olan.project.links.list(projectId, { kind: 'task', id: task.id });
```

`setStatus` moves a linked task by `statusKey` (a key of the project's statuses: the defaults
`todo`, `in_progress`, `done`, `cancelled` or one the app defined), `statusId`, or the CalDAV
`status` (its first status of that kind); a linked issue opens or closes with `state`. The change is
an ordinary edit of the person the app acts for: the project feed shows it under the app and other
apps hear `project.task.updated` / `project.task.completed`. Members may take a link off
(the card disappears); a link of an app removed from the project stays read-only.

**Statuses and labels.** The app defines its own by stable keys (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,62}$`,
≤ 20 per call); `define` adds or updates and returns all of the app's. Members put them on tasks
but cannot rename, recolour or remove them. A key or a name the project already uses is `conflict`;
a status keeps its category. Removing a status moves its tasks to `replacementKey` (a status of the
same kind) or the first status of its kind; the last status of a required kind cannot go (`conflict`).

```ts
await olan.project.statuses.define(projectId, [{ key: 'awaiting-approval', name: 'Onay bekliyor', category: 'started' }]);
await olan.project.labels.define(projectId, [{ key: 'hardware', name: 'Donanım', groupName: 'Tür' }]);
```

**Custom fields** (needs `"sdk": "^1.8.0"`). The project's own fields and the app's, defined by stable keys like
statuses (≤ 20 per call, ≤ 50 fields per project); `define` returns all of the app's. Members fill them in on tasks
and issues (`appliesTo`, default tasks) but cannot change or remove them; a taken key or name is `conflict`, the
`type` is fixed (`invalid_params`). Options keep their `id` (a new one gets a slug of its name); removing an option
or the field clears its values. Values are keyed by field key (the project's own fields: by id): text, url, date
(`YYYY-MM-DD`), select option id and person (a member's user id) are strings, then numbers, `boolean` checkboxes and
lists of option ids. `setValues` changes the fields it names; `null` clears one (not a `required` one:
`invalid_params`); an app's field removed with its app from the project is read-only (`conflict`).

```ts
await olan.project.fields.define(projectId, [{ key: 'channel', name: 'Kanal', type: 'select', options: [{ id: 'ig', name: 'Instagram' }], showOnCard: true }]);
await olan.project.fields.setValues(projectId, { kind: 'task', id: task.id }, { channel: 'ig' });
const { values } = await olan.project.fields.values(projectId, { kind: 'task', id: task.id });   // { channel: 'ig', … }
```

**Calendar layer and feed lines.** Calendar items (one per `externalId`, ≤ 500 per project; all-day
items take dates) show in the project calendar while the app is enabled in the project; `linkId`
makes the item open its record. `list` takes a range of at most 366 days. `activity.post` writes a
line (1–280 characters) in the project feed under the app, optionally about a task or issue.

```ts
await olan.project.calendar.upsert(projectId, { externalId: 'SAT-12', title: 'Teslim: Toplantı masası', start: '2026-11-05', allDay: true, linkId: link.id });
await olan.project.activity.post(projectId, 'SAT-12 bağlandı, onay bekliyor', { target: { kind: 'task', id: task.id } });
```

**Approvals.** `request` asks 1–10 project members who may change the project; they find it in
their approval box (with the record card, if given). `mode: 'all'` (default): every approver
approves, one rejection rejects; `'any'`: the first decision decides. The app hears the outcome as
`project.approval.decided` (server.md#events) and can `cancel` a pending request (`conflict` once
decided).

```ts
const approval = await olan.project.approvals.request(projectId, { title: 'SAT-12 onayı', approverIds: [managerId], mode: 'any', linkId: link.id, card: link.card });
const pending = await olan.project.approvals.list(projectId, { state: 'pending' });   // newest first
```

```ts
type ProjectStatusCategory = 'backlog' | 'unstarted' | 'started' | 'completed' | 'cancelled';
interface ProjectStatus { id: string; projectId: string; name: string; color: string; category: ProjectStatusCategory; position: number; key: string | null; createdByApp: string | null; appInstallationId: string | null; revision: number }
interface ProjectLabel { id: string; projectId: string; name: string; color: string; groupName: string | null; description: string; position: number; key: string | null; createdByApp: string | null; appInstallationId: string | null; revision: number }
type ProjectFieldType = 'text' | 'number' | 'date' | 'select' | 'multi_select' | 'person' | 'url' | 'checkbox';
type ProjectFieldValue = string | number | boolean | string[];
interface ProjectField { id: string; projectId: string; name: string; description: string; type: ProjectFieldType; position: number; options: { id: string; name: string; color: string }[]; required: boolean; appliesTo: ('task' | 'issue')[]; showOnCard: boolean; key: string | null; createdByApp: string | null; appInstallationId: string | null; appName?: string | null; readOnly?: boolean; revision: number }
interface ProjectFieldDefinition { key: string; name: string; type: ProjectFieldType; description?: string; options?: { id?: string; name: string; color?: string }[]; required?: boolean; appliesTo?: ('task' | 'issue')[]; showOnCard?: boolean; position?: number }
interface ProjectFieldValues { target: RecordTarget; values: Record<string, ProjectFieldValue> }
type RecordTarget = { kind: 'task' | 'issue'; id: string };
// RecordLink, ProjectCalendarItem and ProjectApproval also carry the app: installationId, appId, name, active.
interface RecordLink { id: string; projectId: string; target: RecordTarget; externalId: string; title: string; card: AppCard; createdBy: string | null; updatedBy: string | null; revision: number; createdAt: string; updatedAt: string }
interface ProjectCalendarItem { id: string; projectId: string; externalId: string; title: string; start: string; end: string; allDay: boolean; color: string | null; linkId: string | null; target: RecordTarget | null; updatedAt: string }
interface ProjectApproval { id: string; projectId: string; projectName: string; externalId: string | null; linkId: string | null; target: RecordTarget | null; title: string; card: AppCard | null; approvers: string[]; mode: 'all' | 'any'; state: 'pending' | 'approved' | 'rejected' | 'cancelled'; dueAt: string | null; requestedBy: string | null; decisions: { userId: string; decision: 'approve' | 'reject'; note: string; decidedAt: string }[]; createdAt: string; decidedAt: string | null }
```

## olan.users

```ts
const people = await olan.users.get([task.assigneeId, row.createdBy]);   // DirectoryUser[]
```

`DirectoryUser`: `{ id, displayName, email, title?, department?, team?, avatarUrl? }`. Ids are the
central Olan user ids (`useUser().id`, `createdBy`, `assigneeId`, `member.userId`). Unknown ids and
people outside the organization are left out; duplicates are asked once and lists over 100 are
split into several calls. The current user's id needs no permission (`useUser()`); their name
does. `users:read` is all it needs: no other permission is required alongside it. In components
use `useUsers(ids)` (hooks.md).

There is **no lookup by email or name** (no directory search). To relate an email address (e.g. a
`mail.sidebar` sender) to Olan people or tasks, collect the ids you already have (`member.userId`
of `olan.projects.get`, `task.assigneeId`, `createdBy`), call `olan.users.get(ids)` and compare
`user.email.toLowerCase()` with the address; for people outside the organization use
`olan.contacts.search(email)`.

## olan.chat

```ts
const conversations = await olan.chat.conversations();
const messages = await olan.chat.messages(conversations[0].id, { limit: 20 }); // the latest messages (limit default 50)
```

```ts
interface Conversation { id: string; kind: 'direct' | 'group'; title: string | null; projectId?: string | null; createdAt: string; updatedAt: string; unreadCount?: number }
interface Message { id: string; conversationId: string; sender: { id: string; displayName: string }; body: string | null; replyToId: string | null; createdAt: string; editedAt: string | null; deletedAt: string | null }
```

Apps cannot send messages. With `chat:write` they post **cards** as the app:
`olan.chat.postCard({ conversationId, card })` and `olan.chat.updateCard(messageId, card)` (cards.md).

## olan.projects.create / archive

```ts
const project = await olan.projects.create({ title: 'Standup', description: 'Günlük' });   // projects:create
await olan.projects.archive(project.id);                                                  // projects:archive
```

`create` opens the project with its own chat, calendar and default work package, on behalf of the
person; `project.createdByApp` is your app id. `archive` removes (archives) only projects your app
created (others: `forbidden_record`, reason `not_created_by_app`); an archived one answers `conflict`.

## olan.calendar

```ts
const calendars = await olan.calendar.calendars();     // [{ id, name, color, isDefault, mayWrite }]
const events = await olan.calendar.events({ from: '2026-10-19', to: '2026-10-26' });   // ≤ 366 days, limit ≤ 200
const event = await olan.calendar.createEvent({ title: 'Standup notu', start: '2026-10-20T09:00:00+03:00', duration: 'PT15M' });
await olan.calendar.updateEvent(event.id, { location: 'Toplantı odası' });
await olan.calendar.deleteEvent(event.id);
```

```ts
interface CalendarEvent { id: string; calendarId: string; uid: string; title: string; start: string; end: string; timeZone: string | null; isAllDay: boolean; location: string | null; description: string | null; isOrganizer: boolean; createdByApp: string | null; updatedAt: string | null }
```

- Without `calendarId` the default calendar is used (else the first writable one). Pass `end` or an
  ISO 8601 `duration`; neither means one hour (one day for all-day events).
- Apps never send invitations: there is no `participants`.
- `updateEvent` / `deleteEvent` fail with `forbidden_record` for Olan meetings (UID `…@olan.app`) and
  project calendar events (`system_record`), invitations (`not_organizer`), read-only calendars
  (`permission_denied`) and, when the admin requires it, events the app did not create
  (`not_created_by_app`). Calendars themselves cannot be created or deleted. Deletions are audited.

## olan.contacts

```ts
const books = await olan.contacts.addressBooks();        // [{ id, name, isDefault, shared }]
const found = await olan.contacts.search('ayşe');        // name, email or organization; limit ≤ 50
const contact = await olan.contacts.create({ name: 'Ayşe Yılmaz', emails: ['ayse@example.com'] });
await olan.contacts.update(contact.id, { phones: ['+90 555 000 0000'] });
await olan.contacts.delete(contact.id);
```

`Contact`: `{ id, addressBookId, name, emails, phones, organization, title, note, createdByApp, updatedAt }`.
Contacts in shared or directory address books are read-only (`forbidden_record`, `system_record`);
address books cannot be created or deleted.

## olan.mail and olan.meetings

```ts
const { messageId } = useSurfaceParams<'mail.sidebar'>();
const message = await olan.mail.getMessage(messageId);   // { id, subject, from, to, cc, receivedAt, textBody, attachments: [{ name, type, size }] }
const meeting = await olan.meetings.get(meetingId);      // { id, slug, title, startsAt, endsAt, status, organizerId, participants: [{ userId?, displayName, role }] }
```

`mail.getMessage` reads only the email a `mail.sidebar` / `mail.action` surface was opened on (other
ids: `permission_denied`); Olan reads it with the person's own mail session. There is no other
mail access.

## olan.storage

Private key–value storage per app installation **and** user. Values are JSON (≤ 64 KiB each, at
most 1000 keys).

```ts
const favorites = (await olan.storage.get<string[]>('favorites')) ?? [];
await olan.storage.set('favorites', [...favorites, id]);
await olan.storage.remove('favorites');
const keys = await olan.storage.keys();
```

`get` returns `null` for a missing key.

## olan.db

The app's own database: collections declared in the manifest's `data`, rows with revisions,
indexed queries and cursors. Needs `db`. Everything about it is in database.md.

```ts
const decisions = olan.db.collection<{ title: string; status?: 'open' | 'done' }>('decisions');
const row = await decisions.insert({ title: 'Ship 1.1', status: 'open' });
const { rows, nextCursor } = await decisions.query({ where: { status: 'open' }, orderBy: { field: 'title' }, limit: 20 });
await decisions.update(row.id, { status: 'done' }, { revision: row.revision });
```

## olan.settings

```ts
const settings = await olan.settings.get();   // e.g. { threshold: 3, currency: 'TRY' }
```

The values of the manifest `settings` fields (manifest.md), with defaults applied. Admins (or the
user, for a personal installation) edit them in Olan → Ayarlar → Uygulamalar. Apps cannot write
settings. In components prefer `useSettings()` (hooks.md), which re-renders when they change.

## olan.http

The sandbox has no network. `olan.http.fetch` asks Olan to make the request; Olan only reaches
hosts listed as `http:<host>` permissions (permissions.md).

```ts
const response = await olan.http.fetch('https://api.example.com/v1/rates?base=USD', {
  method: 'GET',                         // 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'PATCH' | 'DELETE' | 'HEAD'
  headers: { accept: 'application/json' },
  body: null,                            // string | null; JSON.stringify(...) for JSON bodies
});
if (response.status !== 200) throw new Error(`API answered ${response.status}`);
const data = response.json<{ rates: Record<string, number> }>();
```

`HttpResponse`: `{ status: number; headers: Record<string, string>; body: string; json<T>(): T }`.
`json()` throws `OlanError('invalid_params')` when the body is not JSON. Non-2xx statuses do
**not** reject; check `status`. Redirects are returned, not followed. Request bodies ≤ 512 KiB,
response bodies ≤ 2 MiB (text). Cookies of the user are never sent; put API keys in `headers`
(store them in a `secret` setting). Rejections: `http_blocked` (host not permitted, or a private
address), `host_error`.

## olan.ui

Each call opens the platform's own control and resolves when the user answers.

```ts
if (await olan.ui.confirm({ title: 'Görev silinsin mi?', confirmLabel: 'Sil', destructive: true })) { … }
const name = await olan.ui.prompt({ title: 'Yeni ad', defaultValue: 'Rapor' });   // null = cancelled
await olan.ui.toast({ text: 'Kaydedildi', tone: 'success' });                       // tone: 'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger'
const key = await olan.ui.menu({ items: [{ key: 'edit', label: 'Düzenle' }, { key: 'delete', label: 'Sil', destructive: true }] }); // null = dismissed
const day = await olan.ui.datePicker({ value: '2026-10-16', mode: 'date' });        // ISO string or null
await olan.ui.share({ text: 'Rapor hazır', url: 'https://example.com/r/1' });
```

`olan.ui.menu` items: `{ key: string; label: string; icon?: IconName; destructive?: boolean; disabled?: boolean }`.
For a menu attached to a button, use the `Menu` component instead.

Links and sign-in flows (SDK 1.5, links.md):

```ts
await olan.ui.openUrl('https://media.example.com/items/7');                      // the platform browser; resolves at once
const flow = await olan.ui.openExternal(authorizeUrl, { expectReturn: true });  // system browser / ASWebAuthenticationSession / Custom Tabs
if (flow.returned) await finishConnection(flow.params);                         // the query of https://<Olan web>/apps/return/<installationId>?…
```

Both take `https:` URLs (`http:` only to local addresses in development). `openExternal` resolves
`{ returned: false }` at once without `expectReturn`, and when the person closes the flow or after
30 minutes; check `params.state` on your server.

## olan.remote

The app's own server, as the person (SDK 1.5; manifest `remote` with `"requests": true`; everything
in remote-requests.md):

```ts
const page = await olan.remote.request({ method: 'GET', path: '/items', query: { status: 'ready' } });
const created = await olan.remote.request({ method: 'POST', path: '/items', body: { title: 'Lansman' }, timeoutMs: 60_000 });
```

The result is `{ status, headers: { 'content-type'?, etag? }, body }` for answers 200–399. Failures
reject with `RemoteError` (`code`, `status`, `details` = the server's body for `remote_rejected` and
`remote_unavailable`, `reason?`, `retryAfterSeconds?`); `isRemoteError(error, 'remote_rejected')`
narrows it. Body ≤ 1 MiB, answer ≤ 4 MiB, timeout 1–60 s (default 30 s), 300 requests a minute.

## olan.files

Pick files with the platform picker and upload them straight to the app's server (SDK 1.5,
`files:pick`; everything in files.md):

```ts
const [file] = await olan.files.pick({ accept: ['image/*', 'video/*'], maxBytes: 300 * 1024 * 1024 });   // [] = cancelled
if (file) {
  const task = olan.files.upload(file, { url: uploadUrl, onProgress: ({ loaded, total }) => setProgress(loaded / total) });
  // task.uploadId; task.cancel() (or olan.files.cancel(task.uploadId)) makes it reject with `cancelled`
  const { status, headers, body } = await task;    // every HTTP status resolves: check `status`
}
```

`url` must be on the origin of `remote.url` or a host granted as `http:<host>` (`http_blocked`
otherwise). PUT (default) sends the raw bytes, POST `multipart/form-data`; both send the name in
`x-olan-file-name`.

## olan.navigation

```ts
await olan.navigation.push('task', { taskId: 't1' });
await olan.navigation.replace('done', null);
await olan.navigation.pop();
```

The stack lives in the app; read it with `useNavigation()` (navigation.md). `pop()` on the first
screen keeps the stack and tells Olan, which closes a modal surface.

## olan.backend

`olan.backend.call(name, args?)` runs `functions[name]` of the app's backend code (`server`,
backend.md) with the person's consented permissions and resolves with its JSON result (≤ 256 KiB).
Failures: `backend_function_not_found`, `backend_error` (the function threw; `message` is its
error), `backend_limit`, `backend_busy`, `payload_too_large`, `backend_unavailable`, `backend_migrating` (errors.md).

```tsx
const summary = useQuery(() => olan.backend.call<Summary>('summary'), []);
```

## OlanError

```ts
try {
  await olan.projects.updateTask(projectId, task.id, { status: 'completed', revision: task.revision });
} catch (error) {
  if (isOlanError(error, 'conflict')) { /* reload and retry */ }
  else if (error instanceof OlanError && error.code === 'permission_denied') { /* … */ }
}
```

`error.code` (`OlanErrorCode`: the codes above, or a newer host's) and `error.message`.
`isOlanError(error, code?)` narrows an unknown error. `useQuery` puts the error in
`query.error`, `useCollection` in `list.error`. `error.hostDetails` holds machine-readable extras the
host sent, if any. `RemoteError` (a subclass, from `olan.remote.request`) adds `status`, `details`,
`reason?` and `retryAfterSeconds?` (remote-requests.md#errors-remoteerror).

## Other exports

`defineApp`, `isAppDefinition`, `isOlanError`, `isRemoteError`, `RemoteError`, `SDK_VERSION` (`'1.8.1'`), `PROTOCOL_VERSION` (`1`), `SURFACE_NAMES`, and types
`SurfaceParams`, `AppCard`, `Calendar`, `CalendarEvent`, `Contact`, `AddressBook`, `MailMessage`, `Meeting`,
`AppDefinition`, `AppSurfaces`, `SurfaceComponent`, `SurfaceProps`, `JsonValue`, `Surface`,
`Theme`, `Platform`, `AppContext`, `AppUser`, `DirectoryUser`, `RpcMethods`, `OlanErrorCode`, `DbRow`, `DbWhere`,
`DbCondition`, `DbOrderBy`, `DbQuery`, `DbCollection`, `DbPatch`, `CreateTaskInput`,
`DeleteRecordInput`, `RemoteRequestInit`, `RemoteResponse`, `RemoteErrorReason`, `FileHandle`,
`FilePickOptions`, `FileUploadResult`, `UploadOptions`, `UploadTask`, `ExternalFlowResult`,
`AppSurfaceParams`, `QueryOptions`, (SDK 1.7) `ProjectStatus`, `ProjectLabel`, `RecordLink`, `RecordTarget`,
`ProjectCalendarItem`, `ProjectApproval`, `TaskActionParams`, `IssueActionParams`, `RecordCardParams`, and (SDK 1.8)
`ProjectField`, `ProjectFieldDefinition`, `ProjectFieldType`, `ProjectFieldValue`, `ProjectFieldValues`. The runtime exports (`startRuntime`,
`workerTransport`, `createMemoryChannel`, `createUiRoot`, tree helpers) are used by the CLI and
the Olan host; apps do not call them. `@olan-app/sdk/server` is for the app's own server
(server.md), `@olan-app/sdk/backend` for backend code Olan runs (`defineBackend`, the server-side
`olan`, `OlanBackendError`; backend.md).

<!-- docs/hooks.md -->
# Hooks

```ts
import { useQuery, useCollection, useRecord, useUser, useUsers, useNavigation, useSurfaceParams, useProjectConfig, useSettings, useTheme, useLocale, usePlatform, useAppContext } from '@olan-app/sdk';
import { useState, useEffect, useMemo, useCallback, useRef } from 'react';   // React hooks work as usual
```

Hooks only work inside components rendered by a surface (they read the running session), and
only in named components (`function Projects() { … }`), following the React hook rules.

## useQuery(fn, deps?, options?)

Runs an async function when the component mounts and again whenever `deps` change (like
`useEffect`). Results of superseded runs are ignored. `options.refetchIntervalMs` refreshes it
regularly (SDK 1.5, below).

```ts
const projects = useQuery(() => olan.projects.list({ limit: 50 }));
const detail = useQuery(() => olan.projects.get(projectId), [projectId]);
```

Returns `QueryState<T>`:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | `T \| undefined` | Last successful result; kept while refetching and after an error |
| `error` | `Error \| undefined` | The rejection (an `OlanError` for `olan.*` failures) |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `true` on the first render and during a refetch |
| `fetching` | `boolean` | `true` while any run is in flight, including the quiet interval refreshes (SDK 1.5) |
| `refetch` | `() => Promise<void>` | Runs it again (e.g. after `updateTask`) |

Typical shape:

```tsx
function Projects() {
  const projects = useQuery(() => olan.projects.list({ limit: 50 }));
  if (projects.error) {
    return (
      <Screen title="Projeler">
        <EmptyState title="Projeler yüklenemedi" description={projects.error.message} action={{ label: 'Tekrar dene', onPress: () => projects.refetch() }} />
      </Screen>
    );
  }
  const items = (projects.data?.items ?? []).map((p) => ({ key: p.id, title: p.name }));
  return (
    <Screen title="Projeler" loading={projects.loading}>
      <List items={items} emptyText="Henüz proje yok" />
    </Screen>
  );
}
```

After a change, update and refetch:

```ts
await olan.projects.updateTask(projectId, task.id, { status: 'completed', revision: task.revision });
await tasks.refetch();
```

### Refreshing on an interval (`refetchIntervalMs`)

```tsx
const posts = useQuery(
  () => olan.remote.request({ method: 'GET', path: '/posts' }),
  [brandId],
  { refetchIntervalMs: hasPending ? 10_000 : undefined },      // poll only while something is publishing
);
```

- At least 5000 ms; smaller values are raised to 5000. `undefined`, `0`, `false` or `null` turns
  it off; changing the value restarts the timer.
- Interval runs are quiet: `loading` stays `false`, `data` stays until the new result, a failure
  goes to `error` (and the old `data` stays). `fetching` is `true` while one runs. A tick while a run
  is still in flight is skipped.
- Olan drives the timer, not the sandbox: there are no ticks while the surface is not visible (a
  hidden browser tab, a closed panel, the app in the background on a phone). When it becomes visible
  and the interval has passed, a tick comes at once, then the timer continues.
- At most 16 timers per sandbox. On an Olan server before 1.5 the SDK falls back to a timer inside
  the sandbox.
- Tests: `app.fireTimers()` sends one tick (testing.md).

## useCollection(name, query?, deps?)

Rows of an `olan.db` collection (database.md), loaded on mount and whenever `name`, `query`
(compared by value) or `deps` change. Needs `db`.

```ts
const list = useCollection<Decision>('decisions', { where: { status }, orderBy: { field: 'title' }, limit: 20 });
```

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `rows` | `DbRow<T>[]` | The first page plus every page `loadMore` added |
| `nextCursor` | `string \| null` | `null` on the last page |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `true` on the first render, while refetching and during `loadMore` |
| `error` | `OlanError \| undefined` | e.g. `permission_denied`, `invalid_params` |
| `refetch` | `() => Promise<void>` | Loads the first page again |
| `loadMore` | `() => Promise<void>` | Appends the next page (no-op on the last page) |

`insert`, `update` and `delete` through `olan.db.collection(name)` anywhere in the app reload every
`useCollection`/`useRecord` of that collection; there are no live updates from other people, so
offer a refresh action (`refetch`).

## useRecord(name, id)

One row: `QueryState<DbRow<T> | null>` (`data` is `null` when the row does not exist or is
hidden). `id` `null` skips the call. Reloads when the row changes through `olan.db` in the app.

```ts
const decision = useRecord<Decision>('decisions', params.id);
```

## useUser()

The person using the app: `{ id }`, the central Olan user id (a UUID). It is the same value as
`row.createdBy`, `task.assigneeId`, `task.createdBy` and `member.userId`, so compare with it to show
actions only where they will work. Needs no permission.

```tsx
const me = useUser();
const mine = row.createdBy === me.id;   // e.g. hide "Sil" on other people's rows of a delete: 'owner' collection
const myTasks = tasks.filter((task) => task.assigneeId === me.id);
```

## useUsers(ids)

Directory entries (`olan.users.get`) for a set of ids: `QueryState<DirectoryUser[]>` plus `byId`
(a `Map`). Reloads when the set changes (order and duplicates do not matter); `[]` makes no call.
Unknown or inaccessible ids are missing from the result. Needs `users:read`.

```tsx
const people = useUsers(rows.map((row) => row.createdBy));
const name = (id: string) => people.byId.get(id)?.displayName ?? '—';
```

## useNavigation()

The visible screen of the surface's navigation stack and the navigation actions (navigation.md).

```ts
const { screen, params, depth, push, pop, replace } = useNavigation();
```

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `screen` | `string` | `'index'` on the first screen |
| `params` | `JsonValue` | Params of the visible screen (first screen: the surface params, or the query of an app address, links.md) |
| `depth` | `number` | Screens on the stack (1 on the first screen) |
| `push(screen, params?)` | `Promise<void>` | Same as `olan.navigation.push` |
| `pop()` | `Promise<void>` | |
| `replace(screen, params?)` | `Promise<void>` | |

## useSurfaceParams<S>()

What the host opened the surface on, typed per surface (surfaces.md):

```ts
const { conversationId, message } = useSurfaceParams<'chat.action'>();
const mail = useSurfaceParams<'mail.sidebar'>();
// { messageId, threadId: string | null, subject, from: { name: string | null, email }, to: same[], cc: same[], receivedAt: ISO date-time }
const returned = useSurfaceParams<'app'>()?.return;   // SDK 1.5: an external flow came back with no pending openExternal (links.md)
```

Exact shapes and which fields may be `null`: surfaces.md. In tests they come from the fixtures
(testing.md, "Surface params in tests").

Panels (`mail.sidebar`, `meeting.panel`) re-render with new params when the person opens another
object; use the params as `useQuery` deps. The type argument is not checked at run time.

## useProjectConfig(projectId?)

SDK 1.6: the app's configuration of a project (`olan.project.config`, api.md). Without `projectId`
it uses the project the surface was opened for (`project.widget`, `project.tab`, `project.settings`; SDK 1.7 also `task.action`, `issue.action`, `record.card`).
A `useQuery` state plus `value` (`{}` until set) and `save(value, { revision? })`, which writes on the
loaded `revision` so a change someone made meanwhile fails with `conflict` (then `refetch()`).

```tsx
const config = useProjectConfig();
const brandId = typeof config.value.brandId === 'string' ? config.value.brandId : null;
await config.save({ ...config.value, brandId: 'b2' });   // config.data.revision + 1 afterwards
if (isOlanError(config.error, 'project_not_enabled')) { /* the app was not added to this project */ }
```

## useSettings()

`Record<string, JsonValue>`: the app's settings (manifest `settings` with defaults applied).
Re-renders when an admin changes them.

```ts
const settings = useSettings();
const threshold = typeof settings.threshold === 'number' ? settings.threshold : 3;
```

## useTheme(), useLocale(), usePlatform()

- `useTheme()` → `'light' | 'dark'` (colours stay with the host; use it only for content choices).
- `useLocale()` → the host UI's BCP 47 locale, e.g. `'tr'` or `'en-US'`. Use it with
  `Intl.DateTimeFormat`/`Intl.NumberFormat` and to pick your strings.
- `usePlatform()` → `'web' | 'desktop' | 'ios' | 'android'`.

## useAppContext()

The whole host context: `{ theme, locale, platform, permissions: string[], settings, development: boolean, user: { id } }`.
`permissions` are the permissions the installation granted; `development` is `true` in Studio and
in tests; `user` is what `useUser()` returns.

```ts
const { permissions } = useAppContext();
const canDelete = permissions.includes('tasks:delete');
```

<!-- docs/navigation.md -->
# Navigation

Each surface has its own navigation stack, kept inside the app. The first screen is named
`'index'` and its params are the surface params. `push` adds a screen, `pop` removes the top one,
`replace` swaps the top one. Olan is told about every change so it can show its own back control;
when the user presses back (or swipes back on iOS, or uses the Android back button), Olan pops the
stack.

The pattern: one surface component reads `useNavigation()` and renders the visible screen.

```tsx
import { List, Screen, defineApp, olan, useNavigation, useQuery } from '@olan-app/sdk';

function ProjectsScreen() {
  const navigation = useNavigation();
  const projects = useQuery(() => olan.projects.list({ limit: 50 }));
  const items = (projects.data?.items ?? []).map((p) => ({ key: p.id, title: p.name }));
  return (
    <Screen title="Projeler" loading={projects.loading}>
      <List items={items} onSelect={({ key }) => navigation.push('project', { projectId: String(key) })} />
    </Screen>
  );
}

function ProjectScreen({ projectId }: { projectId: string }) {
  const detail = useQuery(() => olan.projects.get(projectId), [projectId]);
  const items = (detail.data?.tasks ?? []).map((t) => ({ key: t.id, title: t.title }));
  return (
    <Screen title={detail.data?.project.name ?? 'Proje'} loading={detail.loading}>
      <List items={items} emptyText="Görev yok" />
    </Screen>
  );
}

function App() {
  const { screen, params } = useNavigation();
  const p = (params ?? {}) as { projectId?: string };
  if (screen === 'project' && p.projectId) return <ProjectScreen projectId={p.projectId} />;
  return <ProjectsScreen />;
}

export default defineApp({ app: App });
```

Rules:

- Screen names and params are yours; params must be JSON (strings, numbers, booleans, null,
  arrays, objects).
- Each screen component gets fresh state when it is pushed; screens below keep nothing (they
  re-render from their queries when they become visible again).
- Do not add your own "Geri" (back) button for the stack; Olan shows one. A button that calls
  `pop()` after finishing a task (e.g. after a form submit) is fine.
- `pop()` on the first screen keeps the stack; Olan closes a modal surface, other surfaces stay open.
- `project.widget` surfaces are small cards; keep them to one screen.
- An app address (`https://<Olan web>/apps/a/<appId>/<screen>?id=…`, SDK 1.5, links.md) opens the
  `app` surface on that screen: the stack starts as `[index, <screen>]` with the query as the
  screen's params (`index` alone gets them as its params), and back returns to `index`. So read
  every screen's params defensively: they may come from a link, as strings.

Testing navigation (testing.md):

```ts
const app = await renderApp();
await app.press('Lansman');                 // List item title
app.navigation();                           // [{ action: 'push', screen: 'project', params: { projectId: 'launch' } }]
await app.back();                           // the host's back control
```

<!-- docs/surfaces.md -->
# Surfaces

A surface is a place in Olan where the app appears. Declare each one in `olan-app.json`
`surfaces` and define a component with the same name in `defineApp({ … })`:

```tsx
export default defineApp({ app: Home, 'chat.action': AddToStandup, 'mail.sidebar': CustomerPanel });
```

| Surface | Where | Shown as | `params` (`useSurfaceParams<S>()`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `app` | Olan's app list, sidebar, its address `/apps/a/<appId>` | full screen | `null`, or `{ return }` after an external flow (SDK 1.5, links.md) |
| `project.widget` | Project summary page | card | `{ projectId }` |
| `settings` | Ayarlar → Uygulamalar | full screen | `null` |
| `chat.action` | A message's "More" menu → Apps | modal | `{ conversationId, message: { id, body, senderId, senderKind, createdAt, threadRootId } }` |
| `chat.command` | `/<command>` in the chat composer | modal | `{ conversationId, text, threadRootId? }` (`text`: what follows the command) |
| `chat.card` | The `open` button of the app's chat card (cards.md) | modal | `{ conversationId, messageId, payload }` |
| `mail.sidebar` | A tab next to the contact panel of an open email | panel | `{ messageId, threadId, subject, from: { name, email }, to, cc, receivedAt }` |
| `mail.action` | The email toolbar's overflow menu → Apps | modal | same as `mail.sidebar` |
| `calendar.event.action` | The event popover → Apps | modal | `{ calendarId, eventId, uid, title, start, end, timeZone, isAllDay, location?, isOrganizer }` |
| `meeting.panel` | A tab in the meeting room's side panel (not for guests) | panel | `{ meetingId, slug, title, startsAt, endsAt, role: 'organizer' \| 'participant', projectId? }` |
| `project.tab` | A tab of the project page (SDK 1.6) | tab | `{ projectId }` |
| `project.settings` | The project page → Uygulamalar → the app's "Ayarlar" (SDK 1.6) | full screen (a sheet) | `{ projectId }` |
| `task.action` | A task's "…" menu → the app (SDK 1.7) | modal | `{ projectId, task: { id, key, title, status, statusId, statusCategory, assigneeId, due } }` |
| `issue.action` | An issue's "…" menu → the app (SDK 1.7) | modal | `{ projectId, issue: { id, key, number, title, kind, state, stateReason, inTriage } }` |
| `record.card` | The `open` button of the card the app drew on a task or issue (SDK 1.7) | modal | `{ projectId, linkId, target: { kind, id }, externalId, payload }` |

Manifest entries: `app`, `project.widget`, `settings`, `project.tab` and `project.settings` take
`{ "title"?: string }` (the tab label and the settings title fall back to the app name); every other
surface needs `"title"` (1–80, the menu or tab label). `chat.command` also needs `"command"`
(`^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, typed after `/`) and may have `"description"` (≤ 120):

```json
"surfaces": {
  "chat.action": { "title": "Standup'a ekle" },
  "chat.command": { "title": "Standup", "command": "standup", "description": "Bugünün standup'ını aç" },
  "mail.sidebar": { "title": "Müşteri" }
}
```

## Reading the params

```tsx
import { useSurfaceParams, useQuery, olan, Screen, Text } from '@olan-app/sdk';

function CustomerPanel() {
  const mail = useSurfaceParams<'mail.sidebar'>();          // typed per surface
  const contacts = useQuery(() => olan.contacts.search(mail.from.email), [mail.from.email]);
  return <Screen title={mail.subject}><Text text={`${contacts.data?.length ?? 0} kişi`} /></Screen>;
}
```

Exact shapes (types `SurfaceParams`, `MailSurfaceParams` … from `@olan-app/sdk`): keys without
`?` are always present; `?` keys may be absent or `null`. Tests build them from fixtures (testing.md):

```ts
type MailAddress = { name: string | null; email: string };   // name null when the header has none
interface MailSurfaceParams {        // mail.sidebar, mail.action (no body: olan.mail.getMessage)
  messageId: string; threadId: string | null; subject: string;   // '' when there is no subject
  from: MailAddress;                 // the first From address; email '' if the message has none
  to: MailAddress[]; cc: MailAddress[];   // [] when empty (no bcc)
  receivedAt: string;                // ISO 8601 date-time, e.g. '2026-10-16T09:00:00Z'
}
// chat.action: message.body/senderId/threadRootId are string | null; createdAt ISO date-time
// calendar.event.action: start/end ISO date (all-day) or date-time; timeZone/location string | null
// meeting.panel: endsAt/projectId string | null; chat.card: payload is the card action's JsonValue or null
// task.action: task.key ('WEB-12'), statusId, statusCategory, assigneeId, due string | null; status is the CalDAV value
// issue.action: issue.key ('WEB-#4'), kind, stateReason string | null; state 'open' | 'closed'
// record.card: target.kind 'task' | 'issue'; payload is the open action's JsonValue or null
```

Compare email addresses case-insensitively (`from.email.toLowerCase()`).

- The summary fields in `params` need no permission: the person opened the app on that object.
  More than that needs the read permission: the email body (`olan.mail.getMessage`, `mail:read`),
  other messages (`chat:read`), participants (`meetings:read`).
- Panels (`mail.sidebar`, `meeting.panel`) stay open while the person moves to another email or
