  meeting; the component re-renders with the new params (no new start). Key queries on the params.
- Root component: `app`, `settings`, `project.tab` and `project.settings` start with `<Screen>`
  (`validate --strict` warns `ui.root_not_screen` otherwise); `project.widget` renders a `<Card>` (or `EmptyState`). Modals and
  panels should also start with `<Screen>`: its `title`/`actions` become the modal's or panel's
  header (not checked; another root is shown as is, without a header).
- Modals: the surface's first `Screen` is shown in a modal; `olan.navigation.pop()` (or the host's
  close control) on the first screen closes it. One modal per app at a time.
- The `params` prop of the surface component carries the same value (`JsonValue`).

## Project extensions (SDK 1.6)

A project is generic: statuses, labels, work packages. An app turns it into the project of a
process (a marketing calendar, a sales pipeline) only where a member adds it: the project page →
Uygulamalar lists the apps installed in the organization, and "Ekle" / "Kaldır" enables or removes
one there (it also shows in the project's activity). Only then:

- `project.widget` shows in the project's summary, `project.tab` adds a tab with the surface's
  `title` (or the app name), and `project.settings` opens from the app's "Ayarlar" button in
  Uygulamalar. All three get `{ projectId }`.
- `olan.projects.*` on the person's behalf reaches the project (`project_not_enabled` elsewhere).
- `olan.project.config` keeps the app's settings of that project (api.md#olanprojectconfig).

```tsx
function BrandTab() {
  const { projectId } = useSurfaceParams<'project.tab'>();
  const config = useProjectConfig();                       // this project's configuration
  const brandId = typeof config.value.brandId === 'string' ? config.value.brandId : null;
  return <Screen title="Marka">{brandId ? <BrandCalendar brandId={brandId} /> : <EmptyState title="Marka seçilmedi" />}</Screen>;
}
```

`project.tab` fills the tab's content area and keeps its own screen stack
(`olan.navigation.push` works; the back control appears in the tab). `project.settings` opens in a
sheet; `olan.navigation.pop()` on its first screen closes it. Removing the app from the project
hides its surfaces there; its configuration and the records it linked stay.

## Records on tasks and issues (SDK 1.7)

In the projects it is enabled in, an app also adds its own records and process (api.md#olanproject-records-statuses-calendar-feed-approvals):

- `task.action` / `issue.action` put the app in a task's or issue's "…" menu (the entry is the
  surface's `title`); the modal gets the task or issue. A typical action links one of the app's
  records to it: `olan.project.links.upsert` with a card the task or issue then shows.
- `record.card` opens from an `open` button of that card, with the link, its target, the record's
  `externalId` and the button's `payload`. Record cards have no `submit` buttons.
- The app's statuses (`olan.project.statuses.define`), labels and (SDK 1.8) custom fields
  (`olan.project.fields.define`, values with `setValues`) show among the project's; the task
  moves through a link (`olan.project.links.setStatus`). Its calendar items show as a layer of the
  project calendar, its feed lines and the status changes it made under its name in the project
  activity, its approval requests in the approvers' approval box.
- Manifest `projectTemplates` offers whole projects (work packages, statuses, labels, starter tasks)
  in "Yeni proje"; a project made from one has the app added (manifest.md#projecttemplates).

```tsx
function LinkRecord() {
  const { projectId, task } = useSurfaceParams<'task.action'>();
  const link = async () => {
    const created = await olan.project.links.upsert(projectId, { target: { kind: 'task', id: task.id }, externalId: 'SAT-12', card });
    await olan.project.links.setStatus(projectId, created.id, { statusKey: 'awaiting-approval' });
  };
  return <Screen title="Kayda bağla" subtitle={task.title}><Button label="Bağla" onPress={link} /></Screen>;
}
```

`olan-app init --template project-records` builds all of it with tests. Removing the app from the
project hides these surfaces; links and approvals stay read-only, calendar items hide.

## Visibility

An entry is shown when the installation is active, the person consented (the consent screen
opens on first use) and policy does not block it. Each place lists at most 8 apps, the rest go
under "Tüm uygulamalar". Two apps with the same `command` are both listed with their names.
Surfaces need no permission of their own; the consent screen lists them under "Görüneceği yerler".

<!-- docs/cards.md -->
# Chat cards

An app posts a static card into a chat as itself (name and icon of the app). A card is the UI tree
format without handlers, so it renders on web, desktop and mobile without running the app:

```ts
import type { AppCard } from '@olan-app/sdk';

const card: AppCard = {
  version: 1,
  root: 1,
  fallbackText: 'Standup: 3 görev açık',          // 1–500: notifications, search, previews
  nodes: [
    { id: 1, type: 'Card', props: { title: 'Standup', subtitle: '17 Ekim' }, children: [2, 4, 5] },
    { id: 2, type: 'Text', props: {}, children: [3] },
    { id: 3, type: '#text', props: { text: '3 görev açık' }, children: [] },
    { id: 4, type: 'Button', props: { label: 'Aç', action: { kind: 'open', payload: { day: '2026-10-17' } } }, children: [] },
    { id: 5, type: 'Button', props: { label: 'Bitti', variant: 'primary', action: { kind: 'submit', name: 'done' } }, children: [] },
  ],
};
const { messageId } = await olan.chat.postCard({ conversationId, card });   // chat:write
await olan.chat.updateCard(messageId, { ...card, fallbackText: 'Standup bitti' });
```

- Components: `Card`, `Stack`, `Text` (with `#text` children or `text`), `Badge`, `Table`,
  `Button`, `EmptyState`; props as in components.md. No inputs and no handlers (`$handler`,
  `onPress`, `Card.actions`, `EmptyState.action`, `Table.onSelectRow`).
- `Button` has `action` instead of `onPress`:
  - `{ kind: 'open', payload? }` opens the app's `chat.card` surface with
    `{ conversationId, messageId, payload }` (declare `chat.card` in `surfaces`).
  - `{ kind: 'submit', name, payload? }` calls the app's server (`POST {remote.url}/card-actions`,
    server.md); it needs `remote`. The answer may replace the card and show a toast.
- Limits: JSON ≤ 16 KiB, ≤ 100 nodes, depth ≤ 8, each `payload` ≤ 2 KiB. Invalid cards fail with
  `validation_failed`; the message lists `card.*` / `tree.*` codes (errors.md#cards).
- Where: a conversation the person is in (from a chat surface: `useSurfaceParams().conversationId`).
  From the app's server with the app identity: only conversations the app was added to (server.md).
- `updateCard` changes only cards this installation posted. Apps never receive events for their own
  cards. Cards do not trigger push notifications; they count as unread.
- Rate limits: 60 cards per minute per installation, 10 per conversation.

Record cards (SDK 1.7): the same format is the card an app draws on a task or issue
(`olan.project.links.upsert`, api.md) and attaches to an approval request. Its buttons may only
`{ kind: 'open', payload? }`, which opens the app's `record.card` surface with
`{ projectId, linkId, target, externalId, payload }`; `validateRecordCard(card)` checks it.

`validateCard(card, { remote })` from `@olan-app/schema` runs the same checks; `olan-app test`
validates every `postCard` like the server (`app.host.cards` lists what the app posted).

<!-- docs/database.md -->
# App database (`olan.db`)

Each app can have its own database on the Olan server: collections of JSON rows with declared
fields, indexed queries, cursors and per-row revisions. Declare the collections in the manifest's
`data` and request the `db` permission. Needs `@olan-app/sdk` ^1.1.0 (`"sdk": "^1.1.0"`).

`olan.db` is for the app's records (decisions, checklists, pins). For a few per-user preferences
keep using `olan.storage` (api.md); for Olan's own records (tasks) use `olan.projects`.

## Declaring collections

```jsonc
// olan-app.json
"permissions": ["db"],
"data": {
  "version": 1,                                  // integer; increase it whenever the schema changes
  "collections": {
    "decisions": {
      "scope": "organization",                   // shared in the organization (with rules)
      "fields": {
        "title":     { "type": "string", "required": true, "maxLength": 200, "indexed": true },
        "status":    { "type": "string", "enum": ["open", "done"], "indexed": true },
        "projectId": { "type": "ref:project", "indexed": true },
        "taskId":    { "type": "ref:task" },
        "decidedOn": { "type": "date", "indexed": true },
        "score":     { "type": "number", "integer": true, "min": 0, "max": 10 },
        "meta":      { "type": "json" }
      },
      "rules": { "read": "any", "update": "any", "delete": "owner" }
    },
    "pins": { "scope": "user", "fields": { "decisionId": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 64, "indexed": true } } }
  }
}
```

| `type` | Value | Options | Indexable |
|---|---|---|---|
| `string` | string | `maxLength` (default 1000, ≤ 10000), `enum` (≤ 100 values, each ≤ 100 characters) | yes, when `maxLength` ≤ 512 or it has `enum` |
| `number` | finite number | `integer`, `min`, `max` | yes |
| `boolean` | `true` / `false` | – | yes (`eq`/`in` only) |
| `date` | `"YYYY-MM-DD"` (a real calendar day) | – | yes |
| `datetime` | ISO date-time **with offset** (`Z` or `+03:00`); stored as UTC `toISOString()` | – | yes |
| `json` | any JSON, ≤ 16 KiB serialised | – | no |
| `ref:project`, `ref:task`, `ref:user` | UUID string (stored lower-case) | – | yes (`eq`/`in` only) |

Every field also takes `required` (default `false`), `indexed` (default `false`) and `label`
(≤ 80, shown in Studio and exports). A field that is not `required` may be missing or `null`
(both mean "no value"; `null` is not stored). Refs only check the UUID format; Olan does not
check that the project/task/user exists, and does not clean up when it is deleted.

Limits: ≤ 20 collections; ≤ 64 fields and ≤ 5 indexed fields per collection; collection names
`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$`; field names `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}$`; `id`, `createdAt`,
`updatedAt`, `createdBy`, `revision` are reserved; a row's data ≤ 64 KiB as JSON. There are no
composite or unique indexes. `createdAt`, `updatedAt` and `createdBy` are always indexed.

### Scope and rules

- `"scope": "user"`: each person sees only the rows they created. No `rules`.
- `"scope": "organization"`: rows are shared by everyone who uses the installation, subject to
  `rules` — `read`, `update`, `delete`, each `"any"` or `"owner"` (the row's creator). Default
  `{ "read": "any", "update": "any", "delete": "owner" }`. In a personal installation (installed
  by one user for themselves) an organization collection belongs to that user.
- A row the rules hide does not appear in `get`/`query`/`count`; changing or deleting it fails
  with `forbidden_record`. Admins see every row only through export and the admin data browser,
  never inside the app.

### Changing the schema

Increase `data.version` with every change. When a new version is installed, Olan compares it
with the stored schema:

- Applied automatically: new collections, new optional fields, adding or removing `indexed`,
  a larger `maxLength`/`max`, a smaller `min`, new `enum` values, `required: true → false`,
  `rules`, `label`.
- Refused until migrations arrive (Phase 3): removing a collection (`data.collection_removed`)
  or field (`data.field_removed`), changing a type (`data.type_changed`) or scope
  (`data.scope_changed`), adding a required field or making one required
  (`data.required_added`), narrowing a constraint (`data.constraint_tightened`).
- A changed schema with the same `version` is `data.version_not_bumped`; a lower one
  `data.version_downgrade`.

When the app is removed, its data is kept for 30 days and comes back if it is installed again
(with a compatible schema); admins can export it (NDJSON) or delete it earlier.

## API

```ts
import { olan, isOlanError, type DbRow } from '@olan-app/sdk';

type Decision = { title: string; status?: 'open' | 'done'; projectId?: string; score?: number };
const decisions = olan.db.collection<Decision>('decisions');

const row = await decisions.insert({ title: 'Ship 1.1', status: 'open' });
// row: { id, data: { title, status }, revision: 1, createdAt, updatedAt, createdBy }
const same = await decisions.get(row.id);                        // DbRow<Decision> | null
const { rows, nextCursor } = await decisions.query({
  where: { status: 'open', decidedOn: { gte: '2026-01-01' } },
  orderBy: { field: 'decidedOn', direction: 'desc' },
  limit: 20,
});
const changed = await decisions.update(row.id, { status: 'done', score: null }, { revision: row.revision });
await decisions.delete(row.id, { revision: changed.revision });  // revision optional
const open = await decisions.count({ status: 'open' });
```

| Call | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `collection<T>(name)` | `DbCollection<T>` | `name` from `data.collections`; unknown → `invalid_params` |
| `insert(data)` | `DbRow<T>` | `data` is the whole row (validated) |
| `get(id)` | `DbRow<T> \| null` | `null` when missing or hidden by rules |
| `query({ where?, orderBy?, limit?, cursor? })` | `{ rows: DbRow<T>[]; nextCursor: string \| null }` | see below |
| `update(id, patch, { revision })` | `DbRow<T>` | shallow merge; `null` clears a field; `revision` must be current |
| `delete(id, { revision? })` | `void` | with `revision`, only if unchanged |
| `count(where?)` | `number` | same `where` as `query` |

```ts
interface DbRow<T> { id: string; data: T; revision: number; createdAt: string; updatedAt: string; createdBy: string }
type DbScalar = string | number | boolean | null;
type DbCondition = DbScalar | { eq?: DbScalar; in?: DbScalar[]; gt?: DbScalar; gte?: DbScalar; lt?: DbScalar; lte?: DbScalar };
type DbWhere = Record<string, DbCondition>;               // fields are combined with AND
interface DbOrderBy { field: string; direction?: 'asc' | 'desc' }
interface DbQuery { where?: DbWhere; orderBy?: DbOrderBy; limit?: number; cursor?: string }
```

### Queries

- `where` only on indexed fields and `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `createdBy`; at most 5 fields.
  A plain value means `eq`; `{ field: null }` finds rows without a value; `in` takes ≤ 50 values
  (`null` allowed); `gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte` may be combined on one field for a range. `boolean`,
  `ref:*` and `createdBy` allow only `eq`/`in`. Values must match the field type (dates as
  `YYYY-MM-DD`, date-times with an offset). Anything else is `invalid_params`.
- `orderBy`: one indexed field, `createdAt` or `updatedAt`; `direction` defaults to `'asc'`.
  Without `orderBy` rows come newest first (`{ field: 'createdAt', direction: 'desc' }`). Ties are
  broken by `id`; rows without a value come last in both directions. Strings sort by Unicode
  code point (`'B' < 'a'`), not alphabetically for a language.
- `limit` 1–100, default 50. `nextCursor` is `null` on the last page; pass it as `cursor` with the
  **same** `where` and `orderBy` (a different query → `invalid_params`). Cursors are opaque.
- No full-text search, joins or aggregates; filter on indexed fields and finish in JavaScript.

## Hooks

`useCollection(name, query?, deps?)` → `{ rows, nextCursor, loading, error, refetch, loadMore }` and
`useRecord(name, id | null)` → `{ data, error, loading, refetch }` (hooks.md). Mutations through
`olan.db.collection(name)` in the app reload the hooks reading that collection; there are no live
subscriptions, so other people's changes appear after `refetch`.

## Errors

| Code | When | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `validation_failed` | The row does not match the schema. `message` names the first problem: `"data.title: row.required"` (`row.unknown_field`, `row.required`, `row.type`, `row.max_length`, `row.range`, `row.enum`, `row.not_integer`, `row.json_too_large`, `row.too_large`) | Fix the form values; show the field |
| `conflict` | `update`/`delete` with an old `revision` (someone changed the row) | `get` the row again, re-apply the change, retry |
| `not_found` | `update`/`delete` of a row that does not exist (or belongs to another user in a `user` collection) | Refetch the list |
| `forbidden_record` | The collection's `rules` do not allow this user to change/delete the row | Catch it and explain ("only the person who added it can delete it"); see below |
| `quota_exceeded` | The installation's row or size limit is reached (default 100 000 rows, 100 MiB) | Tell the user to contact an admin; delete old rows |
| `invalid_params` | Unknown collection, non-indexed `where`/`orderBy` field, bad `limit` or cursor | Fix the call |
| `permission_denied` | `db` is not granted | Add `"db"` to `permissions` |

```ts
async function markDone(row: DbRow<Decision>) {
  try {
    return await decisions.update(row.id, { status: 'done' }, { revision: row.revision });
  } catch (error) {
    if (!isOlanError(error, 'conflict')) throw error;
    const fresh = await decisions.get(row.id);          // someone else changed it: retry once
    return fresh && decisions.update(fresh.id, { status: 'done' }, { revision: fresh.revision });
  }
}
```

`createdBy` is the central Olan user id, the same as `useUser().id` (hooks.md). With `owner`
rules, show the action only on the user's own rows, and still handle the refusal (the row or the
rules may change in between):

```tsx
const me = useUser();
const canDelete = row.createdBy === me.id;   // rules.delete: 'owner'

async function remove(row: DbRow<Decision>) {
  try {
    await decisions.delete(row.id, { revision: row.revision });
  } catch (error) {
    if (!isOlanError(error, 'forbidden_record')) throw error;
    await olan.ui.toast({ text: 'Bu kararı yalnızca ekleyen kişi silebilir', tone: 'warning' });
  }
}
```

If everyone should be able to do it, use `"any"` for that rule instead; for "my rows only", use
a `"scope": "user"` collection.

## Testing

`olan-app test` and `validate --strict` run the app against an in-memory database with the same
rules and error codes (`@olan-app/sdk/memory-db`). Seed it with `fixtures/db.json`:

```json
{ "decisions": [{ "id": "d1", "data": { "title": "İlk karar", "status": "open" } }] }
```

Missing `id`, `createdBy` (the default user `00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001`), timestamps
and `revision` (1) are filled in; another `"createdBy"` makes a row someone else wrote. Row ids may
be any unique string. Rows must match the schema, and `ref:*` values must be UUIDs, while the
mock's built-in project and task ids are not (`p0`, `p0-t0`): an app that stores project/task ids
needs `fixtures/projects.json` with UUID ids (testing.md, "Fixtures").

<!-- docs/permissions.md -->
# Permissions

Declare every permission the app uses in `olan-app.json`:

```json
"permissions": ["projects:read", "tasks:write", "db", "http:api.example.com"]
```

Olan shows them when someone installs the app, grouped as Okuma (read), Yazma (write), **Silme**
(delete — its own heading with a warning and each permission's description), Uygulama verisi
(app data), Ağ (network) and Ayarlar (settings). Delete permissions start unticked: the admin
grants them explicitly. Olan checks every `olan.*` call against the permissions the installation
granted. Declare only what the app calls.

| Permission | Group | Shown to the user | Allows |
|---|---|---|---|
| `projects:read` | read | Projelerinizi ve görevlerinizi okuyabilir | `olan.projects.list`, `get`, `tasks`; SDK 1.7 the `list` calls of `olan.project.statuses`, `labels`, `links`, `calendar`, `approvals`; SDK 1.8 `olan.project.fields.list`, `values`; `project.task.*`, `project.issue.*`, `project.approval.decided` events |
| `users:read` | read | Kuruluşunuzdaki kişilerin adını, e-postasını ve dizin bilgilerini görebilir | `olan.users.get`, `useUsers` (name, email, title, department, team); a permission of its own, no other one needed |
| `chat:read` | read | Sohbetleri okuyabilir | `olan.chat.conversations`, `messages` |
| `tasks:write` | write | Erişebildiğiniz projelerde görev oluşturabilir ve görevleri değiştirebilir | `olan.projects.createTask`, `updateTask` (reading still needs `projects:read`); SDK 1.7 `olan.project.links.upsert`, `remove`, `setStatus`; SDK 1.8 `olan.project.fields.setValues` |
| `projects:write` | write | Proje görevlerini değiştirebilir | `olan.projects.updateTask` only. Older permission: new apps use `tasks:write` |
| `tasks:delete` | delete | Erişebildiğiniz projelerdeki görevleri silebilir; her silme denetim kaydına yazılır | `olan.projects.deleteTask` |
| `projects:delete` | delete | Erişebildiğiniz projelerde boş iş paketlerini kaldırabilir (arşivler). Proje ve varsayılan iş paketi kaldırılamaz | `olan.projects.deleteList` |
| `storage` | data | Kendi verisini saklayabilir | `olan.storage.*`: small key–value data per installation and user (≤ 64 KiB per value, ≤ 1000 keys), for preferences and cache, not records |
| `db` | data | Kendi veritabanında kayıt oluşturabilir, okuyabilir, değiştirebilir ve silebilir; veriler bu Olan sunucusunda kalır | `olan.db.*` on the collections in the manifest's `data` (database.md) |
| `http:<host>` | network | `<host>` adresine istek atabilir | `olan.http.fetch` to that host |
| `settings:read` | settings | Organizasyon ayarlarını okuyabilir | nothing yet (reserved) |
| `chat:write` | write | Eklendiği ve sizin bulunduğunuz sohbetlere uygulama adına kart gönderebilir | `olan.chat.postCard`, `updateCard` (cards.md) |
| `calendar:read` | read | Takvimlerinizi ve etkinliklerinizi görebilir | `olan.calendar.calendars`, `events`; `calendar.event.*` events |
| `calendar:write` | write | Takvimlerinizde etkinlik oluşturabilir ve değiştirebilir; davet göndermez | `olan.calendar.createEvent`, `updateEvent` |
| `calendar:delete` | delete | Etkinlikleri silebilir; takvimler, varsayılan takvim ve Olan toplantıları silinemez; her silme denetim kaydına yazılır | `olan.calendar.deleteEvent` |
| `contacts:read` | read | Adres defterlerinizi ve kişilerinizi görebilir | `olan.contacts.addressBooks`, `search` |
| `contacts:write` | write | Kişi kartı oluşturabilir ve değiştirebilir | `olan.contacts.create`, `update` |
| `contacts:delete` | delete | Kendi adres defterlerinizdeki kişileri silebilir; adres defterleri silinemez | `olan.contacts.delete` |
| `mail:read` | read | Uygulamayı açtığınız e-postanın içeriğini görebilir; diğer e-postalarınıza erişemez | `olan.mail.getMessage` for the open email only |
| `meetings:read` | read | Görebildiğiniz toplantıların başlığını, saatini ve katılımcılarını görebilir | `olan.meetings.get`; `meeting.*` events |
| `projects:create` | write | Proje oluşturabilir; her proje kendi sohbetini, takvimini ve iş paketini açar | `olan.projects.create` |
| `projects:archive` | delete | Yalnız bu uygulamanın oluşturduğu projeleri kaldırabilir (arşivler) | `olan.projects.archive` |
| `projects:extend` | write | Eklendiği projelerde durum ve etiket tanımlayabilir, takvime katman, etkinlik akışına satır ve onay isteği ekleyebilir | SDK 1.7: `olan.project.statuses.define`, `remove`, `labels.define`, `remove`, `calendar.upsert`, `remove`, `activity.post`, `approvals.request`, `cancel`; SDK 1.8 `fields.define`, `remove` (api.md#olanproject-records-statuses-calendar-feed-approvals); only in projects the app was added to |
| `profile:read` | read | Profilinizi görme: uygulamanın sunucusu adınızı, e-posta adresinizi ve kurumdaki rolünüzü görür | SDK 1.5: adds `user.email`, `user.displayName` and `user.role` (`admin` \| `member`) to the `olan.remote.request` envelopes (remote-requests.md). Nothing in the sandbox changes (`useUser()` stays `{ id }`). Needs `remote` in the manifest (`manifest.profile_requires_remote`) |
| `files:pick` | data | Dosya seçtirme: seçtiğiniz dosyaları okuyabilir ve sizin onayınızla yükleyebilir; başka dosyalarınıza erişemez | SDK 1.5: `olan.files.pick`, `upload`, `cancel` (files.md); uploads go only to the `remote.url` origin or an `http:<host>` host |

Two more are **implied** by the manifest and never listed in `permissions` (`manifest.permission_unknown`):
`remote` (network: "Veriler `<host>` adresindeki uygulama sunucusuna gönderilebilir") when it
declares `remote` (it also covers `olan.remote.request` when `remote.requests` is `true`; there is
no separate permission for requests), and `ai:tools` (network: "Olan asistanı bu uygulamanın araçlarını sizin adınıza
çağırabilir; araç girdileri `<host>`'a gönderilir") when it declares `ai.tools`. Consent screens show
them with the server's host; admins can block them like any permission. Surfaces need no
permission; the consent screen lists them under "Görüneceği yerler".

`db` covers the app's own rows only; deleting them does not need a delete permission. Deleting
Olan records always does, and protected records (projects, the default work package, task
statuses and fields, chats, calendars, address books, Olan meetings, members, accounts) cannot be deleted by any app; such
calls fail with `forbidden_record` and are written to the audit log. An admin can also restrict
an app to deleting only the records it created.

No permission is needed for `olan.settings.get` (the app's own settings), `olan.ui.*` (including
`openUrl` and `openExternal`), `Image` and `Avatar` pictures (the host checks their origin instead),
`olan.navigation.*`, `useTheme`, `useLocale`, `usePlatform`, `useSettings`, `useNavigation`, and
`useUser()` (the current user's id; their name needs `users:read`).

## Reserved permissions

Ids fixed for a later phase fail with `manifest.permission_reserved` (the hint names the phase).
None are reserved today. Deleting projects (as opposed to archiving the app's own), creating work
packages, calendars or address books and sending chat messages are not app permissions.
`projects:delete` keeps its meaning (empty work packages); removing projects is `projects:archive`.

Permissions come in families: `<resource>:read`, `<resource>:write` (create and change) and
`<resource>:delete`. Deleting is always its own permission and is shown separately at install.

## `http:<host>`

- Grammar: `http:` + a DNS host name or IPv4 address + an optional `:port` (1–65535). No scheme,
  path, wildcard (`*.example.com`), user info or IPv6. Hosts are lower-cased
  (`http:API.Example.com` → `http:api.example.com`).
- A permission without a port matches only the scheme's default port: `http:api.example.com`
  allows `https://api.example.com/...` (443) and `http://api.example.com/...` (80), not
  `https://api.example.com:8443/`. A permission with a port matches only that port.
- One permission per host: `api.example.com` does not cover `www.example.com`.
- Only `http` and `https` URLs; URLs with credentials (`https://user:pw@…`) are refused.
- Olan's server additionally refuses private and loopback addresses (`localhost`, `10.x`, …).

## What happens when one is missing

- At run time the call rejects with `OlanError` code `permission_denied` (or `http_blocked` for a
  host that is not allowed). Show an `EmptyState` with the message rather than crashing.
- `olan-app validate --strict` renders every surface with the manifest's permissions and reports
  `permission.missing` / `permission.http_missing` with the permission to add.
- In tests, `renderApp({ permissions: [] })` checks how the app behaves without them.

Admins can block permissions for the whole organization (e.g. every `http:` host); a blocked
permission behaves like a missing one.

<!-- docs/manifest.md -->
# Manifest (`olan-app.json`)

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://olan.app/schemas/olan-app/v1.json",
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "id": "com.example.overdue-tasks",
  "name": "Geciken görevler",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "sdk": "^1.8.0",
  "minServerVersion": "0.1.0",
  "description": "Projelerdeki geciken görevler",
  "entry": "dist/app.js",
  "icon": "assets/icon.png",
  "surfaces": {
    "app": { "title": "Geciken görevler" },
    "project.widget": { "title": "Gecikenler" },
    "settings": { "title": "Ayarlar" }
  },
  "permissions": ["projects:read"],
  "settings": {
    "threshold": { "type": "number", "label": "Gecikme eşiği (gün)", "default": 3 }
  }
}
```

Unknown top-level fields are errors (`manifest.unknown_field`); only `$schema` is extra. The
allowed fields depend on `schemaVersion` (only `1` today).

`server` declares backend code that Olan runs (`server/index.ts` with `@olan-app/sdk/backend`;
backend.md). A server whose administrator turned backends off (`OLAN_APPS_BACKEND=0`) rejects it
with `manifest.feature_not_available`.

| Field | Required | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `$schema` | no | `"https://olan.app/schemas/olan-app/v1.json"` (editor completion) |
| `schemaVersion` | yes | `1` |
| `id` | yes | Reverse domain, lowercase: `[a-z0-9-]+(\.[a-z0-9-]+)+`, ≤ 128. Never change it after publishing |
| `name` | yes | 1–80 characters |
| `version` | yes | Semver `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` (pre-release allowed). Raise it for every new release; an organization catalog (`publish --org`) never takes the same number twice. On the marketplace a `checks_failed`, rejected or withdrawn version number may be submitted again; approved or released ones may not (marketplace.md#publishing) |
| `sdk` | yes | `@olan-app/sdk` range: `"*"`, `"1.2.3"`, `"^1.0.0"`, `"~1.2.0"` or `">=1.0.0 <2.0.0"` (no `\|\|`, no `1.x`). Use `"^1.8.0"` (the current SDK; `olan-app init` writes it; `data` needs ^1.1.0, `useUser`/`olan.users` ^1.2.0, the Phase 3 surfaces, cards, calendar/contacts/mail/meetings calls and `remote` ^1.3.0, backend code (`server`) ^1.4.0, `remote.requests`, `olan.files`, `openUrl`/`openExternal`, `refetchIntervalMs`, the components `Tabs` … `ProgressBar` and `ai.tools` `timeoutMs` ^1.5.0, `project.tab`, `project.settings`, `olan.project.config` and `useProjectConfig` ^1.6.0, `task.action`, `issue.action`, `record.card`, the `olan.project` links/statuses/labels/calendar/activity/approvals calls, `projects:extend` and `projectTemplates` ^1.7.0, `olan.project.fields` ^1.8.0) |
| `minServerVersion` | no | Oldest Olan server that may install it (semver). Use `"0.1.0"`, the first Olan server with Olan Apps (`olan-app init` writes it); raise it only when the app needs a newer server. Olan's own version is still 0.x, so `"1.0.0"` would block every server today |
| `description` | no | ≤ 400 characters |
| `entry` | yes (apps) | Bundle path in the package: `"dist/app.js"` (relative `.js`/`.mjs`, no `..`) |
| `icon` | no | Package path to a png/svg/jpg/webp, e.g. `"assets/icon.png"` (the file must exist) |
| `kind` | no | `"app"` (default) or `"web-link"` |
| `surfaces` | yes (apps) | At least one surface (below, surfaces.md) |
| `permissions` | no | Default `[]`; ≤ 64; no duplicates (permissions.md) |
| `settings` | no | Settings fields (below) |
| `data` | no | App database collections (below, database.md). Apps only, not web links. Needs `"sdk": "^1.1.0"` and the `db` permission |
| `remote` | no | `{ "url", "jwksUrl", "requests"? }` of the app's own server (server.md); implies the `remote` permission. `"requests": true` (default `false`, SDK 1.5) turns on `olan.remote.request`: Olan posts signed requests to `{url}/requests` on behalf of the person (remote-requests.md). `profile:read` needs `remote` (`manifest.profile_requires_remote`) |
| `events` | no | Event types sent to `{remote.url}/events` (server.md#events); needs `remote` and each event's permission |
| `ai` | no | `{ "tools": [ … ] }`: assistant tools run by the app server (server.md#assistant-tools-aitools); needs `remote`, implies `ai:tools`. A tool's `timeoutMs` (1000–60000, default 15000; read-only tools at most 15000, SDK 1.5) sets how long Olan waits for it |
| `projectTemplates` | no | Project templates offered in "Yeni proje" while the app is installed (SDK 1.7, below) |
| `server` | no | Backend code Olan runs (backend.md): `{ "entry": "server/index.ts", "schedules"?: [{ name, cron, timeZone?, function? }] (≤ 10, ≥ 5 min apart), "events"?: { "<event type>": "<function>" }, "hooks"?: [{ name, function?, verify: { kind: "hmac-sha256"\|"standard-webhooks"\|"none", header?, secretSetting? } }] }`; `olan-app build` bundles `entry` into `dist/server.js`. Handlers go in `defineBackend`'s `schedules`/`events`/`hooks` maps by name; `function` (optional; required as the `events` value) only names a fallback in `functions`, and such a function is not callable from the UI (backend.md#handler-resolution) |

## Data (`olan.db`)

`data` declares the app's database collections (since SDK 1.1.0, still `schemaVersion: 1`):

```json
"data": {
  "version": 1,
  "collections": {
    "decisions": {
      "scope": "organization",
      "fields": {
        "title": { "type": "string", "required": true, "maxLength": 200, "indexed": true },
        "status": { "type": "string", "enum": ["open", "done"], "indexed": true },
        "projectId": { "type": "ref:project", "indexed": true }
      },
      "rules": { "read": "any", "update": "any", "delete": "owner" }
    }
  }
}
```

Field types, options, limits, scopes, rules and schema changes: database.md. Errors:
`manifest.data_*` (errors.md).

## Surfaces

| Surface | Where it appears | Params | Root component |
|---|---|---|---|
| `app` | Full screen: Olan's app list (`/apps/<installation>`), sidebar, the permanent address `/apps/a/<appId>` (links.md) | `null`, or `{ return }` (links.md) | `Screen` (required: `ui.root_not_screen`) |
| `project.widget` | A card on the summary page of the projects the app is enabled in | `{ projectId: string }` | `Card` (or `EmptyState`) |
| `project.tab` | A tab of the project page, in projects the app is enabled in (SDK 1.6) | `{ projectId: string }` | `Screen` (required) |
| `project.settings` | The app's settings of one project: project page → Uygulamalar → Ayarlar (SDK 1.6) | `{ projectId: string }` | `Screen` (required) |
| `settings` | Olan → Ayarlar → Uygulamalar, instead of the generated form | `null` | `Screen` (required) |
| `chat.action`, `chat.command`, `chat.card`, `mail.sidebar`, `mail.action`, `calendar.event.action`, `meeting.panel` | Modals and panels in chat, email, calendar and meeting screens (surfaces.md) | the object it was opened on | `Screen` recommended (its title is the header; not checked) |
| `task.action`, `issue.action`, `record.card` | A task's or issue's "…" menu; the `open` button of the app's record card (SDK 1.7, projects the app is enabled in) | `{ projectId, task }`, `{ projectId, issue }`, `{ projectId, linkId, target, externalId, payload }` | `Screen` recommended |

`app`, `project.widget`, `settings`, `project.tab` and `project.settings` entries are
`{ "title"?: string }` (≤ 80; defaults to the app name); the other surfaces need `"title"`, `chat.command` also `"command"` (surfaces.md). Every declared surface
must be defined in `defineApp({ ... })` with the same name (`app.surface_missing`), and a surface
defined in code but not declared is never opened (`app.surface_undeclared`).

```tsx
export default defineApp({ app: Overview, 'project.widget': OverdueCard, settings: SettingsScreen });
```

## `projectTemplates`

SDK 1.7: up to 5 project templates the organization's "Yeni proje" lists while the app is installed
for the person. A project made from one gets the template's work packages, statuses, labels, starter
tasks and task/issue templates, and the app is added to it; the statuses and labels are the app's
(members use them, the app manages them with `olan.project.statuses` / `labels`). A new app version
with the same `key` replaces the template.

```json
"projectTemplates": [{
  "key": "purchasing",
  "name": "Satın alma",
  "description": "Talep, onay, sipariş ve teslim",
  "content": {
    "version": 1,
    "lists": [{ "key": "requests", "title": "Talepler", "steps": [{ "key": "approval", "title": "Onay" }] }],
    "statuses": [
      { "key": "todo", "name": "Yeni talep", "color": "#8A94A6", "category": "unstarted" },
      { "key": "awaiting-approval", "name": "Onay bekliyor", "color": "#E0A526", "category": "started" },
      { "key": "done", "name": "Teslim alındı", "color": "#2F9E6E", "category": "completed" },
      { "key": "cancelled", "name": "İptal", "color": "#A1A7B3", "category": "cancelled" }
    ],
    "labels": [{ "name": "Donanım", "color": "#5B8DEF", "groupName": "Tür" }]
  }
}]
```

- `key` `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,62}$`, unique; `name` 1–120; `description` ≤ 2000; `content` ≤ 64 KiB.
- `content`: `version: 1`; `lists` (1–50 work packages, `key`, `title`, `code?`, `color?`, `steps?` ≤ 50);
  `statuses?` (≤ 30, `{ key, name, color: #RRGGBB, category }`; when given they replace the defaults,
  so include one per `unstarted`, `started`, `completed` and `cancelled`); `labels?` (≤ 100,
  `{ name, color, groupName?, description? }`); `tasks?` (≤ 200) and `recordTemplates?` (≤ 50) in the
  shape of Olan's own project templates; `settings?` (`description`, `coverColor`, `estimateScale`).
- The manifest checks the shape (`manifest.project_template_invalid`); the server checks references
  between keys and skips a template it cannot use.

## Settings fields

`settings` maps a key (`^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}$`, ≤ 64 fields) to a field:

| Property | Notes |
|---|---|
| `type` | `"string"`, `"number"`, `"boolean"` or `"select"` |
| `label` | Required, ≤ 80 |
| `description` | ≤ 400 |
| `default` | Same type as the field; for `select` one of the option values |
| `required` | boolean |
| `secret` | boolean: stored encrypted, masked in admin screens. Apps without `server` still receive the value; with `server` the UI gets `null` and only backend code reads it (`olan.secrets.get`, backend.md#secrets) |
| `options` | `select` only: `[{ "value": "TRY", "label": "Türk lirası" }]`, ≥ 1, unique values |

```json
"settings": {
  "currency": { "type": "select", "label": "Para birimi", "default": "TRY", "options": [
    { "value": "TRY", "label": "Türk lirası" }, { "value": "EUR", "label": "Euro" } ] },
  "apiKey": { "type": "string", "label": "API anahtarı", "secret": true },
  "showDone": { "type": "boolean", "label": "Bitenleri göster", "default": false }
}
```

Olan generates the settings form from these fields (unless the app has a `settings` surface).
Read values with `useSettings()` or `olan.settings.get()`; defaults apply to unset fields. In tests
and `validate --strict` the defaults apply too, overridden by `fixtures/settings.json`.

## Web links

`{ "kind": "web-link", "url": "https://…" }` describes a link instead of a packaged app: no
`entry`, no `settings`, no permissions, no `remote`/`events`/`ai`, only the `app` surface (optional), and `icon` is an
http(s) URL or an Olan icon name. Users add web links in Olan → Uygulamalar; they are not built
with this SDK.

## Package (`olan-app pack`)

`dist/<id>-<version>.olanapp` is a ZIP of `olan-app.json`, `dist/app.js`, `dist/server.js` (when
the manifest declares `server`), `assets/**`, a
`digest.json` (SHA-256 of every file and of the whole package) and, when signed (`--dev-sign`,
or `olan-app.key.json` exists), `signature.json` (Ed25519; optional `keyId`, cli.md#signing-and-publishing).
The package must stay ≤ 5 MiB. The bundles keep the license comments of bundled code at the end
of the file; other notices go in `assets/NOTICE` or `assets/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES` (marketplace.md#automatic-checks). Organization admins upload it
(`olan-app publish --org`, or the admin panel's Uygulamalar section).

<!-- docs/server.md -->
# The app's own server (`remote`)

An app may run its own HTTPS server. Olan then sends it signed **events**, runs its **assistant
tools** there, forwards **card actions** and (SDK 1.5, `"requests": true`) the app's own
**requests** made as the person (`olan.remote.request`, remote-requests.md); the server calls Olan
back with short-lived tokens.

```json
"remote": { "url": "https://standup.example.com/olan", "jwksUrl": "https://standup.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json" },
"events": ["project.task.created", "chat.message.created"],
"permissions": ["projects:read", "chat:read"],
"ai": { "tools": [ { "name": "standup_summary", "title": "Standup özeti", "description": "Summarises today's standup of a project.",
  "input": { "type": "object", "properties": { "projectId": { "type": "string" } }, "required": ["projectId"] },
  "permissions": ["projects:read"], "readOnly": true } ] }
```

- `remote.url`: https. Olan posts to `{url}/events`, `{url}/ai-tools/{name}`, `{url}/card-actions`
  and `{url}/requests`. Its origin is also where uploads (files.md) and `Image` pictures may come from.
  `http://127.0.0.1`, `localhost` and private addresses validate, but Olan only delivers to them
  for development installations on servers with `OLAN_APPS_REMOTE_ALLOW_PRIVATE=1`. An admin may
  point an installation to another copy of the server (`remoteUrlOverride`).
- `remote.jwksUrl`: https, your public keys (JWKS) for token requests.
- `remote` implies the permission `remote` ("Veriler `<host>` adresindeki uygulama sunucusuna
  gönderilebilir"), `ai.tools` implies `ai:tools`. Never list them in `permissions`.
- `events` and `ai.tools` need `remote`. Code that Olan runs for you (no server of your own) is
  `server`: backend.md.

## `@olan-app/sdk/server`

Plain Node ≥ 22 (WebCrypto, no dependencies; also Deno, Bun, edge runtimes). Create one per app.

**Where the code lives.** Your own server is a separate Node program that you run and host. In an
app project keep it in `app-server/` (`olan-app init --template remote` creates `app-server/server.ts`,
`routes.ts` and `tsconfig.json`), **not** in `server/`: `server/` is backend code that Olan runs for
you (manifest `server`, backend.md), bundled into the package. `app-server/` is never packed.
`olan-app validate` type-checks it through `app-server/tsconfig.json` (Node types), next to
`tsconfig.json` and `tests/tsconfig.json`; tests import it (`../app-server/server.ts`).

**Running TypeScript.** Node ≥ 22.18 (and 23.6+) runs `.ts` files directly (`node app-server/server.ts`;
type stripping: no enums or namespaces, relative imports with the `.ts` extension). Older Node 22
needs `node --experimental-strip-types app-server/server.ts`, or compile it first (`tsc`, esbuild).

```ts
import { createServer } from 'node:http';
import { createOlanServer, fromNodeRequest, sendNodeResponse, ToolError } from '@olan-app/sdk/server';

const olan = createOlanServer({
  appId: 'com.example.team-standup',
  privateKeyPem: process.env.OLAN_APP_KEY,          // PKCS#8 Ed25519 (or P-256 / RSA) private key
  issuers: process.env.OLAN_ISSUERS!.split(','),    // every Olan server you accept: always explicit
});

createServer(async (req, res) => {
  if (req.url === '/.well-known/jwks.json') return sendNodeResponse(res, Response.json(await olan.jwks()));
  const request = await fromNodeRequest(req);       // raw body: the signature covers the exact bytes
  if (req.url === '/olan/events') {
    return sendNodeResponse(res, await olan.handleEvent(request, {
      'project.task.created': async (event) => { /* event.data.task */ },
    }));
  }
  if (req.url?.startsWith('/olan/ai-tools/')) {
    return sendNodeResponse(res, await olan.handleToolCall(request, {
      standup_summary: async (input, ctx) => {
        const r = await fetch(`${ctx.issuer}/api/v2/projects/${input.projectId}`,
          { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${ctx.token.accessToken}` } });
        if (!r.ok) throw new ToolError('not_found', 'Proje bulunamadı');
        return { result: await r.json(), summary: 'Standup özeti hazır' };
      },
    }));
  }
  if (req.url === '/olan/card-actions') {
    return sendNodeResponse(res, await olan.handleCardAction(request, async (action) => ({ toast: { text: 'Kaydedildi' } })));
  }
  if (req.url === '/olan/requests') {                // olan.remote.request (remote-requests.md)
    return sendNodeResponse(res, await olan.handleRequest(request, {
      'GET /standups/:day': async (ctx) => ({ body: await loadStandup(ctx.user!.organizationId, ctx.params.day) }),
    }));
  }
  res.writeHead(404).end();
}).listen(4100);
```

**Always pass `issuers` explicitly**, e.g. `[process.env.OLAN_ISSUER]` with the `apps.issuer` of the
Olan server's `/.well-known/olan` (Olan's cloud: `https://api.olan.app`). The default
`DEFAULT_ISSUERS` is `['https://api.olan.app']` only (since SDK 1.5; `https://olan.app` before):
self-hosted and development servers are never in it, and requests from an issuer that is not
listed are rejected.

Other helpers: `handleRequest` (remote-requests.md), `appReturnUrl({ issuer, installationId })` and
`isAppReturnUrl({ issuer, installationId, url })` for external flows (links.md), `RequestError`,
`matchRemoteRoute` and `runRemoteRoute` (the router `handleRequest` uses).

`await generateAppKey()` (async, WebCrypto) makes a new Ed25519 key: `{ privateKeyPem, publicJwk,
keyId }`; `jwks()` serves its public half. The `kid` defaults to the key's RFC 7638 thumbprint
(`keyId` overrides it). To replace the key without a gap, see
[Rotating the app key](#rotating-the-app-key).

### `createOlanServer(options)`

| Option | Type | Default | Needed for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appId` **required** | `string` | — | Everything (`iss`/`sub` of client assertions) |
| `issuers` | `readonly string[] \| ((issuer: string) => boolean)` | `DEFAULT_ISSUERS` (`['https://api.olan.app']`) | Always set it (above) |
| `privateKeyPem` | `string` (PKCS#8 PEM: Ed25519, P-256 or RSA) | — | Only `jwks()`, `getInstallationToken()` and `createClientAssertion()`: without it they throw `OlanServerError('no_private_key')`. **Not** needed to verify: `verify`, `handleRequest`, `handleEvent`, `handleToolCall`, `handleCardAction`, `appReturnUrl` work without it |
| `keyId` | `string` | RFC 7638 thumbprint | `kid` of the key in your JWKS |
| `nextPrivateKeyPem`, `nextKeyId` | `string` | — | Key rotation: `jwks()` publishes this key too, tokens are still signed with `privateKeyPem` ([Rotating the app key](#rotating-the-app-key)) |
| `additionalPublicKeys` | `readonly Jwk[]` (each with `kid`) | — | More public keys for `jwks()`, e.g. the retired key while a rotation finishes; private members are dropped |
| `idempotency` | `IdempotencyStore \| false` | `memoryIdempotencyStore()` | Seen `webhook-id`s: `handleEvent` (24 h, a retry is processed once), `handleRequest` (`req_` ids) and `handleCardAction` (`act_` ids), 10 min each (a repeat is a replay: 409 `duplicate_request`); `false` turns the checks off |
| `toleranceSeconds` | `number` | `300` | Allowed clock skew of `webhook-timestamp` |
| `jwksCacheSeconds` | `number` | `600` | Cache of the issuer's `/.well-known/olan` and JWKS |
| `fetch` | `typeof fetch` | global `fetch` | Tests (a fake issuer) |
| `now` | `() => number` | `Date.now` | Tests (ms since the epoch) |

```ts
/** Share one across processes (Redis SET NX EX, a table with a unique key and an expiry). */
interface IdempotencyStore {
  has(id: string): boolean | Promise<boolean>;
  add(id: string, ttlSeconds: number): void | Promise<void>;
}
```

Types exported by `@olan-app/sdk/server`: `OlanServer` (what `createOlanServer` returns),
`OlanServerOptions`, `IdempotencyStore`, `OlanServerError` (`code`, `status`, `detail?`),
`VerifiedRequest`, `IncomingRequest` (a WHATWG `Request` or `{ headers, body: string | Uint8Array }`),
`InstallationToken`, `ToolHandler`/`ToolContext`/`ToolOutput`/`ToolError`, `EventHandler(s)`/`EventContext`,
`CardActionHandler`, and for `handleRequest`: **`RemoteRoutes`** (the router object,
`Readonly<Record<"METHOD /path", RemoteRequestHandler>>`), `RemoteRequestHandler`
(`(ctx: RemoteRequestContext) => RemoteRequestResult | void | Promise<…>`), `RemoteRequestContext`,
`RemoteRequestResult` (`{ status?, headers?, body? }`), `RequestError`, plus `RemoteRequestEnvelope`,
`RemoteRequestUser`, `RemoteAnswer`. Helpers: `memoryIdempotencyStore()`, `fromNodeRequest(req, { maxBytes? })`
(1 MiB default; keeps `req.url`), `sendNodeResponse(res, response)`, `cardResponse(card?, toast?)`.
Constants: `DEFAULT_ISSUERS`, `WEBHOOK_HEADERS`, `REQUEST_ID_RETENTION_SECONDS`, `PROFILE_REQUIRED`,
`TOKEN_INVALIDATING_EVENTS`, `STALE_TOKEN_ERRORS` ([Calling Olan back](#calling-olan-back)).

```ts
import type { RemoteRoutes } from '@olan-app/sdk/server';
export const routes: RemoteRoutes = { 'GET /items': async (ctx) => ({ body: await list(ctx.installationId) }) };
```

## Verifying Olan's requests

Every request from Olan (events, tool calls, card actions, requests) is signed (Standard Webhooks, asymmetric):

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `webhook-id` | `evt_…` / `call_…` / `act_…` / `req_…`: equals the body's `id`; the same on every retry (requests are never retried) |
| `webhook-timestamp` | Unix seconds of this attempt |
| `webhook-signature` | `v1a,<base64 Ed25519 signature of "<id>.<timestamp>.<raw body>">` (several, space-separated, during key rotation) |
| `olan-issuer` | The Olan server, e.g. `https://olan.example.com` |
| `olan-key-id` | `kid` of the signing key in the issuer's JWKS |
| `olan-installation-id` | The installation |
| `olan-event-type`, `olan-delivery-attempt` | Events only |

`olan.verify(request)` checks, in order: the issuer is in `issuers` → the `kid` is in the issuer's
JWKS (found through `<issuer>/.well-known/olan` → `apps.jwksUri`, cached 10 minutes, refetched
at most once a minute for an unknown `kid`) → the signature → the timestamp is within ±5 minutes.
It throws `OlanServerError` (`issuer_not_allowed`, `unknown_key`, `invalid_signature`,
`timestamp_out_of_range`, `missing_header`, `jwks_unavailable`, `invalid_body`); the `handle*`
helpers answer 401 for these. Keep the issuer list explicit: anyone can run "an Olan server".

The signature covers the id, the timestamp and the body, not the URL. The handlers therefore also
check what the body claims against how it arrived:

| Helper | Check | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| all | `body.id === webhook-id` | 400 `invalid_body` |
| `handleRequest` | the envelope's `issuer` equals the `olan-issuer` header (trailing `/` ignored); you map accounts by it | 401 `issuer_mismatch` (400 `invalid_body` without `issuer`) |
| `handleToolCall` | the tool in the URL (`…/ai-tools/{name}`) equals the body's `tool` | 400 `tool_mismatch` |
| `handleRequest`, `handleCardAction` | the `req_` / `act_` id was not seen in the last 10 minutes (Olan never retries them) | 409 `duplicate_request` |
| `handleEvent` | the `evt_` id was not processed in the last 24 h (Olan retries events) | 200 `{ ok: true, duplicate: true }` |

`handleToolCall` knows the URL from a WHATWG `Request` (`request.url`) or from
`fromNodeRequest(req)`, which keeps `req.url`; for a hand-made `{ headers, body }` add `url`
(the path is enough), otherwise only the body names the tool.

## The `/.well-known/olan` document

`GET <issuer>/.well-known/olan` (public, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`) describes an Olan
server. App servers need `apps.issuer`, `apps.jwksUri`, `apps.tokenEndpoint` and `webOrigin`
(`createOlanServer` reads them for you); the CLI and Studio read the rest. An Olan 1.5 server answers:

```json
{
  "apiVersion": 1,
  "serverVersion": "1.5.0",
  "sdkVersions": ["^1.0.0"],
  "apps": {
    "enabled": true,
    "maxPackageBytes": 5242880,
    "surfaces": ["app", "project.widget", "settings", "chat.action", "chat.command", "chat.card", "mail.sidebar", "mail.action", "calendar.event.action", "meeting.panel"],
    "permissions": ["projects:read", "projects:write", "…"],
    "trustedKeyFingerprints": ["3f2957e0dbdd6b87"],
    "builtInKeys": [{ "keyId": "olan-marketplace-2026-10-17", "fingerprint": "3f2957e0dbdd6b87" }],
    "trustedKeys": [{ "name": "olan-marketplace-2026-10-17", "publicKey": "Y/CrYSv6RfoVrZCRFUy6c/JGXsGRtVU9fDOQr8SNHEI=", "fingerprint": "3f2957e0dbdd6b87" }],
    "features": ["db", "record-writes", "remote", "events", "ai-tools", "pim-writes", "project-writes", "app-cards", "remote-requests", "files", "external-return", "app-links"],
    "issuer": "https://api.olan.app",
    "jwksUri": "https://api.olan.app/api/v2/apps/jwks.json",
    "tokenEndpoint": "https://api.olan.app/api/v2/apps/oauth/token",
    "events": ["app.installed", "app.updated", "…"],
    "returnUrlTemplate": "https://olan.app/apps/return/{installationId}",
    "appUrlTemplate": "https://olan.app/apps/a/{appId}"
  },
  "webOrigin": "https://olan.app",
  "catalogUrl": "https://api.olan.app/api/v2/apps/catalog",
  "marketplaceUrl": "https://marketplace.olan.app",
  "revocationsUrl": "https://api.olan.app/api/v2/apps/revocations",
  "marketplaceKeysUrl": "https://api.olan.app/api/v2/apps/marketplace-keys",
  "issuer": "https://api.olan.app"
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `apiVersion`, `serverVersion`, `sdkVersions` | Discovery version (1), the server's version (`minServerVersion` is checked against it), SDK ranges its host serves |
| `apps.enabled` | Olan Apps are on for this server |
| `apps.maxPackageBytes`, `apps.surfaces`, `apps.permissions` | Package size limit (5 MiB), the surfaces and permission ids it knows |
| `apps.trustedKeyFingerprints`, `apps.builtInKeys`, `apps.trustedKeys` | Package signing keys it trusts (first 16 hex of sha256 of the raw key); `builtInKeys` cannot be removed (cli.md#signing-and-publishing). Developers' registered keys are not listed: each vouches only for its developer's own development installations |
| `apps.features` | Capabilities; `remote-requests`, `files`, `external-return`, `app-links` since 1.5 |
| `apps.issuer` | **The issuer to list in `issuers`** (`OLAN_PUBLIC_URL`; also `olan-issuer` and the envelope's `issuer`) |
| `apps.jwksUri` | The Ed25519 keys that sign Olan's requests to app servers (`kid` = `olan-key-id`) |
| `apps.tokenEndpoint` | Where `getInstallationToken` posts its client assertion |
| `apps.events` | Event types this server delivers |
| `apps.returnUrlTemplate`, `apps.appUrlTemplate` | Return address of external flows and permanent app address (links.md); since 1.5, only when the web origin is configured |
| `webOrigin` | Origin of Olan's web app (`OLAN_WEB_URL`), e.g. `https://olan.app` for the API `https://api.olan.app`: return addresses and the CORS origin of uploads (files.md). Missing before 1.5 (`appReturnUrl` then throws `web_origin_unknown`) |
| `catalogUrl`, `revocationsUrl`, `marketplaceKeysUrl` | Organization catalog, signed revocation list and marketplace key set (authenticated) |
| `marketplaceUrl` | Olan Marketplace this server uses (null from older servers) |
| `marketplaceOwnership` | Only while an ownership proof runs (then `Cache-Control: no-store`): `{ serverId, challenge, token }` |
| `issuer` | Same as `apps.issuer` |

Older servers may lack the newer fields: read them as optional. The CLI's local issuers
(`events send`, `requests send`, `dev --remote live`, `createTestIssuer` in tests) serve the same shape.

## Events

Delivered to `POST {remote.url}/events` with this body (`data` version 1):

```json
{ "id": "evt_…", "type": "project.task.created", "version": 1, "occurredAt": "…", "issuer": "https://olan.example.com",
  "installationId": "…", "appId": "com.example.team-standup", "actor": { "kind": "user", "id": "…" }, "data": { … } }
```

| Event | Permission | Sent for | `data` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `app.installed`, `app.updated`, `app.uninstalled` | none, always sent | the installation | `{ versionId, version, scope, grantedPermissions, organizationId }` (`organizationId`, the tenant id = `user.organizationId` of requests, since Olan 1.5; `uninstalled`: `{}`) |
| `app.consent.changed` | none, always sent | the installation | `{ userId, permissions, declined }` |
| `chat.message.created` | `chat:read` | conversations the app was added to | `{ conversationId, message: { id, body, senderId, senderKind, createdAt, replyToId, threadRootId, attachments } }` |
| `project.task.created`, `project.task.updated` | `projects:read` | projects the app was added to | `{ projectId, task, changed? }` |
| `project.task.deleted` | `projects:read` | projects the app was added to | `{ projectId, taskId, title }` |
| `project.task.completed` | `projects:read` | projects the app was added to (SDK 1.7) | `{ projectId, task, changed }`: the task moved to a completed status (also sent as `project.task.updated`) |
| `project.issue.opened`, `.closed`, `.triaged` | `projects:read` | projects the app was added to (SDK 1.7) | `{ projectId, issue: { id, key, number, title, kind, state, stateReason, priority, assigneeId, labels, triagedAt, … }, decision? }` (`triaged`: `accepted`, `declined`, `duplicate`, `snoozed`) |
| `project.approval.decided` | `projects:read` | only the installation that asked (`olan.project.approvals.request`, SDK 1.7) | `{ projectId, installationId, approvalId, externalId, linkId, state: approved \| rejected \| cancelled, decisions }` |
| `calendar.event.created`, `.updated`, `.deleted` | `calendar:read` | people whose consent includes it | `{ userId, calendarId, eventId, uid, event? }` |
| `meeting.created`, `.started`, `.ended`, `.cancelled` | `meetings:read` | meetings of consenting organizers or of granted projects | `{ meetingId, slug, title, startsAt, endsAt, organizerId, projectId? }` |

- Answer 2xx within 10 s. Anything else is retried after 30 s, 2 min, 10 min, 30 min, 1 h, 3 h,
  6 h and 12 h (±20 %, `Retry-After` honoured for 429/503); `410` stops at once. Order is not guaranteed.
- `handleEvent` skips `webhook-id`s it already processed (in memory; pass `idempotency` with a shared
  store when running several processes) and answers 500 when the handler throws, so Olan retries.
- Bodies over 256 KiB cut `chat.message.created` `body` (`truncated: true`). An app does not get
  events it caused itself.

## Assistant tools (`ai.tools`)

The Olan assistant (and Olan's MCP server) lists the tools of apps the person consented to
(`ai:tools` plus each tool's `permissions`) as `app_<slug>_<name>`, where `slug` is the last part
of the app id in `[a-z0-9]` (≤ 16): `app_teamstandup_standup_summary`.

- Manifest: ≤ 16 tools; `name` `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,31}$`; `title` ≤ 80; `description` 1–1024 (the
  model reads it); `input` a JSON Schema with `"type": "object"` (≤ 8 KiB, only local `$ref`);
  `permissions` ⊆ the manifest's; `readOnly` (runs without confirmation, retried once) or
  `destructive` (always confirmed), not both. Other tools are confirmed by the person first.
- Request body: `{ id: "call_…", tool, installationId, appId, issuer, channel: "assistant" | "mcp",
  user: { id, locale, timeZone }, input, token: { accessToken, expiresIn: 300 } }`.
- `timeoutMs` (SDK 1.5): 1000–60000, default 15000; a `readOnly` tool keeps at most 15000
  (`manifest.ai_tool_invalid`). Use it for slow tools that change something (an AI draft).
- Answer HTTP 200 within the tool's timeout: `{ "ok": true, "result": …, "summary"?: "≤ 500" }` or
  `{ "ok": false, "error": { "code", "message" } }`, ≤ 64 KiB. Olan reports `app_tool_timeout`,
  `app_tool_failed` (non-2xx), `app_tool_result_too_large`, `app_tool_unavailable`.
- Tool results are untrusted content for the assistant: writes after them ask for confirmation.

## Card actions

A card's `submit` button (cards.md) posts `{ id: "act_…", issuer, installationId, user: { id, locale },
conversationId, messageId, name, payload, token }` to `{url}/card-actions`; answer within 5 s with
`{ card?, toast? }` (`card` replaces the message's card). Olan sends each action once:
`handleCardAction` answers a repeated `act_` id with 409 `duplicate_request` without running the
handler (ids kept 10 minutes in `idempotency`; share the store across processes).

## Calling Olan back

- **Embedded tokens.** Tool calls and card actions carry `token.accessToken` (300 s, on behalf of the
  person; permissions = the tool's ∩ the person's). Use it as `Authorization: Bearer …` on the routes
  app tokens may call (e.g. `GET <issuer>/api/v2/projects/:projectId`, `…/apps/installations/:id/…`).
- **Installation tokens.** `await olan.getInstallationToken({ issuer, installationId, userId? })` signs
  a client assertion (RFC 7523 `private_key_jwt`: `iss = sub = appId`,
  `aud = <issuer>/api/v2/apps/oauth/token`, ≤ 300 s, single-use `jti`, `olan_installation_id`,
  optional `olan_user_id`) and returns `{ accessToken, expiresIn (≤ 900), permissions }` (cached).
  - Without `userId` (**app identity**): only the app's own `db` collections, `users.get` with
    `users:read`, and the projects and conversations people added the app to (project/chat
    settings → Uygulamalar). Never calendars, contacts, mail, meetings or creating projects.
  - With `userId`: on behalf of that person; fails with `consent_required` until they consented.
  - Errors: `invalid_client` (unknown key, bad signature), `invalid_grant`, `consent_required`.
- **After a grant change.** A cached token keeps the permissions it was issued with (≤ 15 min), so
  after a new version or a consent change the first call needing a new permission would be refused.
  `handleEvent` drops the installation's cached tokens (app identity and every person) on
  `app.updated`, `app.consent.changed` and `app.uninstalled` (`TOKEN_INVALIDATING_EVENTS`) before
  your handler runs. Handling events yourself, or in another process or `createOlanServer` instance
  (one per app id)? Call `olan.invalidateToken(installationId, { issuer? })` (returns how many it
  dropped) or `olan.clearTokenCache()`.
- **`olan.fetchOlan({ issuer, installationId, userId? }, path, init?)`** sends `init` to
  `<issuer><path>` with the installation token (another origin is refused). A 403
  `permission_denied` or `insufficient_scope` (`STALE_TOKEN_ERRORS`: the token predates the grant)
  is retried **once** with a fresh token (bodies must be replayable: string, bytes, `FormData`, …);
  a second refusal and other 403s (`app_project_forbidden`, …) come back unchanged.

## Rotating the app key

Olan verifies your client assertions with the keys at `remote.jwksUrl`, cached 10 minutes and
refetched at most once a minute for an unknown `kid`. Publish the new key before you sign with it:

1. **Publish the next key.** `const next = await generateAppKey()`; store `next.privateKeyPem` as a
   second secret and deploy with
   `createOlanServer({ …, privateKeyPem: CURRENT, keyId: 'app-2026-10', nextPrivateKeyPem: NEXT, nextKeyId: 'app-2027-01' })`.
   `jwks()` now serves both keys (current first); tokens are still signed with the current key.
2. **Wait** at least 10 minutes (Olan's JWKS cache), longer if a CDN caches your `jwksUrl`.
3. **Switch.** Deploy with `privateKeyPem: NEXT, keyId: 'app-2027-01'` and
   `additionalPublicKeys: [{ ...currentPublicJwk, kid: 'app-2026-10' }]` (the old public half,
   e.g. `(await previousServer.jwks()).keys[0]`), so assertions signed by processes that still run
   the old key keep verifying.
4. **Retire.** After every process runs the new key (and at least 5 minutes: an assertion lives
   60 s), drop `additionalPublicKeys` and delete the old secret.

A key that leaked is removed at once instead: switch to the new key without `additionalPublicKeys`.
Tokens issued before stay valid until they expire (≤ 15 minutes). Never reuse a `kid`.

## When the app needs the person's profile

`email`, `displayName` and `role` reach `handleRequest` only with `profile:read`
(remote-requests.md#the-person-user). When a route needs them and they are missing, answer the
generic error `profile_required` (exported as `PROFILE_REQUIRED` by `@olan-app/sdk/server` and
`@olan-app/sdk`) instead of creating an account from `user.id` alone:

```ts
import { PROFILE_REQUIRED, RequestError } from '@olan-app/sdk/server';

'POST /connections/start': async (ctx) => {
  if (!ctx.user?.email) throw new RequestError(409, { error: PROFILE_REQUIRED, message: 'Profil izni gerekli' });
  …
},
```

The app gets a `RemoteError` `remote_rejected` with `status` 409 and
`details.error === PROFILE_REQUIRED`, and explains that the app needs "Profilinizi görme".

## Self-hosted Olan servers

Each Olan server signs with its own key and is its own issuer (`OLAN_PUBLIC_URL`): add every
server you serve to `issuers`. Olan servers that the internet cannot reach still deliver to you,
but embedded tokens only work where your server can reach that Olan. Deliveries follow the
organization's egress rules.

## Developing locally

```sh
npx olan-app events send project.task.created        # signed event to remote.url/events (sample data from fixtures)
npx olan-app events send chat.message.created --data @event-data.json --to http://127.0.0.1:4100/olan
npx olan-app tools call standup_summary --input '{"projectId":"p0"}'
npx olan-app requests send GET "/standups/2026-10-18?team=web"   # olan.remote.request to remote.url/requests
npx olan-app dev --remote live                       # the dev server forwards the app's remote.request calls
```

They sign with your development key and serve its JWKS from a local issuer
`http://127.0.0.1:5180` while the request runs (for `dev --remote live`, while dev runs): add it to
`issuers` in development (`issuers: ['https://olan.example.com', 'http://127.0.0.1:5180']`). The
embedded token is a placeholder (`olan-app-dev-token`); calls back to Olan need a local Olan server.
MCP: `olan_app_event_send`, `olan_app_tool_call`, `olan_app_request_send`. Automated server tests:
`createTestIssuer` and `signRemoteRequest` (remote-requests.md#testing-the-app-server).

<!-- docs/remote-requests.md -->
# Remote requests (`olan.remote.request`)

An app with its own server (`remote`, server.md) can ask that server for data **as the person using
the app** (SDK 1.5). The sandbox never sees a token and the app server never sees Olan's cookie:

```
sandbox ── olan.remote.request ──▶ Olan host ──▶ Olan server ── signed POST {remote.url}/requests ──▶ app server
        ◀── { status, headers, body } ◀────────────────────────── HTTP 200 { status, headers?, body } ◀──
```

Olan checks the installation, the person's consent and the limits, signs an envelope with the
person's identity and a 300 s token, posts it, and passes the app server's answer back. Olan never
retries a request.

## Manifest

```json
"sdk": "^1.5.0",
"remote": { "url": "https://media.example.com/olan", "jwksUrl": "https://media.example.com/olan/jwks.json", "requests": true },
"permissions": ["profile:read"]
```

- `remote.requests: true` turns the call on (default `false`; without it every call fails with
  `permission_denied`, "manifest does not declare remote.requests").
- No permission of its own: it uses the implied `remote` permission. An admin who blocks `remote`
  blocks it (`permission_denied`).
- `profile:read` (optional) adds the person's email, name and role to the envelope (below).
- UI only: backend code (`server`, backend.md) has no `olan.remote`; it uses `olan.http.fetch`.

## Calling it

```tsx
import { isRemoteError, olan, useQuery } from '@olan-app/sdk';

const items = useQuery(() => olan.remote.request({ method: 'GET', path: '/items', query: { status: ['ready', 'processing'] } }), []);
// items.data: { status: 200, headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' }, body: [...] }

const created = await olan.remote.request({
  method: 'POST',
  path: '/brands/b1/posts',
  body: { text: 'Merhaba' },
  headers: { 'idempotency-key': draftId },
  timeoutMs: 60_000,                 // a slow AI draft; default 30 s
});
```

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `method` **required** | `'GET' \| 'POST' \| 'PUT' \| 'PATCH' \| 'DELETE'` |
| `path` **required** | Starts with `/`, ≤ 2048, no `?`, `#`, `\`, `//`, `.`/`..` segments, encoded `/` or control characters. Put parameters in `query`, encode segments with `encodeURIComponent` |
| `query` | `Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| (string \| number \| boolean)[]>`, ≤ 50 keys (≤ 128 characters each), ≤ 100 values per key. The app server gets strings (`true` → `"true"`) |
| `headers` | Only `accept`, `accept-language`, `if-match`, `if-none-match`, `idempotency-key` (names lower-cased, values one line ≤ 1024). Others: `invalid_params` |
| `body` | Any JSON value, ≤ 1 MiB serialised (`payload_too_large`); not with `GET` and `DELETE` |
| `timeoutMs` | Integer 1000–60000, default 30000 |

The result (`RemoteResponse`) is `{ status, headers: { 'content-type'?, etag? }, body }` for an app
server status **200–399**. `body` is the app server's JSON as it is (`null` when it had none).

## Errors: `RemoteError`

Every failure rejects with a `RemoteError` (a subclass of `OlanError`, so `isOlanError` is true too):

| `code` | When | `status` | `details` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `remote_rejected` | The app server answered 400–499 | its status | its `body` |
| `remote_unavailable` | The app server answered 500–599 (`reason: 'http_status'`), or no usable answer: `reason` `timeout`, `network`, `invalid_response` (not the wrapper below, not JSON, HTTP status other than 200), `response_too_large` (> 4 MiB) | its status, else `0` | its `body`, else `null` |
| `consent_required` | The person has not consented to the app yet | `403` | `null` |
| `permission_denied` | No `remote.requests`, or `remote` is blocked by policy | `403` | `null` |
| `feature_not_enabled` | The organization's plan does not include the app's feature | `403` | `null` |
| `payload_too_large` | `body` over 1 MiB | `413` | `null` |
| `rate_limited` | Over 300 requests a minute, or 8 at once, per person and installation; `retryAfterSeconds` says when to retry | `429` | `null` |
| `invalid_params` | A field breaks the rules above | `400` | `null` |
| `not_installed`, `cancelled`, `host_error`, `unknown_method` | As for every call (errors.md); `unknown_method` on an Olan server before 1.5 | | |

```tsx
try {
  await olan.remote.request({ method: 'POST', path: '/items', body: draft });
} catch (error) {
  if (isRemoteError(error, 'remote_rejected') && error.status === 422) {
    setIssues((error.details as { issues?: Issue[] } | null)?.issues ?? []);   // the server's 422 body
  } else if (isRemoteError(error, 'remote_unavailable')) {
    setBanner(error.reason === 'timeout' ? 'Sunucu yanıt vermedi' : 'Sunucuya ulaşılamıyor');
  } else throw error;
}
```

`RemoteError`: `code`, `message`, `status: number`, `details: JsonValue`, `reason?` and
`retryAfterSeconds?`. `isRemoteError(error, code?)` narrows an unknown error. In `useQuery` the
`RemoteError` is in `query.error`.

## The app server: `handleRequest`

```ts
import { createOlanServer, RequestError } from '@olan-app/sdk/server';

const olan = createOlanServer({
  appId: 'com.example.media-desk',
  privateKeyPem: process.env.OLAN_APP_KEY,
  issuers: (process.env.OLAN_ISSUERS ?? '').split(',').filter(Boolean),   // always explicit
});

// POST {remote.url}/requests
const response = await olan.handleRequest(request, {
  'GET /items': async (ctx) => ({ body: await listItems(ctx.user!.organizationId) }),
  'POST /items': async (ctx) => ({ status: 201, body: await createItem(ctx.user!, ctx.body) }),
  'GET /items/:id': async (ctx) => {
    const item = await findItem(ctx.params.id);
    if (!item) throw new RequestError(404, { error: 'item_not_found' });
    return { body: item, headers: { etag: `"${item.revision}"` } };
  },
  'GET /files/*': async (ctx) => ({ body: await describe(ctx.params['*']) }),   // the rest of the path
});
```

`request` is a WHATWG `Request`, or `{ headers, body: Uint8Array }` from `fromNodeRequest(req)`
(server.md); the answer is a `Response` (`sendNodeResponse(res, response)` in Node).

- `handleRequest(request, router)` verifies the request (below), checks the envelope (`id` equals
  `webhook-id`, `installationId`, `appId`, `request.method`, `request.path`; `issuer` equals the
  `olan-issuer` header, else HTTP 401 `{ error: 'issuer_mismatch' }`), refuses a repeated
  `req_` id with **HTTP 409** `{ error: 'duplicate_request' }` (ids are kept 10 minutes in the
  `idempotency` store; pass a shared one when you run several processes), then routes.
- Routes are `"METHOD /path"`: `:name` matches one segment (decoded into `ctx.params.name`), a
  trailing `/*` the rest (`ctx.params['*']`), `*` as the method any method. The first matching route
  in declaration order wins: list specific routes first. `router` may also be one function.
- Unknown path: `status: 404` `{ error: 'unknown_route' }`; known path, other method: `status: 405`
  `{ error: 'method_not_allowed' }`. Both are wrapped (HTTP 200), so the app sees `remote_rejected`.
- A route returns `{ status?, headers?, body? }` (`status` default 200, 200–599; `body` default
  `null`). `throw new RequestError(status, body?, headers?)` answers that status; any other
  exception answers `status: 500` `{ error: 'internal_error' }` (the app sees `remote_unavailable`).
- Answer within the request's `ctx.timeoutMs` (default 30 s, at most 60 s): Olan gives up then.

The route context (`RemoteRequestContext`):

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `id` | `req_<uuid>`, also the `webhook-id` |
| `issuer` | The Olan server (`https://api.olan.app` for Olan's cloud) |
| `installationId`, `appId` | The installation that called |
| `user` | `{ id, organizationId, locale, timeZone, email?, displayName?, role? }`; `null` for an app-identity call (none in SDK 1.5: every request comes from a person) |
| `method`, `path`, `params` | The request and the route's parameters |
| `query` | `Record<string, string \| string[]>` (normalised) |
| `headers` | Only the allowed request headers, lower-case |
| `body` | JSON, `null` when none |
| `token` | `{ accessToken, expiresIn: 300 }` on behalf of the person: call Olan back (server.md#calling-olan-back) |
| `timeoutMs` | What the app asked for |

### The person (`user`)

- `user.id` is the central Olan user id (the OIDC `sub` of "Olan ile giriş yap") and
  `user.organizationId` the tenant id. Map them to your accounts as `(issuer, user.id)` and
  `(issuer, user.organizationId)`: ids are unique per issuer only.
- `locale` (`tr`, `en-US`) and `timeZone` (IANA) are always present.
- `email`, `displayName` and `role` are present **only** when the person's permissions include
  `profile:read` (permissions.md); otherwise the keys are missing. `email` is the Olan account's
  address (verified by Olan). `displayName` is missing when the person has none. `role` is
  `'admin'` (organization admins) or `'member'`.
- Without `profile:read`, do not create accounts from `user.id` alone if you need an email; answer
  the generic `409 { error: 'profile_required' }` (`throw new RequestError(409, { error: PROFILE_REQUIRED })`,
  server.md#when-the-app-needs-the-persons-profile) and let the app explain it: it gets
  `remote_rejected` with `error.details.error === PROFILE_REQUIRED` (exported by `@olan-app/sdk`).
- No `user` means the app identity (Phase 3 tokens): never act on behalf of a person then.

## The envelope

`POST {remote.url}/requests` (the installation's `remoteUrlOverride` applies), signed like events
(server.md#verifying-olans-requests):

```
POST https://media.example.com/olan/requests
content-type: application/json
webhook-id: req_5f0c2a8e-1b7d-4c31-9b0e-2f7d8c1a9e44
webhook-timestamp: 1792310400
webhook-signature: v1a,<base64 Ed25519 signature of "<webhook-id>.<webhook-timestamp>.<raw body>">
olan-issuer: https://api.olan.app
olan-key-id: olan-apps-2026-10-17
olan-installation-id: 6d3f8e2a-0c4b-4f7e-9a51-3b2c1d0e9f87
```

```json
{
  "id": "req_5f0c2a8e-1b7d-4c31-9b0e-2f7d8c1a9e44",
  "issuer": "https://api.olan.app",
  "installationId": "6d3f8e2a-0c4b-4f7e-9a51-3b2c1d0e9f87",
  "appId": "com.example.media-desk",
  "user": { "id": "0b7a1c2d-…", "organizationId": "9c8b7a6d-…", "locale": "tr", "timeZone": "Europe/Istanbul",
            "email": "utku@example.com", "displayName": "Utku Gökcan", "role": "admin" },
  "request": { "method": "POST", "path": "/brands/b1/posts", "query": { "draft": "true", "channel": ["instagram", "tiktok"] },
               "headers": { "idempotency-key": "c1f2" }, "body": { "text": "Merhaba" }, "timeoutMs": 60000 },
  "token": { "accessToken": "eyJhbGciOi…", "expiresIn": 300 }
}
```

No `olan-event-type` or `olan-delivery-attempt` header. Verify in this order: issuer in your
allowlist → `kid` in the issuer's JWKS → signature over the raw bytes → timestamp within ±5 minutes
→ `body.id === webhook-id` → `body.issuer` is the `olan-issuer` header → the `req_` id not seen in the last 10 minutes (a repeat is a replay,
since Olan never retries). `handleRequest` does all of it.

## The answer: the JSON wrapper

To every **verified** request the app server answers **HTTP 200**, `content-type: application/json`:

```json
{ "status": 201, "headers": { "content-type": "application/json", "etag": "\"v7\"" }, "body": { "id": "post_9", "status": "draft" } }
```

- `status`: the app's own status, an integer 200–599 (404 "no such brand", 422 validation …).
- `headers`: optional; Olan passes only `content-type` and `etag` to the app.
- `body`: any JSON value, `null` when none. The raw answer is ≤ 4 MiB.
- A request that fails verification gets **HTTP 401** `{ error, message }` without the wrapper; a
  malformed envelope HTTP 400; a replayed id HTTP 409.
- Any HTTP status other than 200, a body that is not the wrapper, more than 4 MiB or no answer in
  time is `remote_unavailable` for the app (`reason`: `http_status`, `invalid_response`,
  `response_too_large`, `timeout`, `network`).

The wrapper keeps your own statuses apart from transport failures (a 401 signature error, a 502
proxy, a missing `/requests` route). A server that already has an HTTP API can forward the request
internally and wrap that answer (`{ status: res.statusCode, headers: res.headers, body: res.json() }`).

Without the SDK (another language), follow the same rules: verify as above, answer the wrapper,
keep seen ids 10 minutes.

## Limits

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Request body | 1 MiB (JSON) |
| App server answer | 4 MiB |
| Timeout | 30 s default, 1–60 s |
| Rate | 300 a minute and 8 at once per person and installation (`rate_limited`, `Retry-After`) |
| Path / query | 2048 characters / 50 keys, 100 values per key |
| Replay window | Keep `req_` ids ≥ 10 minutes |

Olan writes an audit row per request (`remote.request { method, status, durationMs, errorCode? }`);
paths, queries, headers and bodies are never stored.

## Issuers: always pass them explicitly

`createOlanServer({ issuers })` decides which Olan servers you accept. Always set it, e.g.
`issuers: [process.env.OLAN_ISSUER]` with the `apps.issuer` of the Olan server's
`/.well-known/olan` (Olan's cloud: `https://api.olan.app`). The default (`DEFAULT_ISSUERS`,
`['https://api.olan.app']`) is Olan's cloud only; self-hosted and development servers (e.g.
`http://localhost:4000`, the CLI's `http://127.0.0.1:5180`) are never in it, and a request from an
issuer that is not listed is rejected (`issuer_not_allowed`, HTTP 401).

## Testing

**The app.** `renderApp({ remote })` runs `olan.remote.request` against routes in the same
`"METHOD /path"` format (or `fixtures/remote.json` answers), with the same wrapper and `RemoteError`
mapping; `app.host.remoteRequests` holds each envelope and answer (testing.md#remote-requests-files-and-links).
Pass your server's own routes object to test the UI against the real route code.

### Testing the app server

`@olan-app/cli/testing` has a local Olan issuer for server tests (`olan-app init --template remote`
writes this test): `createTestIssuer()` serves `/.well-known/olan` (with `webOrigin`) and the JWKS
of a fresh Ed25519 key on `127.0.0.1` and returns `{ issuer, keyId, jwk, wellKnown(), sign(), close() }`;
`signRemoteRequest(issuer, input, options?)` returns `{ headers, body, envelope }`, exactly what Olan
posts to `{remote.url}/requests`. Your server lists `issuer.issuer` in `issuers` and verifies the
