| `publish --org [--server <api url>] [--token <t>] [--file <pkg>] [--dev-sign]` | Packs and uploads to an organization catalog (admins; development and offline servers). Token from `--token` or `OLAN_TOKEN`, server from `--server`, `OLAN_SERVER` or `OLAN_API_URL`. Warns when the server will not install the version |
| `try [--server <api url>] [--token <t>]` | Packs (validate + build, like `pack`), signs with your development key and installs the app for your organization on a development server (`POST <server>/api/v2/apps/developer/try`, multipart `package`; needs developer access and a server that trusts the key). Same server and token as `publish --org`. Prints the app address `<webOrigin>/apps/<installationId>` (below) |
| `revocations sign --dev --in list.json [--out revocations.json]` | Development only: signs a revocation list with your development key (below) |
| `events send <type> [--to <url>] [--data <json\|@file>] [--installation <id>] [--attempt <n>] [--id <evt_…>] [--issuer-port 5180]` | Sends one signed event to the app's own server (`{remote.url}/events`), signed with your development key; a local issuer `http://127.0.0.1:5180` serves its JWKS meanwhile (server.md#developing-locally). Non-2xx: `events.delivery_failed` |
| `tools call <name> [--input <json\|@file>] [--to <url>] [--user <id>] [--channel assistant\|mcp]` | Calls an `ai.tools` tool on the app server like the Olan assistant and checks input and answer |
| `requests send <METHOD> <path[?query]> [--body <json\|@file>] [--query <json>] [--headers <json>] [--user <id>] [--profile\|--no-profile] [--role admin\|member] [--timeout <ms>] [--to <url>] [--issuer-port 5180]` | Sends one signed `olan.remote.request` envelope to `{remote.url}/requests` (development key, local issuer `http://127.0.0.1:5180`) and reads the answer as Olan does: prints the `{ status, headers, body }` wrapper and what the app gets (the response or a `RemoteError`). `--profile` (default: when the manifest has `profile:read`) adds `email`, `displayName`, `role`. No usable answer (401, not the wrapper, not running): `requests.delivery_failed`. Git Bash rewrites `/items` into a Windows path: use `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` or `//items` there |
| `docs <query> [--limit 8]` | Searches these docs offline |
| `mcp` | MCP server over stdio (below) |

## The agent loop

1. Edit `src/app.tsx` (and `olan-app.json`, `fixtures/`, `tests/`).
2. `npx olan-app validate --strict --json` — fix every error (each has `code`, `file`, `line`, `hint`).
3. `npx olan-app test --json` — fix failing tests or the app.
4. Repeat until both report `"ok": true`. That is "done".

## Output

Without `--json`: results on stdout, progress and problems on stderr as
`file:line:column code: message` plus `hint:` lines.

With `--json`, stdout holds exactly one JSON object (for marketplace commands the marketplace's answer, marketplace.md):

```json
{ "ok": true, "command": "validate", "result": { … }, "warnings": [ … ] }
{ "ok": false, "command": "validate", "errors": [{ "code": "tree.unknown_prop", "message": "…", "file": "src/app.tsx", "line": 12, "column": 5, "hint": "…" }], "result": { … } }
```

`dev --json` prints the envelope on one line, then one JSON line per event
(`{"type":"rebuilt","buildId":"…","durationMs":…}`, `{"type":"error","errors":[…]}`,
`{"type":"manifest"}`, `{"type":"log","level":"info","args":[…],"at":"…"}`).

Exit codes: `0` success, `1` the command failed (errors), `2` usage error (unknown command or
option).

`validate --json` result: `{ app: { id, version }, strict, checks: [{ name, ok, skipped? }],
bundleBytes, surfaces: [{ surface, rendered, nodes, calls: [{ method, ok, code? }], text }], review? }`;
`--strict` adds `review: { findings: [{ check, code, severity, message, path?, hint?, rule? }], usage }`
(every marketplace finding, info included); review issues in `errors`/`warnings` carry `rule`.
Checks: `manifest`, `build`, `files`, `size`, `backend` (with `server`), `typescript`, `strict`. With `server` the result also has
`backend: { bytes, engine, handlers: { functions, schedules, events, hooks, migrate } }`; `build --json` has
`backend: { file, bytes, sha256 }`; `pack` puts `dist/server.js` in the package.

`pack --json` result: `{ file, bytes, sha256, signed, publicKey, keyFingerprint, files: [{ path, bytes, sha256 }] }`
(`files` are the app files; the archive also holds `digest.json` and, when signed, `signature.json`:
"3 app files (+ digest, signature)"),
plus `devKey: { file, created, fingerprint, envLine }` with `--dev-sign`. `sign --json` result:
`{ file, bytes, sha256, publicKey, keyFingerprint, keyId, signedAt, replaced }`. `publish --json` adds
`trust` (the server's verdict, below). `test --report --json` adds `report: { file, appId, appVersion,
packageSha256, package, keyFingerprint, keyFile, keyCreated }`.

## dev server

`olan-app dev` listens on `http://localhost:5178` (127.0.0.1 only). `--host 0.0.0.0` listens on
every interface and prints the LAN addresses (`result.lanUrls`) for the Olan mobile app's direct
mode (development builds); anyone on that network can then reach the server, so use it only on a
trusted network.

| Endpoint | |
|---|---|
| `GET /manifest` | The parsed `olan-app.json` (422 `{ error: 'manifest_invalid', issues }`) |
| `GET /app.js` | Latest successful bundle (503 `{ error: 'build_failed', errors }`) |
| `GET /package` | That bundle (and, with `server`, the backend) packed and signed with your development key: `application/octet-stream`, `content-disposition: attachment; filename="<id>-<version>.olanapp"`, `x-olan-package-sha256`, `x-olan-signing-key` (fingerprint). Studio's "Bu kurumda dene" uploads it. `?version=<semver>` packs and signs it with that `version` in the packaged `olan-app.json` (the server-named `-dev.N`; the file on disk is not changed; otherwise 400 `version_invalid`). 503 `build_failed` while a build fails, 422 `manifest_invalid` |
| `GET /status` | `{ appId, version, buildId, errors, builtAt, user: { id } }`; hosts using `/rpc` send `user` as `context.user` |
| `GET /fixtures` | The mock data |
| `POST /rpc` | `{ method, params, permissions? }` → the mock host's answer |
| `POST /logs` | `{ entries: [{ level, args, at }] }` (≤ 100 entries, ≤ 8 KiB each) → 204; printed as `[app <level>] …` (`--json`: `log` events) |
| `ws://localhost:5178/ws` | `{ type: 'rebuilt', buildId }`, `{ type: 'error', errors }`, `{ type: 'manifest' }`; with a backend also `{ type: 'backend', kind, name, ok }`, `backend-built`, `backend-error` |

With `server` (backend.md) the backend runs locally in `@olan-app/runtime` on the same mock host
(`olan.backend.call` through `/rpc` reaches it), is rebuilt when files under `server/` change, and
every invocation is printed with its console lines (`backend schedule digest: ok (4 ms)`,
`  [backend log] …`; `--json`: `backend-invocation` events). `--engine` forces an engine; `auto` falls
back to QuickJS where isolated-vm has no prebuild and prints
`isolated-vm prebuild not available on <platform>; using QuickJS (slower)`. `dev` bundles the
backend in memory, unminified (it writes no `dist/server.js`): its `sha256` differs from the
minified `dist/server.js` of `olan-app build`.

| Endpoint | |
|---|---|
| `GET /backend` | `{ engine, sha256, errors, schedules, hooks, events }` (also `status.backend`) |
| `POST /backend/call` | `{ name, args?, permissions? }` → `{ ok, value \| error, logs, cpuMs, wallMs }` (`result`: alias of `value`); a trigger's fallback function answers `backend_function_not_found` |
| `POST /backend/schedules/<name>/run` | Run a schedule now → `{ ok, value \| error, logs, cpuMs, wallMs }` |
| `POST /backend/events/<type>` | `{ data? }` (default: sample data from the fixtures) → the handler's outcome |
| `POST /hooks/<name>` | Raw body ≤ 1 MiB: verified like Olan does (secret from `fixtures/settings.json`), then the hook's answer, or `202` after 10 s |

In Olan open Studio (`/studio`, needs developer access from an admin), add the address under
"Geliştirme sunucuları", and the preview reloads on every save. `--open` opens
`<server>/studio?dev=<dev url>`.

**Remote requests in dev.** By default `dev` answers `olan.remote.request` (through `/rpc`) from
`fixtures/remote.json`, like tests do. `--remote live` sends each call to your running app server
instead: a signed envelope to `{remote.url}/requests` from the development issuer
`http://127.0.0.1:<--issuer-port, 5180>` (your development key; it runs as long as `dev` and serves
its `/.well-known/olan` and JWKS), read with Olan's rules (HTTP 200 + wrapper, ≤ 4 MiB, the call's
`timeoutMs`). List that issuer in the server's `issuers`. Each call is printed
(`remote GET /items → 200 (12 ms)`; `--json`: `{"type":"remote","message":…}`); a 401 means the
issuer is not listed. The envelope's `installationId` is `00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000a1` and
the token a placeholder.

**Stopping `dev`.** Ctrl+C or SIGTERM. On Windows Ctrl+C works in Windows Terminal, PowerShell and
cmd; closing the terminal window, or ending the shell or agent process that started `dev`, also
stops it within 2 s (it watches its parent process), so no orphaned server keeps the port. With
`--detach` it keeps running: stop it with `Stop-Process -Id <pid>` (PowerShell) or
`taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F` (the PID of the `node` process listening on 5178:
`netstat -ano | findstr :5178`), or `kill <pid>` elsewhere.

## Signing and publishing

An Olan server installs and runs a package only when its Ed25519 signature verifies **and** the
signing key is on the server's trusted key list (`OLAN_APPS_TRUSTED_KEYS`). The public key inside
`signature.json` proves nothing by itself. Every Olan server ships with the **Olan Marketplace key** built in (key id `olan-marketplace-2026-10-17`); `OLAN_APPS_TRUSTED_KEYS` can add keys but cannot remove the built-in one, which is revoked only through the marketplace revocation list (Phase 4a).
In production the list holds the **Olan Marketplace key only**: every app, organization-only apps included, is reviewed and signed by Olan Marketplace
(Phase 4). There is no organization key, and an administrator's approval does not replace the
signature.

| Package | Upload to a catalog | Install / run |
|---|---|---|
| Signed with a trusted key | accepted | yes |
| Unsigned | accepted, marked "İmzasız" | no: `package_unsigned` |
| Signed with another key | accepted, marked "Bilinmeyen anahtar" | no: `package_untrusted_key` |
| Bad signature or digest | rejected: `package_invalid` | — |

Trust is checked again on every install, version change, bundle and app-token request, so a key
removed from the list stops its apps. Unsigned code runs only in development: Studio, `olan-app dev`
and "Olan'da dene" (`/apps/dev`), for people with the `developer` grant, under a "Geliştirme" label.

Who installs: catalog uploads are for admins, and an organization without an install policy is **admin only** by default until an admin lets members install (Olan → Yönetim → Uygulamalar).

Local development with your own Olan:

```sh
npx olan-app keygen --dev             # once: ~/.olan/olan-app-dev.key.json, prints the env line
# add the printed line to the local Platform API environment and restart it:
#   OLAN_APPS_TRUSTED_KEYS=dev-local=<your public key>
npx olan-app keys register            # or instead: register the key on the server (your development installations only)
npx olan-app validate --strict && npx olan-app test
npx olan-app pack --dev-sign          # dist/<id>-<version>.olanapp, signed with the development key
npx olan-app publish --org --dev-sign --server http://localhost:4000 --token "$OLAN_TOKEN"
olan app publish --org --dev-sign     # the same with the Olan CLI signed in (sets OLAN_TOKEN and --server)
npx olan-app try --server http://localhost:4000 --token "$OLAN_TOKEN"   # install it for your organization now
```

**Trying an app in your organization.** `olan-app try` packs and dev-signs like `pack --dev-sign`,
then uploads to `POST <server>/api/v2/apps/developer/try` (multipart field `package`, the same bearer
token as `publish --org`). The server installs it for your organization and answers
`{ installationId, appId, version }`; `try` prints `Open: <webOrigin>/apps/<installationId>`
(`webOrigin` from `/.well-known/olan`; without it, open Olan → Uygulamalar). `--json` result:
`{ server, endpoint, file, installationId, appId, version, appUrl, keyFingerprint }`. Refusals come
back as `try.<error>` (e.g. `try.developer_required`) or the package issue codes. Studio does the same
from a running `olan-app dev` ("Bu kurumda dene" uploads `GET /package`). **Developer keys:** instead of `OLAN_APPS_TRUSTED_KEYS`, register the key on the server once (`olan-app keys register`, or Studio → Geliştir → "Geliştirici anahtarları"). It vouches only for your own development installations (`try`) in your organization, while you are a member and until you revoke it; then they stop (`developer_key_revoked` / `developer_not_member`) but are not deleted. It never vouches for catalog uploads (`publish --org`), marketplace packages or other people.

**Development versions (`-dev.N`).** A version in the organization's catalog never changes. When you
try a changed build under a version the catalog already holds, the server answers
`409 version_exists` with `nextVersion`, the next free development prerelease of that app
(`1.2.0` → `1.2.0-dev.1`, then `1.2.0-dev.2`, …; a `-dev.N` version counts on from the same base).
`olan-app.json` is part of the signed digest, so the server cannot rename the package: `try` packs
and signs the same build again with `version` set to `nextVersion` and uploads it once more (the
`file` and `version` of the result name it; `olan-app.json` on disk is not changed). Studio asks the
dev server for `GET /package?version=<nextVersion>` and does the same. A second conflict, or a server
that names no `nextVersion`, is reported as `try.version_exists`: raise `version` yourself. To ask
first: `GET <server>/api/v2/apps/developer/try/next-version?appId=<id>&version=<version>` →
`{ appId, version }` (the version itself while the catalog does not hold it). The catalog upload
(`publish --org`) keeps a plain `version_exists`.

`/.well-known/olan` lists the fingerprints of the keys a server trusts
(`apps.trustedKeyFingerprints`); `pack` prints your key's fingerprint to compare. Never add a
development key to a production server. `olan-app keygen` without `--dev` writes a key into the
app (`olan-app.key.json`, git-ignored) for servers that are configured to trust it, such as an
offline test server.

**Internal: signing Olan's own apps.** Until Olan Marketplace signs packages itself, Olan signs its own apps with the marketplace key: `npx olan-app pack --no-sign`, then `npx olan-app sign --key <marketplace.pem> --key-id olan-marketplace-2026-10-17 dist/<id>-<version>.olanapp`. `sign` reads an unencrypted PKCS#8 Ed25519 PEM (`-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----`, e.g. `openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519`) and refuses other key types and encrypted keys, verifies the package digest, then writes `signature.json` (replacing an existing one; other files stay byte-identical). `--key-id` becomes `keyId`, the key's name on the server's trusted list (1-64 letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`); it is informational, servers trust the public key. The private key stays in memory only: never printed, logged, copied or stored. App developers use `pack --dev-sign` instead.

**Revocation lists (development).** Olan Marketplace signs the list of revoked apps; servers and
the mobile app refuse to open a revoked version. To try this locally:

```sh
echo '[{ "appId": "com.example.my-app", "versions": ["0.1.0"], "reason": "Test" }]' > list.json
npx olan-app revocations sign --dev --in list.json --out revocations.json
```

The output is `{ "payload": "<JSON text>", "signature": { "keyId": "dev-local", "algorithm": "ed25519", "signature": "…" } }`,
signed over the payload text with your development key. `--in` holds the entries (`appId`, then
`versions` or `packageSha256` or neither for every version, `reason`, `revokedAt`?) or
`{ issuedAt?, expiresAt?, sequence?, entries }`; missing values become now, now + 48 h and the time
in seconds. Only development builds accept such a list.

`publish` prints a warning (`publish.package_unsigned`, `publish.package_untrusted_key`) when the
server stored the version but will not install it. Server rejections come back as
`publish.<error>` (e.g. `publish.version_exists`: bump `version`) or the package issue codes.

## Olan Marketplace

The production path: `login --marketplace` once (browser sign-in or the Olan CLI; CI uses the saved session as `OLAN_MARKETPLACE_SESSION`), `developer create` once, `keys register` once per computer, then `test --report`, `publish --marketplace --test-report`, `status --marketplace`, `app set --age-rating` once and, after approval, `release`. Sign-in, the
marketplace address order, `--visibility`, the `--json` answers, `nextAction`, review levels and
every automatic check with its finding codes: marketplace.md. Error codes: errors.md#olan-marketplace.

## MCP server

`olan-app mcp` gives Claude Code and Codex the same tools over stdio:

```sh
claude mcp add olan-app -- npx olan-app mcp
```

```toml
# ~/.codex/config.toml
[mcp_servers.olan-app]
command = "npx"
args = ["olan-app", "mcp"]
```

| Tool | Input | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `olan_app_validate` | `{ dir?, strict? = true }` | validate result or errors |
| `olan_app_build` | `{ dir? }` | build result |
| `olan_app_test` | `{ dir?, pattern? }` | test summary |
| `olan_app_render` | `{ dir?, surface?, params?, permissions?, fixtures?, settings?, userId?, locale?, theme?, now? }` | `{ surface, tree, text, calls, toasts, navigation, errors }`; becomes the session |
| `olan_app_dispatch` | `{ action: 'press' \| 'fill' \| 'select' \| 'submit' \| 'back', label?, value? }` | the new view of the session |
| `olan_app_logs` | `{}` | session logs, errors, calls; last build and test |
| `olan_app_db` | `{ collection?, where?, limit? }` | the session's mock `olan.db`: collections with row counts and usage, or the rows of one collection (every user's, with owner), newest first (default 50, max 500) |
| `olan_app_event_send` | `{ type, dir?, to?, data?, installationId?, attempt?, id?, issuerPort? }` | the signed event, HTTP status and the app server's answer |
| `olan_app_tool_call` | `{ name, dir?, input?, to?, userId?, channel?, issuerPort? }` | the tool's answer (`{ ok, result \| error }`) |
| `olan_app_request_send` | `{ method, path, dir?, query?, body?, headers?, timeoutMs?, userId?, profile?, role?, to?, issuerPort? }` | the signed envelope, the app server's wrapper and what the app gets (`requests send`) |
| `olan_app_docs_search` | `{ query, limit? }` | matching doc sections |

Every tool answers `{ ok, result }` or `{ ok: false, errors }` as JSON text.

<!-- docs/marketplace.md -->
# Olan Marketplace

Apps reach production Olan servers through Olan Marketplace: automatic checks run on the package, a person reviews it, and the marketplace signs the approved version with the marketplace key.

```sh
npx olan-app login --marketplace --server https://api.example.com   # once: browser sign-in, 30-day session
npx olan-app developer create --marketplace --slug acme --name "Acme Ltd" --accept-agreement   # once
npx olan-app keys register --marketplace    # once per computer: your development key signs test reports
npx olan-app validate --strict && npx olan-app test --report test-report.json   # packs, then tests
npx olan-app publish --marketplace --test-report test-report.json   # submits, attaches, waits for the checks
npx olan-app status --marketplace com.example.my-app --wait-decision
npx olan-app app set --marketplace com.example.my-app --age-rating 4+   # once: required before release
npx olan-app release --marketplace com.example.my-app 1.0.0 --percent 10   # after approval
```

Reviewers apply review-guidelines.md (rule numbers like `2.1` in findings and rejections). **Studio** does the same in the browser: sign in to your Olan web app (e.g. `https://olan.example.com`) with an account that has developer access (the `developer` grant), open `<Olan web address>/tr/studio?section=publish` (Studio → Yayınla): developer accounts, store settings and page, submissions, test reports, releases.

## Signing in

The marketplace trusts your Olan server: `login` gets a 5-minute identity token from the server (`POST /api/v2/apps/marketplace/identity-token`; your account needs the `developer` grant from an admin) and exchanges it for a developer session. There are three ways to give `login` your Olan sign-in:

1. **Browser (default).** `olan-app login --marketplace --server <Olan API address>` opens the browser at the server's sign-in page (OAuth 2.0 authorization code with PKCE; the endpoints come from `<server>/.well-known/openid-configuration`, client `olan-app-cli`) and receives the answer on `http://127.0.0.1:<random port>/callback`. `--no-browser` only prints the address; open it in a browser **on the same computer** (the redirect goes to 127.0.0.1). The CLI waits 5 minutes.
2. **Olan CLI.** `olan app login --marketplace` with the Olan CLI signed in (`olan auth login`) passes your access token (`OLAN_TOKEN`) and server. Every `olan app …` command needs an Olan CLI that has the `app` command (`olan app --help` works; Olan Apps 4a release or newer); with an older `olan` use `npx olan-app …` and 1.
3. **CI.** Olan has no personal access tokens or API keys to create for CI, and `olan` does not print its token. CI uses a marketplace session instead: run `olan-app login --marketplace --server <api>` once on your computer (browser), then store the contents of `~/.olan/marketplace.json` (or only its `token`) as the CI secret `OLAN_MARKETPLACE_SESSION`; it replaces the file, lasts 30 days (sign in again and update the secret before `expiresAt`) and is all `publish`, `status`, `app`, `release`, `keys` need. `OLAN_TOKEN` / `--token` is only an input to `login` (an Olan access token the Olan CLI passes); CI never needs it.

The server is `--server`, else `OLAN_SERVER`, else `OLAN_API_URL` (the Olan CLI sets them). The session is saved in `~/.olan/marketplace.json` (`{ url, token, expiresAt, userRef, … }`, mode 0600; on Windows restricted to your user with `icacls`, best effort) and lasts 30 days. No token is ever printed or logged, and the session token is not accepted on the command line.

**Marketplace address**, first of: `--marketplace <url>`, `OLAN_MARKETPLACE_URL`, the saved session's marketplace (`publish`, `status`, `developer`), the server's `/.well-known/olan` `marketplaceUrl` (when a server is known: `login --server`, `OLAN_SERVER`, `OLAN_API_URL`), `https://marketplace.olan.app`.

## Developer accounts

Apps belong to a developer account (a person or a company); you can be a member of several.

- `olan-app developer create --marketplace [url] --slug <slug> --name <name> [--kind person|company] --accept-agreement` creates one and makes you its owner. `--slug` is the developer name in app pages (a-z, 0-9 and `-`, 2-63 characters; `olan…` is reserved). Creating an account accepts the current developer agreement; `--accept-agreement` is required and the CLI reads the version from `GET /api/v1/developer/me`.
- `olan-app developer list` shows your accounts, roles, agreement state and pending invites (invites are accepted in Studio → Yayınla).

## Publishing

- **publish.** A new app needs a developer account; `--developer <slug>` picks one when you have several. Existing apps get a new version (versions only go up). `--channel stable|beta [--percent N]` releases on approval. `--visibility public` (default) or `--visibility organization:<serverId>/<organizationId>` limits a new app to one organization on one Olan server; `--visibility org` fills both from the session (the server must be registered with the marketplace). Visibility is set when the app is created; later in Studio. `publish` waits while the checks run (`--no-wait` does not) and exits 1 with the findings on `checks_failed`. `--age-rating 4+|9+|13+` sets the app's age rating after uploading.
- **Version numbers.** A `checks_failed`, `rejected` or withdrawn version may be submitted again under the same number (it was never signed); one that is in review, approved or released may not (`version_exists`), and a new version must be higher than the latest (`version_not_increasing`). Organization catalog uploads (`publish --org`) always need a new number (manifest.md).
- **status.** Without a version: the newest. Prints the state, each check's status, the review level and reasons and `Next:` with the exact command (rejections too, on stderr before the findings). Exit 0 for `approved`, `checking`, `in_review`; 1 for `checks_failed`, `rejected`, `withdrawn`. `--wait-decision` polls every 5 s until a decision.
- **Store settings.** `olan-app app show --marketplace <appId>` and `olan-app app set --marketplace <appId> [--age-rating 4+|9+|13+] [--category <id>] [--platforms web,desktop,ios,android] [--support-url <url>] [--privacy-url <url>]` (developer role; `PATCH /api/v1/developer/apps/:appId`). Before the first release the change applies at once; for an app live in the public store it is reviewed first (`202 { pendingChange }`, printed as "in review"). Studio → Yayınla → the app → Mağaza sayfası is the same.
- **`--json`** prints the marketplace's answer unchanged (no `{ ok, … }` envelope): `publish` → `{ app, version, createdApp, submission }` (the submission as last polled; with `--test-report` also `testReport`; with `--age-rating` also `storeSettings`), `app` → `{ app, pendingChange? }`, `status` → `{ version, submission }`, `keys` → `{ key }` / `{ keys }`, `login` → `{ url, expiresAt, user, developers, sessionFile }`, `developer list` → `{ user, developers, agreement, invites }`, `developer create` → `{ developer }`, errors → `{ error, message, issues?, hint? }`.

## Releasing and rollout

After approval (`status` says `nextAction: release`), with an owner or admin role. **The app needs an age rating first** (4+, 9+ or 13+; guideline 5.4): `olan-app app set --marketplace <appId> --age-rating 4+`, `publish --marketplace --age-rating 4+`, or Studio → Yayınla → the app → Mağaza sayfası; without it `release` fails with `age_rating_required`.

- `olan-app release --marketplace [url] <appId> <version> [--channel stable|beta] [--percent N]`: publish to a channel (default `stable`, 100%). `--percent 10` is a staged rollout: only that share of servers get it (chosen deterministically per server). `beta` reaches only the organizations on the app's beta list (Studio → Yayınla).
- `olan-app rollout … --percent N`: widen it (10 → 50 → 100). It never narrows (`rollout_invalid`); it also resumes a halted rollout.
- `olan-app halt --marketplace <appId> <version>`: no new servers get the version; installed copies stay.
- `olan-app withdraw --marketplace <appId> <version>`: take back a submission still `checking` or `in_review`.

Each prints the marketplace answer with `--json` (`{ version }`, `withdraw`: `{ submission }`; errors `{ error, message }`) and exits 0 on success, 1 on failure (2: unknown option).

## Signed test reports

The marketplace cannot run your own tests (a package has no sources), so you attach their result, bound to the exact package and signed with your development key:

1. `olan-app keys register --marketplace [--developer <slug>] [--name <name>]` registers the public half of `~/.olan/olan-app-dev.key.json` (`OLAN_APP_DEV_KEY` overrides; created on first use) with the developer account. `keys list` and `keys remove <fingerprint>` manage them. (Without `--marketplace`, `keys register` registers the key on your Olan server for your development installations instead: cli.md.)
2. `olan-app test --report test-report.json` packs the app first (unsigned, into `.olan-app/report/`; a signature does not change `digest.package`), runs the whole suite and writes the report. Generate it **after** your last source change: `publish` packs the same sources to the same `digest.package`; a report for another build is refused (`test_report_mismatch`). `--package <file>` binds it to a package you packed yourself (for `publish --file`). Failing runs still write a report (and exit 1); reviewers see the failures.
3. `olan-app publish --marketplace --test-report test-report.json` checks the report locally, submits, then attaches it (`PUT …/versions/:version/test-report`, only while `checking`/`in_review`). `--json` adds `testReport` (`{ status: verified|unregistered_key, keyFingerprint, summary, failed }`).

The file is `{ payload, signature: { algorithm: "ed25519", publicKey, signature, keyId } }`: `payload` is the JSON text of `{ version: 1, appId, appVersion, packageSha256, generatedAt, tool: { cli, runner }, summary: { passed, failed, skipped, durationMs }, tests: [{ file, name, status, durationMs?, error? }] }`, signed over its UTF-8 bytes (`@olan-app/schema` `TestReportDocument`, `verifyTestReport`). A registered key shows as `verified` to reviewers, any other as `unregistered_key`.

## Submissions

A submission has `state`, `reviewLevel`, `reviewReasons`, `checks` (the report below), `rejection` (`{ rule, code, notes, findings }`), `release`, `testReport`, `notes` (reviewer notes) and `nextAction`. `checks` is null while checking, then `{ version: 1, passed, startedAt, finishedAt, usage: { rpcMethods, permissionsUsed, permissionsUnused, httpHosts }, checks: [{ id, status: passed|warning|failed|skipped, durationMs, findings: [{ check, code, severity, message, path?, rule?, hint? }] }] }` (`@olan/contracts` `OlanAppCheckReport`), one entry per check below.

| `nextAction` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `wait` | `checking` or `in_review`: automatic checks or a reviewer are working |
| `fix_and_resubmit` | `checks_failed` or `rejected`: fix the findings, publish again (same version allowed) |
| `release` | `approved` without a release: `olan-app release` (or Studio → Yayınla) |
| `none` | `approved` and released (on approval or with `olan-app release`) |
| `resubmit` | `withdrawn`: publish again |

`reviewLevel` is `light` or `full`. `reviewReasons` say why a review is full: `first_version`, `new_permissions` (permissions the last approved version did not have), `unverified_developer`, `security_findings` (a warning or error under guideline 1.x).

## Automatic checks

Every submission runs these checks on the package (the same static checks the marketplace shares with `@olan-app/schema`). `checks.passed` is false when any finding is an `error`; warnings go to the reviewer; `info` findings are notes. Each finding has `check`, `code`, `severity`, `message`, and often `path`, `rule` (the guideline, e.g. `2.1`) and `hint`.

| Check | Looks at | Common codes |
|---|---|---|
| `manifest` | `olan-app.json`, digest, signature and package layout (the server's install validation) | `manifest.*`, `package.*` (errors; the other checks are skipped) |
| `size` | Package and entry size (≤ 5 MiB) | `size.package_too_large` (error), `size.entry_large` (warning), `size.summary` (info) |
| `files` | File types in the package | `files.entry_missing`, `files.native_binary`, `files.type_not_allowed`, `files.svg_active_content` (errors), `files.source_map` (warning) |
| `permissions` | Declared permissions against `olan.*` calls in the bundle, in the backend (`dist/server.js`, since 1.5.1), during the render, and the event subscriptions and assistant tools that need them | `permissions.missing`, `permissions.http_missing` (errors), `permissions.unused`, `permissions.http_unused` (warnings), `permissions.http_hosts` (info) |
| `forbidden-apis` | Code the sandbox forbids (guideline 1.x) | `forbidden.eval`, `forbidden.function_constructor`, `forbidden.dynamic_import`, `forbidden.fetch`, `forbidden.xhr`, `forbidden.websocket`, `forbidden.dom`, `forbidden.browser_storage`, `forbidden.workers`, `forbidden.crypto_mining` (errors); `forbidden.navigator`, `forbidden.location`, `forbidden.require`, `obfuscation.*` (warnings) |
| `surfaces` | Renders every declared surface with sample data | `surfaces.not_rendered`, `surfaces.load_error`, `surfaces.timeout`, `surfaces.unknown_method`, `surfaces.limit_exceeded`, `surfaces.app_error` (errors; `surfaces.runner_failed` is the marketplace's own failure: publish again); `surfaces.empty`, `surfaces.root_not_screen`, `surfaces.not_settled` (warnings) |
| `interaction` | Presses the buttons and menus of each rendered surface | `interaction.app_error` (error), `interaction.summary` (info), `interaction.developer_tests_unavailable` (info; `interaction.developer_tests_reported` once a test report is attached) |
| `accessibility` | Labels and keys in the rendered trees (guideline 4.x) | `a11y.button_label_missing`, `a11y.field_label_missing`, `a11y.action_label_missing`, `a11y.menu_item_label_missing` (errors); `a11y.image_alt_missing`, `a11y.menu_label_missing`, `a11y.list_key_missing`, `a11y.duplicate_key` (warnings) |
| `licenses` | License files and notices in the bundle (guideline 6.x) | `licenses.found` (info), `licenses.notices_missing` (info), `licenses.copyleft` (warning) |

`validate --strict` catches most of these before you submit. `interaction.developer_tests_unavailable` is always informational: a package does not contain your source, so your own `olan-app test` suites cannot run on the marketplace; attach a signed test report instead (above). The checks may finish before the report arrives; once it is attached the note reads `interaction.developer_tests_reported` with the report's counts. What each `rule` means and how to fix it: review-guidelines.md. `olan-app build` keeps the license comments of bundled code (React, MIT) at the end of `dist/app.js` and `dist/server.js`, which satisfies `licenses.notices_missing`; extra notices go in a `NOTICE` or `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES` file under `assets/` (only `assets/**` is packed).

Marketplace error codes (`marketplace.<code>`) are listed in errors.md#olan-marketplace.

<!-- docs/review-guidelines.md -->
# Olan App Review Guidelines (summary)

Every app submitted to Olan Marketplace follows these rules, public and organization-only apps alike. Rule numbers are stable: automatic check findings (`rule`), rejections (`rejection.rule` in `olan-app status --json`) and `validate --strict` findings (`(guideline 2.1)`) cite them.

## How review works

- **Automatic checks first** (minutes; marketplace.md#automatic-checks). Any `error` finding ends the submission as `checks_failed` without a human review: fix it and publish again.
- **A person reviews every version**; nothing is approved automatically, organization-only apps included. **Full review**: the first version, a version that asks for a new permission or host, an unverified developer, security findings (1.x). **Light review**: everything else (`reviewLevel`, `reviewReasons`).
- **Store page changes** (listing text, age rating, category, links) of a live public app go live after a quick review (7.x; `olan-app app set` prints "in review"); for organization-only apps they apply at once.
- **Approval signs** the package with the Olan Marketplace key; Olan can stop a signed app on every server (revocation list).
- **A rejection names the rule.** A rejected or `checks_failed` version was never signed, so its version number may be submitted again; an approved or released number may not.

## Rules

| Rule | What it means | Typical findings | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.1 No obfuscation | Minified code is fine; deliberately obscured code, encrypted or encoded payloads and code decoded at run time are not | `obfuscation.*` | Ship the plain output of `olan-app build` |
| 1.2 No dynamic code | No `eval`, `new Function`, dynamic `import()` or downloaded code: the behaviour is in the reviewed package | `forbidden.eval`, `forbidden.function_constructor`, `forbidden.dynamic_import` | Static imports; data, not code, from the network |
| 1.3 No native binaries | Only JavaScript, JSON, images and text (`.so`, `.dex`, `.jar`, `.wasm`, `.hbc`, `.node`, `.exe`, `.dylib` are refused) | `files.native_binary`, `files.type_not_allowed` | Remove them from `assets/` |
| 1.4 Only `olan.*` | No direct `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `WebSocket`, DOM, `localStorage`, `navigator` or sandbox escapes; device APIs (location, camera, contacts) are not available | `forbidden.fetch`, `forbidden.dom`, `forbidden.browser_storage`, `surfaces.unknown_method` | `olan.http.fetch`, `olan.storage`, SDK components (api.md) |
| 1.5 No mining or abuse | The app does not use the device or the Olan server for anything but its purpose | `forbidden.crypto_mining` | Remove it |
| 2.1 Least privilege | Every permission backs a visible feature; no unused permissions; `*:delete` never deletes without asking the person | `permissions.missing`, `permissions.unused` | Declare what you call, drop the rest; `olan.ui.confirm` before deleting (examples.md#confirm-before-a-destructive-action) |
| 2.2 Honest data-use declaration | The store page's data declaration (data, purposes, third parties) matches what the app does | Reviewer | Update the listing in Studio → Yayınla |
| 2.3 Justified network access | `http:<host>` only for hosts the app's job needs, each named in the declaration; no personal data leaves Olan without consent | `permissions.http_missing`, `permissions.http_unused`, `permissions.http_hosts` (info) | Grant only the hosts you fetch; explain each in the listing |
| 2.4 KVKK and GDPR | Apps that process personal data give a privacy policy URL and honour deletion and export requests; sensitive data (health, ID numbers) needs a separate justification | Reviewer | `olan-app app set --marketplace <appId> --privacy-url <https url>` |
| 3.1 Every surface opens | Each declared surface opens with sample data without errors | `surfaces.*` | `olan-app validate --strict`; render an `EmptyState` rather than nothing |
| 3.2 Headless tests | Your `olan-app test` suites pass; a signed test report (key registered with the account) shows reviewers your results, failures included | `interaction.developer_tests_unavailable`, `interaction.developer_tests_reported` (info) | `olan-app test --report r.json`, `publish --marketplace --test-report r.json` (marketplace.md#signed-test-reports) |
| 3.3 No crash on interaction | Pressing buttons and submitting forms raises no error; failures show the person a clear message | `interaction.app_error` | Catch failures; show a toast or an `EmptyState` |
| 4.1 Labelled controls | Every button, menu, menu item, action and form field has a label | `a11y.button_label_missing`, `a11y.field_label_missing`, `a11y.action_label_missing`, `a11y.menu_item_label_missing` | Give each a `label`, even with an icon |
| 4.2 Image descriptions | Meaningful images have alternative text | `a11y.image_alt_missing` | Add `alt` |
| 5.1 Not misleading | Name, description, screenshots and the app tell the same story | Reviewer; `manifest.description_template` (warning) | Write your own `description` |
| 5.2 Not impersonating Olan | No Olan name, logo or design imitation; `com.olan.*`, `app.olan.*`, `olan.*` ids are Olan's | `app_id_reserved` | Choose your own id and branding |
| 5.3 User content | Apps that show user or AI-generated content offer filtering, reporting and blocking | Reviewer | Add those controls |
| 5.4 Correct age rating | 4+, 9+ or 13+ matching the content; Olan is rated 13+, so 16+ and 18+ apps are not accepted. Required before release | `age_rating_required`, `age_rating_not_allowed` | `olan-app app set --marketplace <appId> --age-rating 4+` (or Studio) |
| 6.1 License notices kept | Notices of bundled third-party code stay in the package | `licenses.notices_missing` (info) | `olan-app build` keeps them; more in `assets/NOTICE` |
| 6.2 Copyleft reviewed | GPL, AGPL, LGPL, SSPL code is reviewed separately | `licenses.copyleft` (warning) | Explain it in the review notes, or replace it |
| 7.1 Accurate store page | Screenshots are from the real app; the description is complete in TR or EN | Reviewer | Studio → Yayınla → store page |
| 7.2 Working support and privacy links | Both open and belong to the app | Reviewer | `olan-app app set --marketplace <appId> --support-url … --privacy-url …` |
| 8.1 Organization-only apps | The same rules and a person reviews every version; only visibility differs and store page changes apply without review. The submitter signs in through that organization's verified Olan server as an admin or developer | `organization_not_allowed`, `server_not_verified` | `olan-app login --marketplace --server <that server>` |

Every app page has "Bildir" (report); Olan may revoke a version or the whole app after a report and tells the developer why. Legal terms (developer agreement, data processing) are separate documents.

<!-- docs/errors.md -->
# Error codes

## Run time: `OlanError.code`

| Code | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `permission_denied` | The installation did not grant the permission the call needs | Add it to `permissions` (permissions.md); handle the error with an `EmptyState` |
| `http_blocked` | `olan.http.fetch` to a host without `http:<host>`, a private address, or (tests) a URL without an HTTP fixture | Add `http:<host>`; add the URL to `fixtures/http.json` |
| `invalid_params` | Bad arguments: storage value > 64 KiB, `json()` on a non-JSON body, unknown `olan.db` collection, `where`/`orderBy` on a field that is not indexed, `limit` outside 1–100, a cursor from another query | Check the arguments (database.md#queries) |
| `validation_failed` | An `olan.db` row does not match the manifest `data` schema; `message` is `"data.<field>: row.<code>"` (`row.unknown_field`, `row.required`, `row.type`, `row.max_length`, `row.range`, `row.enum`, `row.not_integer`, `row.json_too_large`, `row.too_large`), `"data.<field>: ref.not_found"` (the referenced project, task or user does not exist or is not visible; on `insert` and on changed `update` fields), `ref.too_many` (> 20 references per call); or a card is invalid (`card.*`, below) | Fix the value of that field |
| `conflict` | Stale `revision` in `olan.db` `update`/`delete`, `updateTask`, `deleteTask` or `deleteList` (older servers: `invalid_params`) | Reload (`get`/`refetch`) and retry with the new `revision` |
| `not_found` | The row, task or work package does not exist (any more) | Refetch the list |
| `forbidden_record` | A protected record (default work package, non-empty work package, task with an approval workflow, a record the app did not create when the admin requires that; Olan meetings, project calendar events and shared contacts `system_record`; invitations `not_organizer`; read-only calendars `permission_denied`; a project the app did not create `not_created_by_app`) or an `olan.db` row the collection's `rules` do not allow this user to change | Show "Bu kayıt korunuyor"; do not retry |
| `quota_exceeded` | The installation's database is full (rows or bytes) | Ask an admin to raise the limit, or delete rows |
| `not_installed` | The app is not installed (or was disabled) for this user | Nothing to do in code |
| `unknown_method` | The host does not know the call (older Olan) | Check `olan.*` names; require a newer server with `minServerVersion` |
| `host_error` | The host failed, or `olan.*` was called before the runtime started (e.g. at module top level) | Call `olan.*` from effects, handlers or `useQuery` |
| `cancelled` | The app was closed while the call was pending | Ignore |
| `backend_function_not_found` | `olan.backend.call(name)`: the backend has no `functions[name]` | Add it to `defineBackend({ functions })` (backend.md) |
| `backend_error` | The backend function threw (`message` is its error) or `dist/server.js` does not load | Fix the function; check the logs (Studio → Backend, `olan-app dev`) |
| `backend_limit` | The backend call ran out of CPU (1 s), time (10 s) or memory (64 MiB) | Do less per call; move periodic work to `schedules` |
| `backend_busy` | More than 4 backend calls at once for this installation | Retry later |
| `payload_too_large` | `backend.call` arguments or result over 256 KiB | Send ids, page results |
| `backend_unavailable` | The app has no `server`, or backends are off on this server | Declare `server`; ask the admin |
| `backend_migrating` | After an update, the new version's `migrate` has not succeeded yet (retried with backoff, then by hand) | Retry later; fix `migrate` (Studio → Backend shows the error) |
| `remote_rejected` | `olan.remote.request`: the app server answered 400–499; `RemoteError.status` is its status, `details` its body (remote-requests.md) | Show the server's reason (e.g. 422 `issues` per field); do not retry unchanged |
| `remote_unavailable` | `olan.remote.request`: the app server answered 500–599 (`reason: 'http_status'`) or gave no usable answer: `timeout`, `network`, `invalid_response` (not HTTP 200 with the `{ status, headers?, body? }` wrapper), `response_too_large` (> 4 MiB) | A `Banner` with "Tekrar dene"; on the server, check the `/requests` route and the wrapper |
| `consent_required` | The person has not consented to the app yet (remote requests) | Nothing in code: Olan shows the consent screen on the next open |
| `rate_limited` | Over 300 remote requests a minute (or 8 at once) per person and installation; `RemoteError.retryAfterSeconds` | Wait and retry; poll less often |
| `feature_not_enabled` | The organization's plan does not include this app (`details.feature` on the server) | Nothing in code; an admin changes the plan |
| `payload_too_large` | Also: a `remote.request` body over 1 MiB | Send less, or upload files with `olan.files.upload` |
| `upload_failed` | `olan.files.upload`: network error, or no progress for 60 s | Offer to retry the upload |
| `project_not_enabled` | SDK 1.6: the call names a project the app was not added to (`olan.projects.*`, `olan.project.*`) | Say "Uygulama bu projeye eklenmemiş"; a member adds it on the project page → Uygulamalar |

`olan.project.*` (SDK 1.7) map the server's reasons to these codes; the reason is in `message`:
`not_found` — `link_not_found`, `status_not_found`, `label_not_found`, `calendar_item_not_found`,
`approval_not_found`, `field_not_found`, `task_not_found`, `issue_not_found` (refetch); `validation_failed` —
`invalid_card` (a record card with a `submit` button or another card problem: use `{ kind: 'open' }`);
`conflict` — `status_key_taken`, `label_key_taken`, `field_key_taken`, `status_name_taken`, `label_name_taken`,
`field_name_taken` (the project already uses the key or name: pick another), `field_read_only` (the field's app was
removed from the project), `approval_not_pending` (already decided or cancelled),
`last_status_in_category` (the project keeps one status of each required kind), `project_archived`;
`quota_exceeded` — `record_links_limit` (10 records per task or issue), `calendar_items_limit` (500 per
project), `fields_limit` (50 fields per project); `invalid_params` — `invalid_key`, `invalid_definitions`, `status_category_immutable`,
`invalid_target`, `invalid_status`, `invalid_state`, `invalid_range`, `invalid_approvers` (not a
member who may change the project), `invalid_text`, and for fields `invalid_field_type`, `field_type_immutable`,
`invalid_field_options`, `invalid_field` (no such field for that task or issue), `invalid_field_value`, `field_required`.
| `cancelled` | Also: an upload stopped with `task.cancel()` / `olan.files.cancel` | Expected after your own cancel; reset the progress UI |
| `http_blocked` | Also: an upload `url` that is not on the `remote.url` origin or a granted `http:<host>` (or `http:` outside development) | Upload to your app server's origin (files.md#where-uploads-may-go) |

## `olan-app validate`

Each error has `code`, `message`, `file`, `line`/`column` when known, and a `hint`.

### Manifest (`olan-app.json`)

| Code | Fix |
|---|---|
| `manifest.missing` | Create `olan-app.json` (`olan-app init`, or copy manifest.md) |
| `manifest.invalid_json` / `manifest.not_object` | Fix the JSON syntax; the file is one object |
| `manifest.unknown_field` | Remove the field (only the fields in manifest.md exist) |
| `manifest.feature_not_available` | This server turned backend code off (`OLAN_APPS_BACKEND=0`; locally the same variable): remove `server`, or use your own server (`remote`, server.md) or `olan.http.fetch` |
| `manifest.schema_version` | `"schemaVersion": 1` |
| `manifest.id` | Lowercase reverse domain: `"com.example.my-app"` |
| `manifest.name` | 1–80 characters |
| `manifest.version` | Semver: `"0.1.0"` |
| `manifest.sdk` | `"^1.5.0"` |
| `manifest.schema_url` | `$schema` is `"https://olan.app/schemas/olan-app/v1.json"`, or remove it |
| `manifest.min_server_version` | Semver, or remove it |
| `manifest.description` | ≤ 400 characters |
| `manifest.entry` / `manifest.entry_required` | `"entry": "dist/app.js"` |
| `manifest.icon` | A png/svg/jpg/webp path in the package, e.g. `"assets/icon.png"` |
| `manifest.kind` | `"app"` or `"web-link"` |
| `manifest.surfaces_required` | `"surfaces": { "app": { "title": "…" } }` |
| `manifest.surface_unknown` | Use a surface from surfaces.md |
| `manifest.surface_invalid` | `app`/`project.widget`/`settings`: `{ "title"?: string }`; other surfaces need `"title"` (1–80); `chat.command` `description` ≤ 120 |
| `manifest.project_template_invalid` | `projectTemplates`: ≤ 5 `{ key, name, description?, content }` with unique keys; `content` is `{ version: 1, lists, statuses?, labels?, tasks?, recordTemplates?, settings? }` (manifest.md#projecttemplates) |
| `manifest.command_invalid` | `chat.command` needs `"command"`: `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, e.g. `"standup"` |
| `manifest.permissions` / `manifest.permission_unknown` | Use a permission from permissions.md or `http:<host>` (no scheme or path); `remote` and `ai:tools` are implied, never listed |
| `manifest.permission_reserved` | The permission is reserved for a later phase (none today) |
| `manifest.remote_invalid_url` | `remote` is `{ "url", "jwksUrl", "requests"? }`: https URLs without credentials, query or fragment (http only for localhost/private addresses); `requests` a boolean |
| `manifest.profile_requires_remote` | `profile:read` only adds fields to remote requests: add `"remote": { "url", "jwksUrl", "requests": true }`, or remove `profile:read` |
| `manifest.events_require_remote`, `manifest.ai_tools_require_remote` | Add `remote`: events and tools go to the app's own server |
| `manifest.event_unknown` | Use an event type from server.md#events |
| `manifest.event_permission_missing` | Add the permission the event needs (`detail: { event, permission }`) |
| `manifest.ai_tool_invalid` | Tool `name` `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,31}$` and unique, `description` 1–1024, `input` a JSON Schema with `"type": "object"` (≤ 8 KiB, only `#…` `$ref`), not both `readOnly` and `destructive`, ≤ 16 tools; `timeoutMs` an integer 1000–60000, at most 15000 on a `readOnly` tool |
| `manifest.ai_tool_permission_missing` | A tool's `permissions` must also be in the manifest's `permissions` |
| `manifest.web_link_remote` | Web links have no `remote`, `events`, `ai` or `server` |
| `manifest.server_invalid` | Fix `server` (`entry` a .ts/.js path in the package, `schedules` cron ≥ 5 minutes apart and unique names, `hooks` `verify` with `header` and a `secret: true` `secretSetting`) |
| `manifest.permission_duplicate` | Remove the repeated permission |
| `manifest.settings_field` | Fix the settings field: `type`, `label`, `default` of the right type, `select` with `options` containing the default |
| `manifest.url` / `manifest.url_required` / `manifest.url_not_allowed` | `url` only for `kind: "web-link"` |
| `manifest.web_link_entry` / `_surface` / `_permissions` / `_settings` / `_data` | Web links have none of these |
| `manifest.data_version` | `data.version` is an integer 1–1000000; increase it when the schema changes |
| `manifest.data_collections_required` | `data` is `{ "version", "collections" }` with at least one collection |
| `manifest.data_collection_name` / `manifest.data_collection_limit` | Collection names `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$`; at most 20 |
| `manifest.data_scope` | `"scope": "organization"` or `"user"` |
| `manifest.data_field_name` / `manifest.data_field_reserved` / `manifest.data_field_limit` | Field names `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}$`, not `id`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `createdBy`, `revision`; at most 64 |
| `manifest.data_field_type` | `type`: `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `json`, `ref:project`, `ref:task`, `ref:user` |
| `manifest.data_field_option` | An option the type does not have (e.g. `maxLength` on a number) or a bad value (`maxLength` 1–10000, `enum` 1–100 unique strings, `min` ≤ `max`) |
| `manifest.data_index_limit` / `manifest.data_index_type` | At most 5 `indexed` fields; `json` cannot be indexed, strings only with `maxLength` ≤ 512 or `enum` |
| `manifest.data_rules` | `rules` only on `organization` collections; values `"any"` or `"owner"` |
| `manifest.invalid` | Other schema error; read the message |

### Build and files

| Code | Fix |
|---|---|
| `build.entry_missing` | Create `src/app.tsx` with `export default defineApp({ … })` |
| `build.sdk_missing` | `npm install` |
| `build.error` | Syntax or import error at `file:line`; "Could not resolve" → install the package or fix the path |
| `build.forbidden_import` | Remove imports of `react-dom`, `react-native`, Node built-ins or `@olan-app/cli` from `src/` |
| `build.manifest_invalid` (warning) | `build` ran although `olan-app.json` has errors; run `olan-app validate` |
| `build.warning` (warning) | esbuild warning; usually a real bug |
| `build.too_large` (warning), `validate.bundle_too_large`, `validate.package_too_large` | Bundle/package over 5 MiB: drop big dependencies (`olan-app build --json` → `largestInputs`) or assets |
| `validate.entry_missing` | Run `olan-app build` (or drop `--no-build`) |
| `validate.icon_missing` | Add the icon file or remove `"icon"` |
| `validate.typescript_missing` (warning) | `npm install -D typescript` |
| `build.backend_node_import` | Backend code (`server/`) imported a Node module (`fs`, `crypto`, `node:*`, `axios`, …): use `olan.http.fetch`, `olan.db`, `olan.secrets` (backend.md) |
| `build.backend_forbidden_import` | Backend code may import only `@olan-app/sdk/backend` from the SDK, no React and no `@olan-app/cli` |
| `build.backend_entry_missing`, `build.backend_missing` | Create `server.entry` (`export default defineBackend({ … })`) |
| `build.backend_error` | Syntax or import error in backend code at `file:line` |
| `build.backend_large` (warning) | `dist/server.js` is over 1 MiB; every new sandbox loads it |
| `validate.backend_missing` | `dist/server.js` does not exist: run `olan-app build` (or drop `--no-build`) |
| `validate.backend_load`, `validate.backend_default_export` | `dist/server.js` does not load in the backend runtime (a top-level throw, a Node API at the top level) or has no `export default defineBackend(...)` |
| `validate.backend_handler_missing` | A `server.schedules`/`events`/`hooks` entry has no handler: add `schedules[name]`/`events[type]`/`hooks[name]` or `functions[<its function>]` (backend.md#handler-resolution) |
| `validate.backend_handler_unused` (warning) | `defineBackend` has a schedule, event or hook handler the manifest does not declare, so Olan never runs it |
| `backend.engine` (warning) | The backend engine fell back (`isolated-vm prebuild not available on <platform>; using QuickJS (slower)`) |
| `backend.engine_unavailable`, `backend.runtime_missing` | `--engine isolated-vm` cannot start here: use `--engine quickjs` or `auto`; reinstall `@olan-app/cli` |
| `typescript.TS<n>` | A type error at `file:line` (e.g. `typescript.TS2322`: wrong prop type, `TS2741`: missing required prop) |
| `typescript.failed` | `tsc` could not run; read the message |

### `--strict`: rendering every surface

| Code | Fix |
|---|---|
| `app.default_export` | End `src/app.tsx` with `export default defineApp({ app: MyScreen })` |
| `app.surface_missing` | The manifest declares a surface `defineApp` does not define: add it or remove it from `surfaces` |
| `app.surface_undeclared` (warning) | Declare the surface in `olan-app.json` or remove it from `defineApp` |
| `runtime.load_failed` | `src/app.tsx` throws at import time (top-level code); move it into components |
| `runtime.render_failed` / `runtime.error` | The surface threw while rendering with the default fixtures. "`fetch`/`window`/`document`/`localStorage` is not defined" → use `olan.*`; otherwise guard missing data (`data?.items ?? []`) |
| `runtime.unknown_method` | Use only the `olan.*` calls in api.md |
| `permission.missing` | A write in a handler (found in `src/`, at `file:line`) or a backend call needs a permission the manifest lacks: add it. `olan.files.*` needs `files:pick`; `olan.remote.request` needs `"requests": true` in `remote` |
| `fixtures.db_invalid`, `fixtures.db_unknown_collection` | A row in `fixtures/db.json` does not match its collection in `data.collections`, or names a collection the manifest does not declare; fix the row or the collection name (rendering continues on an empty database) |
| `fixtures.http_missing` (warning) | Add the URL to `fixtures/http.json` so headless runs get a response |
| `fixtures.remote_missing` (warning) | Add the route to `fixtures/remote.json` (or pass `renderApp({ remote })`) so `olan.remote.request` gets an answer |
| `tree.unknown_type` | Only the 23 SDK components exist; no `<div>`, `<span>`, `<img>` (use `Image`). An Olan server before 1.5 reports it for the SDK 1.5 components |
| `tree.unknown_prop` | Remove the prop (no `style`, `className`, `color`, `onClick` — it is `onPress`) |
| `tree.invalid_prop` | Wrong value: check the allowed values in components.md (e.g. `gap="16"` → `gap="md"`, missing required `label`, `Menu` without `label` and `icon`, `format: 'currency'` without `currency`, `Tabs` with fewer than 2 or more than 8 items, `stacked` on a line chart, an `Image` `src` that is not an http(s) URL) |
| `tree.text_outside_text` | Wrap strings and numbers in `<Text>` |
| `tree.children_not_allowed` | Only `Screen`, `Stack`, `Card`, `Form` take children; `Text` takes text; `List`, `Button`, `Badge` … take none (use props) |
| `tree.text_invalid` | Text nodes carry one string |
| `tree.child_missing`, `tree.cycle`, `tree.shared_child`, `tree.root_missing`, `tree.id_mismatch`, `tree.invalid_node` | Internal tree errors; report them with the app source |
| `ui.empty_tree` (warning) | The surface rendered nothing; render an `EmptyState` instead of `null` |
| `ui.root_not_screen` (warning) | Start `app`/`settings` surfaces with `<Screen>` (only these two are checked; `project.widget` uses `Card`, modals and panels should use `Screen`) |

### `--strict`: Olan Marketplace review checks

The marketplace's static checks (`@olan-app/schema` `runStaticReviewChecks`, `reviewPermissions`,
`lintUiTree`) on the files `pack` would package, merged with the calls the surfaces made: the same
codes, severities and guideline (`rule`, explained in review-guidelines.md) the marketplace reports (marketplace.md#automatic-checks).
Errors fail `validate`, warnings print, info findings show with `--verbose` (`--json`: `result.review`).

| Code | Fix |
|---|---|
| `permissions.missing` | Add the named permission (or remove the call); with a `file:line` in `src/` when the source scan found the call |
| `permissions.http_missing` | `olan.http.fetch` without `http:<host>`, or a fetched host not granted: add `http:<host>` |
| `permissions.unused`, `permissions.http_unused` (warnings) | Remove permissions nothing uses. Counted as use: `olan.*` calls in `dist/app.js` and, with `server`, in `dist/server.js` (SDK 1.5.1; before, backend-only use was not seen), event subscriptions (`events`, `server.events`) and `ai.tools[].permissions`. What your own server (`remote`) does with its tokens is not visible: the reviewer reads your listing |
| `permissions.http_hosts` (info) | The hosts the app may call; the listing must explain each |
| `a11y.button_label_missing`, `a11y.field_label_missing`, `a11y.menu_item_label_missing`, `a11y.action_label_missing` | Give every `Button`, field (also `Switch`, `MultiSelect`), menu item and action (also a `Banner` action) a non-empty `label` |
| `a11y.tab_label_missing` | Every `Tabs` item needs a non-empty `label`; the `Tabs` `label` (the group's name) is optional but not empty |
| `a11y.avatar_name_missing` | Give every `Avatar` the person's or brand's `name` (read aloud, and the initials) |
| `a11y.menu_label_missing`, `a11y.image_alt_missing` (warnings) | Add `label` to icon-only menus; `alt` to images (`""` only for decoration) |
| `a11y.list_key_missing`, `a11y.duplicate_key` (warnings) | Every `List` item needs a unique `key`; make `Menu` item, `Table` row and action keys unique |
| `forbidden.*` (e.g. `forbidden.eval`, `forbidden.function_constructor`, `forbidden.dom`, `forbidden.fetch`) | Remove the API from the bundle (`dist/app.js#line:column`); use `olan.*` and SDK components |
| `files.native_binary`, `files.type_not_allowed`, `files.svg_active_content`, `files.entry_missing`, `files.source_map` (warning) | Package only JS, JSON, images, text; plain SVGs; no source maps |
| `size.package_too_large`, `size.entry_large` (warning), `size.summary` (info) | Stay ≤ 5 MiB; keep the entry under 2 MiB |
| `licenses.copyleft` (warning), `licenses.found`, `licenses.notices_missing` (info) | Copyleft code gets manual review; `olan-app` keeps license comments at the end of `dist/app.js` |

### Data schema changes (install and update)

The server compares the new `data` with the stored one: `409 data_schema_incompatible` with
`issues`. Fix: keep the change additive and increase `data.version` (database.md#changing-the-schema).

| Code | Fix |
|---|---|
| `data.version_not_bumped` | The schema changed: increase `data.version` |
| `data.version_downgrade` | `data.version` must not go down |
| `data.collection_removed`, `data.field_removed` | Keep it (stop using it instead) |
| `data.type_changed`, `data.scope_changed` | Add a new field or collection instead |
| `data.required_added` | Add the field as optional |
| `data.constraint_tightened` | Keep `maxLength`/`max` as large, `min` as small, every `enum` value, no new `integer` |

## Other commands

| Code | Fix |
|---|---|
| `cli.unknown_command`, `cli.unknown_option`, `cli.missing_value`, `cli.invalid_option` | See `olan-app <command> --help` (exit code 2) |
| `cli.internal` | An unexpected failure; the message (and the stack without `--json`) says where |
| `project.not_found` | Run inside an app directory or pass `--cwd` |
| `test.none` | Add `tests/*.test.ts` with at least one `test(...)` |
| `test.build_error` | The test file does not compile; see `file:line` |
| `test.failed` | Assertion or app failure; the message includes the visible text |
| `test.process_crashed` (warning) | Every test of the file passed, then its process exited with a non-zero code (on Windows often `0xC0000409`, the Node/libuv abort while sockets close); not counted as a failure. Rerun; if it repeats, look for `process.exit()` or aborts in `after()` hooks |
| `test.report_pattern`, `test.package_without_report` | A report covers the whole suite (drop the pattern); `--package` needs `--report` |
| `test.report_too_many`, `test.report_too_large`, `test.report_invalid` | A report holds ≤ 2000 tests and ≤ 512 KiB; shorten names or split the suite |
| `test.report_package_stale` (warning) | `dist/<id>-<version>.olanapp` is another build than the report's package: pack again before `publish --file` |
| `package.missing`, `package.unreadable` | `--package` must be a `.olanapp` made by `olan-app pack` |
| `fixtures.invalid_json`, `fixtures.invalid`, `fixtures.users_invalid` | Fix the fixture file (testing.md#fixtures; users need `id`, `displayName`, `email`) |
| `init.name_required`, `init.name_too_long`, `init.invalid_id`, `init.not_empty`, `init.unknown_template`, `init.template_conflict` | Fix the `init` arguments (`--backend` is the `backend` template; it cannot be combined with another `--template`) |
| `pack.key_missing`, `pack.key_invalid` | Run `olan-app keygen` or pass a valid `--sign-key` (`--dev-sign` creates the development key itself) |
| `pack.validation_failed` | `pack` ran the `validate` checks and found the errors listed after it: fix them (and run `validate --strict`); `--no-validate` packages anyway |
| `pack.sign_conflict` | `--dev-sign` signs with the development key; drop `--sign-key`/`--no-sign` |
| `pack.entry_missing`, `pack.icon_missing`, `pack.unsafe_path`, `pack.too_large`, `pack.web_link`, `pack.signature_failed` | Fix the files named in the message |
| `pack.version_invalid` | The version to package (`olan-app try`'s server-named `-dev.N`) is not semver: check the server's `nextVersion` |
| `pack.backend_missing` | The manifest has `server` but `dist/server.js` is missing: run `olan-app build` |
| `keygen.exists` | Keep the key, or `--force` to replace it |
| `keygen.dev_out` | `--dev` keeps the key in `~/.olan`; set `OLAN_APP_DEV_KEY` for another file |
| `sign.key_required`, `sign.key_missing`, `sign.key_invalid`, `sign.key_encrypted`, `sign.key_not_ed25519`, `sign.key_id_invalid` | Internal `olan-app sign`: pass `--key` with an unencrypted PKCS#8 Ed25519 PEM; `--key-id` is 1-64 letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-` |
| `sign.package_required`, `sign.package_missing`, `sign.package_invalid`, `sign.package_too_large`, `sign.digest_missing`, `sign.digest_invalid`, `sign.digest_mismatch`, `sign.signature_failed` | Pass one package made by `olan-app pack`; if it changed after packing, pack it again |
| `validate.unsigned` (warning, `--strict`) | Nothing to do for `publish --marketplace` (the marketplace signs approved versions). For an organization catalog (`publish --org`) a plain `pack` is unsigned and not installable: `olan-app pack --dev-sign` / `publish --org --dev-sign` locally with your development key (`keygen --dev`; cli.md#signing-and-publishing) |
| `manifest.description_template` (warning, `--strict`) | `description` is still the `olan-app init` template's: describe your app (guideline 5.1) |
| `publish.target_required` | Pass `--marketplace` (production, marketplace.md) or `--org` (development servers) |
| `publish.target_conflict`, `publish.marketplace_option` | Use one target; `--developer`, `--channel`, `--percent`, `--visibility` are for `--marketplace` only |
| `publish.server_required`, `publish.token_required` | Use `olan app publish --org` (signed in), or pass `--server` and `--token`/`OLAN_TOKEN` |
| `publish.network` | Check `--server` (the API address) |
| `publish.test_report_missing`, `publish.test_report_invalid` | `--test-report` must be the JSON file `olan-app test --report <file>` wrote |
| `publish.file_missing` | The `--file` package does not exist; run `olan-app pack` or drop `--file` |
| `publish.apps_disabled` | Olan Apps are turned off on that server |
| `publish.dev_sign_file` | `--dev-sign` packs and signs; drop `--file` (or upload a package you packed with `pack --dev-sign`) |
| `publish.package_unsigned` (warning) | Uploaded but unsigned, so it cannot be installed. Locally: `publish --dev-sign` and trust the key (`keygen --dev`); production installs need Olan Marketplace signing |
| `publish.package_untrusted_key` (warning) | Uploaded, but the server does not trust the signing key; on a development server add it to `OLAN_APPS_TRUSTED_KEYS` |
| `publish.<server error>` | e.g. `publish.version_exists` (bump `version`), `publish.forbidden`/`admin_required` (admins only), `publish.invalid_token` (sign in again); package issues come with their own codes (`package.*`, `manifest.*`) |
| `docs.query_required`, `docs.sdk_missing` | Pass a query; `npm install` |
| `dev.port_in_use` | Stop the other server or `--port <n>` |
| `dev.remote_missing` | `dev --remote live` needs `remote` (with `requests: true`) in `olan-app.json` |
| `cli.usage`, `revocations.dev_required`, `revocations.input_required`, `revocations.input_missing`, `revocations.input_invalid`, `revocations.entry_invalid`, `revocations.signature_failed` | `olan-app revocations sign --dev --in list.json`; entries need `appId` (and `versions`/`packageSha256`, `reason`) |
| `mcp.no_session`, `mcp.invalid_input` | Call `olan_app_render` first; pass `label`/`value` |
| `events.unknown_type` | Use an event type from server.md#events |
| `events.delivery_failed` | The app server did not answer 2xx; 401 usually means the dev issuer `http://127.0.0.1:5180` is not in its `issuers` |
| `events.not_subscribed`, `events.permission_missing` (warnings) | Olan would not send this event: add it to `events` / add its permission |
| `tools.unknown_tool`, `tools.input_invalid` | Use a tool from `ai.tools`; make `--input` match its `input` schema |
| `tools.response_invalid` | Answer HTTP 200 with `{ ok: true, result }` or `{ ok: false, error: { code, message } }`, ≤ 64 KiB, `summary` ≤ 500 |
| `remote.missing`, `remote.invalid_url`, `remote.unreachable`, `remote.issuer_port` | Add `remote` or pass `--to`; start the app server; free port 5180 or pass `--issuer-port` |
| `remote.request_invalid` | `requests send`: the method, path, query, headers or body break the `olan.remote.request` rules (remote-requests.md#calling-it); put the query in `?…` or `--query`, not in the path segments |
| `requests.delivery_failed` | `requests send` got no usable answer (the app sees `remote_unavailable` with that `reason`): 401 = the app server does not list the dev issuer `http://127.0.0.1:5180`; `invalid_response` = not HTTP 200 with `{ status, headers?, body? }`; `network` = not running |
| `requests.not_enabled` (warning) | `remote` has no `"requests": true`, so Olan refuses `olan.remote.request` |

## Olan Marketplace

`login`, `developer`, `app`, `publish --marketplace`, `status --marketplace` and `release` report `marketplace.<code>`
in human output; with `--json` they print `{ error: "<code>", message, hint?, issues? }` (marketplace.md).

| Code | Fix |
|---|---|
| `marketplace.target_required`, `marketplace.app_required`, `marketplace.action_required`, `marketplace.invalid_option`, `marketplace.invalid_url` | Fix the arguments: `--marketplace [url]`, the app id, `developer create\|list`, `--channel stable\|beta`, `--percent 1-100` (needs `--channel`), `--visibility public\|org\|organization:<serverId>/<organizationId>`, `--slug`/`--name`/`--kind` |
| `marketplace.server_required` | `login` needs the Olan API address: `--server <url>`, `OLAN_SERVER` or `OLAN_API_URL` |
| `marketplace.token_required` | `--token` was empty: drop it to sign in in the browser, or pass an Olan access token (`olan app login --marketplace` passes one; CI uses `OLAN_MARKETPLACE_SESSION` instead) |
| `marketplace.server_unreachable`, `marketplace.network` | Check `--server` / `--marketplace` (or `OLAN_MARKETPLACE_URL`) and the connection |
| `marketplace.sign_in_unsupported` | The server has no OpenID configuration with PKCE: check `--server`, or use `OLAN_TOKEN` / `olan app login --marketplace` |
| `marketplace.sign_in_timeout`, `marketplace.sign_in_denied` | Run `login` again and finish signing in within 5 minutes, in a browser on the same computer |
| `marketplace.sign_in_failed` | The server refused the code exchange; `invalid_client`: the server predates the `olan-app-cli` client (update it, or use `OLAN_TOKEN`) |
| `marketplace.identity_token_failed` | 401: the access token expired (sign in again); 403: ask an admin for the `developer` grant; 404: the server predates marketplace sign-in |
| `marketplace.identity_invalid`, `marketplace.identity_untrusted_issuer` | The marketplace did not accept your server's identity: sign in again; an unregistered server must be verified with the marketplace by its administrator |
| `marketplace.session_missing`, `marketplace.session_expired`, `marketplace.developer_sign_in_required`, `marketplace.session_invalid`, `marketplace.session_other_marketplace` | Run `olan-app login --marketplace [url]` (CI: a valid `OLAN_MARKETPLACE_SESSION`) |
| `marketplace.session_env_override` (warning) | `OLAN_MARKETPLACE_SESSION` replaces the session `login` just saved; unset it |
| `marketplace.developer_account_missing` | `olan-app developer create --marketplace --slug <slug> --name <name> --accept-agreement` (or accept an invite) |
| `marketplace.developer_required` | You belong to several developer accounts: pass `--developer <slug>` |
| `marketplace.developer_not_found`, `marketplace.developer_role_required` | Check `--developer` (`olan-app developer list`); ask an owner or admin for the role |
| `marketplace.developer_exists` | The developer name is taken (`olan…` is reserved): choose another `--slug` |
| `marketplace.agreement_required`, `marketplace.agreement_unknown` | Pass `--accept-agreement` to `developer create`; existing accounts accept a new version in Studio → Yayınla |
| `marketplace.file_missing`, `marketplace.package_unreadable` | `--file` must be a package made by `olan-app pack` |
| `marketplace.package_invalid` (with issues), `marketplace.package_too_large` | Fix the listed package issues (`validate --strict`); stay ≤ 5 MiB |
| `marketplace.version_exists`, `marketplace.version_not_increasing` | Raise `version` in `olan-app.json` |
| `marketplace.app_not_found`, `marketplace.version_not_found` | No such app in your developer accounts, or no such version: check the id and version (`status` shows the newest) |
| `marketplace.app_owned_by_other_developer`, `marketplace.app_id_reserved` | Change `id` (`com.olan.*`, `app.olan.*`, `olan.*` are Olan's), or pass the owning `--developer` |
| `marketplace.age_rating_required`, `marketplace.age_rating_not_allowed` | Release needs an age rating: `olan-app app set --marketplace <appId> --age-rating 4+` (4+, 9+ or 13+; or Studio → Yayınla → the app → Mağaza sayfası); Olan does not accept 16+ or 18+ (guideline 5.4) |
| `marketplace.age_rating_not_set` | `publish --age-rating` submitted the version but could not save the rating: run the `olan-app app set` command in the hint |
| `marketplace.visibility_org_unknown`, `marketplace.visibility_ignored` (warning) | Pass `--visibility organization:<serverId>/<organizationId>`; visibility applies only when an app is created |
| `marketplace.server_not_found`, `marketplace.server_not_verified`, `marketplace.organization_not_allowed` | Organization-only apps need a server registered and verified with the marketplace, and an admin or developer sign-in through it |
| `marketplace.checks_failed`, `marketplace.rejected`, `marketplace.withdrawn` | Fix the findings listed after it (marketplace.md#automatic-checks) or the review notes, then publish again; the cited guideline is explained in review-guidelines.md |
| `marketplace.review_state_conflict`, `marketplace.rollout_invalid` | Only approved versions are released; a rollout only widens (10 → 50 → 100) and only once released; `halt` stops it |
| `marketplace.app_not_active`, `marketplace.package_revoked` | The app is suspended or the version revoked by Olan: publish a fixed version |
| `marketplace.submission_not_found`, `marketplace.submission_state_conflict` | `withdraw` and test reports need a submission that is still `checking` or `in_review` |
| `marketplace.test_report_invalid`, `marketplace.test_report_signature_invalid`, `marketplace.test_report_mismatch` | Generate the report again after packing, from the sources you publish (`olan-app test --report <file>`), and do not edit it |
| `marketplace.test_report_not_attached` | The package was submitted, the report was not: fix it and attach it in Studio → Yayınla |
| `marketplace.invalid_request` | The marketplace refused a parameter; check the command's options |
| `marketplace.rate_limited`, `marketplace.http_<status>` | Wait and retry; another status means the marketplace answered without an error body |

## Cards

`olan.chat.postCard` / `updateCard` fail with `validation_failed` listing these (cards.md):

| Code | Fix |
|---|---|
| `card.invalid` | `{ version: 1, root, nodes, fallbackText }` and nothing else |
| `card.fallback_text` | `fallbackText` 1–500 characters |
| `card.too_large`, `card.too_many_nodes`, `card.too_deep` | ≤ 16 KiB, ≤ 100 nodes, depth ≤ 8 |
| `card.component_not_allowed` | Only `Card`, `Stack`, `Text`, `Badge`, `Table`, `Button`, `EmptyState` |
| `card.handler_not_allowed` | No handlers in cards; buttons use `action` |
| `card.action_invalid`, `card.payload_too_large` | `{ kind: 'open', payload? }` or `{ kind: 'submit', name, payload? }`, `payload` ≤ 2 KiB; record cards (`olan.project.links.upsert`, `approvals.request`) only `open` |
| `card.submit_requires_remote` | `submit` buttons need `remote`; use `open` |
| `tree.*` | As in validate (props, children, text placement) |

## Install errors from the server

Uploading accepts any well-formed package; installing it is another matter (cli.md#signing-and-publishing).

| Error | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `package_unsigned` (403) | The version has no `signature.json`; the server installs, updates to or serves only signed versions | Locally: `olan-app pack --dev-sign` with your key on the server's `OLAN_APPS_TRUSTED_KEYS`; production: Olan Marketplace signs the app |
| `package_untrusted_key` (403, `keyFingerprint`) | Signed, but by a key not on the server's trusted list (or a key that was removed); from `developer/try` also when the key is not one you registered (`reason: developer_key_revoked \| developer_not_member` for one that stopped) | Sign with a trusted key; for `olan-app try`, register your development key (`olan-app keys register`); development servers may add it to `OLAN_APPS_TRUSTED_KEYS` |
| `developer_key_revoked` / `developer_not_member` (403) | A development installation signed with your registered key: the key was revoked, or you are no longer a member of the organization. The installation is kept | Register a new key (`keygen --dev --force`, `keys register`) and `olan-app try` again |
| `key_exists` (409) | `keys register`: the key is already registered (a revoked key cannot come back) | Use it, or create a new key |
| `package_invalid` with `package.signature_invalid` (400, on upload) | The signature does not verify against the package digest | Pack again; do not edit a package after signing |

<!-- docs/examples.md -->
# Examples

Complete apps live in the Olan repository under `examples/` (each passes `validate --strict` and
`test`, with fixtures and tests to copy):

| Example | Shows |
|---|---|
| `examples/project-pulse` | `app` surface, three screens on the navigation stack, status `Badge`s, `Menu` → `olan.projects.updateTask` with `revision`, `OlanError` handling, toasts (`projects:read`, `projects:write`) |
| `examples/overdue-widget` | `project.widget` surface with `params.projectId`, manifest `settings` + `useSettings`, date logic tested with a frozen clock (`projects:read`) |
| `examples/exchange-rates` | `olan.http.fetch` with `http:<host>`, `Table`, `Chart`, a `settings` surface with a `Select` saving to `olan.storage`, HTTP fixtures, retry (`http:rates.example.com`, `storage`) |
| `examples/decision-log` | `olan.db` with an `organization` and a `user` collection, `useCollection` with a status filter and `loadMore`, `useRecord`, "Göreve dönüştür" → `olan.projects.createTask`, `deleteTask`, `deleteList` with `forbidden_record` → toast, `fixtures/db.json` (`projects:read`, `db`, `tasks:write`, `tasks:delete`, `projects:delete`) |
